readings.summary: Package root: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kairalimacmini-Claude/d81b3f6b-c18e-4430-a22c-d47fbdad6a32/scratchpad/os2026/Digital_Growth_Agency_OS_2026/. This section supplies one doctrine file (02_COMPETITIVE_INTELLIGENCE/COMPETITIVE_INTELLIGENCE_AND_MARKET_SHARE_PLAYBOOK_2026.md) and five empty CSV registers (07_TEMPLATES/). Core content: a 10-step competitive-intelligence lifecycle; a 12-module deep-dive matrix (each module = metrics / tools / exact-capture rules / target logic / explicit 'Do not' prohibitions); a 9-type competitor roster taxonomy; a 7-way strategy classification (defend | match | flank | attack | create | partner | ignore — 'partner' is in the lifecycle and CSV enum but has no playbook section); a 13-field opportunity scorecard; a 4-tier monitoring cadence; and an ethical/legal red-lines list with mandatory legal review for comparative claims. Evidence discipline (separate facts/estimates/calculations/assumptions, confidence class, peer-median → upper-quartile → leader benchmark ladder) aligns tightly with v1 HARD GATE 'never invent facts', EVIDENCE LAW, and R2/R4/R6. The playbook is pure doctrine — no launch/approval authority is defined, so its 'test or launch' step must be subordinated to v1 FRONT GATES and owner approval, and its red lines should land as ADDED rows in gates/registry.yaml (never replacing existing gates). No prompt-injection content found in any of the six files. Biggest genuinely new capabilities: AI-answer visibility prompt panel, quantified market-share opportunity backlog, competitor page-teardown register, and the deliberate-ignore-with-reconsideration-trigger decision class. Scope expansions needing owner ruling: paid media and retention/lifecycle modules assume channels (ad accounts, CRM/CDP, email/SMS) outside the current web-factory mandate.

structures.name: Definition of market-share capture (purpose doctrine)
structures.detail: 'Eat into market share' = winning a defined group of qualified customers, demand, transactions or attention PROFITABLY. Explicitly NOT: copying competitors, attacking their infrastructure, creating false reviews, manipulating links, or making unsupported comparative claims.

structures.name: Competitive intelligence lifecycle — exact 10 steps, numbered
structures.detail: 1 Define the exact market and denominator. 2 Build a multi-channel competitor universe. 3 Capture evidence using the same period, market, language and device. 4 Separate facts, estimates, calculations and assumptions. 5 Diagnose parity gaps, competitor weaknesses and defendable advantages. 6 Quantify the opportunity and cost. 7 Select defend, match, flank, attack, create, partner or ignore. 8 Build the page/product/channel changes and acceptance criteria. 9 Test or launch with commercial guardrails. 10 Monitor competitor reactions, market share and profitability. NOTE: no owner-approval or stop-launch step exists anywhere in this chain — approval authority is entirely undefined in the package file.

structures.name: Deep-dive module matrix — 12 modules, fixed 5-facet schema
structures.detail: Columns per module: Metrics | Tools | Exact capture | Target logic | Do not. The 12 modules in order: (1) Market definition and denominator; (2) Competitor universe; (3) Demand and share of search; (4) Organic and SERP ownership; (5) AI-answer visibility; (6) Content and topical advantage; (7) Backlinks, PR and reputation; (8) Offer, product and pricing; (9) Paid media and creative; (10) UX, CRO and performance; (11) Local, regional and localization; (12) Retention and lifecycle.

structures.name: Per-module 'Do not' prohibited-shortcut list (verbatim highlights)
structures.detail: M1: confusing traffic share with revenue share; mixing branded/generic demand; comparing global data to local market. M2: only analysing companies named by management; same competitor set in every channel. M3: search volume without revenue/intent; treating Google Trends index as absolute volume. M4: broad vanity keywords; copying competitor word count; average position alone. M5: claiming deterministic rankings in LLMs; fake mentions; one prompt run as stable benchmark; relying on llms.txt for Google. M6: commodity AI volume; pages for slight keyword variants; copying structure or protected content. M7: buying bulk links; chasing DA/DR; automated disavow from toxicity score; fake reviews or negative SEO. M8: price collusion; deceptive comparisons; permanent discounting; copying competitor claims. M9: trademark misuse; misleading comparisons; bidding without profit model; copying creatives. M10: redesigning because a competitor looks newer; declaring causality from a heatmap; copying dark patterns. M11: machine translation without review; doorway location pages; forced geo redirects; inconsistent NAP. M12: optimizing front-end CVR while refunds/churn/support costs worsen.

structures.name: Benchmark ladder / benchmark classes
structures.source: §3 M4 & M10 target logic + COMPETITOR_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.csv columns
structures.detail: Comparison classes: our_value → peer_median → peer_upper_quartile → leader_value, plus gap. Target logic: 'Beat the peer median first; aim for upper quartile in priority clusters; require profitability/lead-quality guardrails' (M4); 'Use own baseline and peer quartiles' (M10).

structures.name: Evidence classification discipline
structures.detail: Every captured data point is classed as fact | estimate | calculation | assumption (lifecycle step 4: 'Separate facts, estimates, calculations and assumptions') and carries a confidence field; capture must hold period/market/language/device constant (step 3); M1 requires 'Show confidence range' and actual market share captured separately from digital proxies.

structures.name: Competitor roster taxonomy — 9 competitor types
structures.detail: Per target market, SEPARATE lists for: (1) commercial competitors selling the same outcome; (2) substitutes solving the problem differently; (3) organic search competitors ranking for priority queries; (4) paid competitors bidding/advertising into the audience; (5) marketplaces, retailers, aggregators and distributors; (6) publishers, forums, YouTube channels and creators controlling attention; (7) businesses recommended by AI systems; (8) local/map competitors by physical location or service area; (9) aspirational experience/brand references (not direct commercial rivals). Rule: roster records competitor TYPE and MARKET — never one undifferentiated list; a domain can be strong SEO / weak commercial competitor or vice versa. M2 target: at least 3-5 direct + recurring top domains per priority demand cluster; update quarterly.

structures.name: Market-share attack strategy — decision classification
structures.detail: Six documented strategies: 5.1 Defend (protect branded demand, best-converting pages, high-margin products, link-earning assets, locations, reviews, cohorts; fix migration and tracking risk BEFORE attacking); 5.2 Match mandatory parity (mobile usability, credible proof, clear price/terms, delivery, returns, availability, page speed, search/filter, accessibility, support — 'parity is not differentiation'); 5.3 Flank (underserved profitable segment by location/language/audience/use case/price tier/format/urgency/channel/information need/service model); 5.4 Attack a vulnerable demand pool (coordinated offer+page+content+link/PR+paid+local+merchant+lifecycle plan around a QUANTIFIED cluster with expected incremental contribution, capacity and guardrails); 5.5 Create a category or moat (proprietary research, clinical/technical expertise, first-party data, unique products, tools, service processes, communities, partnerships, credible proof); 5.6 Ignore deliberately (record reason: low-margin / legally risky / operationally impossible / outside brand strategy / weak estimates — MUST include a reconsideration trigger). Seventh option 'partner' appears in lifecycle step 7 and the backlog CSV enum (strategy_defend_match_flank_attack_create_partner_ignore) but has NO §5 section — internal package inconsistency.

structures.name: Opportunity scorecard — 13 mandatory capture fields
structures.detail: market/region/language/location; customer segment and job-to-be-done; demand size and source; current own share and competitor shares; attainable share range; conversion and contribution assumptions; capacity constraint; time to value; confidence class; legal/brand/platform risk; required pages/products/content/links/ads/localization/operations; expected incremental contribution under downside/base/upside cases; owner and next evidence required.

structures.name: Competitor monitoring cadence — 4 tiers
structures.detail: Daily/weekly: paid creative, pricing/availability, major rankings, local reviews, outages, launches, high-priority changes. Monthly: SOV, traffic/channel estimates, backlinks, content, offer, SERP/AI visibility, landing-page changes. Quarterly: complete market map, peer percentiles, strategic position, customer research, attack backlog. Event-driven: funding, acquisition, regulation, new market entry, product recall, domain migration, brand crisis, major algorithm/platform change.

structures.name: Ethical and legal red lines — prohibited-action list + mandatory legal review
structures.detail: Prohibited: unauthorized access; personal-data collection; evasion of technical restrictions; negative SEO; fake reviews; impersonation; trademark misuse; content theft; price coordination; fabricated comparisons; undisclosed sponsored advocacy. Evidence must be public, licensed, client-owned or properly consented. Legal review is MANDATORY for: comparative claims, regulated categories, sensitive data. This is ready-made gate text — the only hard stop-condition language in the section.

structures.name: AI-answer visibility capture protocol
structures.detail: Run VERSIONED prompt sets by persona, market, language, journey stage. Store exact prompt / model / date / output and cited sources per run (CSV: exact_prompt, model, model_version, run_date, run_number, raw_output_artifact, reviewer). Benchmark only against the SAME prompt set and model; one prompt run is never a stable benchmark. Metrics: generative impressions/pages/countries/devices, prompt mention share, citation share, source diversity, factual accuracy. Target: increase accurate qualified mentions and cited pages.

structures.name: Declared tool stack per module (feeds R7 tool/skill map)
structures.detail: Semrush (Position Tracking, Keyword Gap, Advertising, AI); DataForSEO (SERP, Labs, Merchant, Business); Similarweb (incl. AI); Google Trends; Keyword Planner; GSC (incl. Generative AI reports where available); Screaming Frog; Ahrefs; Google/Meta ad libraries; marketplaces; maps; AI engines; media databases; review platforms; Google Business Profile; local rank grid; hreflang crawl; translation QA; Baymard criteria; Clarity/Hotjar; usability tests; GA4/Shopify; PSI/CrUX/GTmetrix; CRM/CDP; Shopify cohorts; email/SMS platform; finance data; Google Ads; controlled prompt panels.

readings.summary: The 07_TEMPLATES/V1_* set is the per-project, per-release instantiation kit of the package: one charter (project identity + a 7-phase gate table, phases 0 Classification through 6 Stabilisation exit, gated on open P0/P1 counts with named Approver/Decision/Date, plus an accepted-risks ledger) and nine header-only CSV registers covering URL inventory/migration, redirects, sitemap changes, page briefs, launch tests, KPI guardrails, issues, experiments, and report runs. Everything is inert schema — no data, no prose, no values enumerated, no AI-directed instructions (injection_flags is genuinely empty). The set maps cleanly onto v1's MINE FIRST / PROTECTION MAP / evidence-law machinery and onto R3/R6, but it is register-shaped, not enforcement-shaped: it has no site-class dimension, no beauty/go-science/design-review/golden-page gates, no human-only approver constraint, and a stop/rollback threshold whose execution semantics must be bound to the human-only production rule. Merge posture: adopt the register schemas as evidence artifacts inside launches/<domain>/, keep gates/registry.yaml and approvals.yaml as the enforcement layer, and nest the v1 front gates inside package phases 2–3 (R8).

structures.name: Charter project-identity block (13 fields)
structures.detail: Project ID; Client/brand; Business model; Workflow file; New/existing; Production domain/property; Staging domain; Regions/languages/currencies/locations; Primary commercial outcome; Accountable owner; Release owner; Target launch; Risk level. Notable: 'Workflow file' binds each project to one of the package's 02_WORKFLOWS files; 'Accountable owner' vs 'Release owner' is a two-role split; 'Risk level' is set at classification.

structures.name: Phase-gate chain — EXACT names and order
structures.detail: 0 Classification -> 1 Baseline -> 2 Strategy -> 3 Build complete -> 4 Launch readiness -> 5 Launch acceptance -> 6 Stabilisation exit. Approval table columns per phase: Phase | Evidence location | Open P0 | Open P1 | Approver | Decision | Date. Gate mechanic implied by columns: a phase decision is recorded against counts of open P0 and open P1 issues plus an evidence location; no pass/fail values or thresholds are enumerated in the template itself.

structures.name: Accepted-risks record (6 fields)
structures.detail: issue ID, consequence, reason, accountable approver, expiry/review date, mitigation. This is the package's formal gate-waiver mechanism — risks expire and are reviewed, and each has a named accountable approver.

structures.name: P0/P1 severity classes
structures.detail: Charter counts 'Open P0' and 'Open P1' per phase; issue register has free 'severity' and computed 'priority_score' columns. Only P0 and P1 are named anywhere; full severity scale is undefined in these files.

structures.name: Migration verification flag chain (per URL)
structures.detail: current_action -> new_url -> migration_action -> redirect_target -> content_migrated -> metadata_migrated -> schema_migrated -> redirect_tested -> post_launch_status. Plus dual-canonical check (current_canonical vs google_canonical), indexability, in_xml_sitemap, crawl_depth, internal_inlinks — a per-URL protection lifecycle with three separate migration checkboxes and a post-launch closure status.

structures.name: Redirect QA chain
structures.detail: prelaunch_test -> chain_loop_test -> postlaunch_status, plus two propagation flags: internal_links_updated and ads_email_offline_updated. source_variants and source_value (value-weighted redirects) and intent_match (destination must match intent) are explicit columns; redirect_type and implementation_layer are free fields (no enumerated values).

structures.name: Sitemap change current-vs-proposed pairing
structures.detail: Every row pairs current_url/current_parent/current_depth/current_template/current_sitemap/current_indexable/current_performance_value against proposed_url/proposed_parent/proposed_depth/proposed_template/proposed_xml_sitemap, then action, reason, owner, approval, qa_status. current_performance_value is the baseline-informed field — the register structurally requires knowing the old page's value before proposing the change (R6-aligned).

structures.name: Page brief field set (27 columns)
structures.detail: Includes journey_stage, primary/secondary conversion, value_proposition, protected_elements (elements that must survive rebuild), required_sections, proof_trust, objections, internal_links_in/out, schema, media, accessibility, performance_budget, analytics_events, split content_owner vs design_owner, approval_status. No golden-page or design-source concept present.

structures.name: Launch-test triple status chain
structures.detail: Per test: prelaunch_status -> launch_status -> postlaunch_status, with evidence, incident_id, retest, approval columns. Keyed by test_id + project_id + release_version + phase + market_domain — the only place 'release_version' appears, implying V1_* files are instantiated per release. Flat list: NO site-class (commerce/organic/landing) column and no required|adapted|n_a classification.

structures.name: KPI guardrail threshold ladder
structures.detail: Per metric: definition, source_of_truth, segment, baseline_period/baseline_value, comparison_period, target, warning_threshold, stop_rollback_threshold, owner, report_cadence. Two-level guardrail: warning then stop/rollback — the package's stop-launch/rollback trigger mechanism. Old-vs-new comparison is native (baseline_period vs comparison_period), matching R6.

structures.name: Issue lifecycle fields
structures.detail: issue_id, project_id, workflow, phase, workstream, severity, observation, evidence_location, affected_urls_count, affected_urls_export, business_consequence, recommendation, acceptance_criteria, owner, dependency, effort, priority_score, status, retest_evidence, accepted_risk_by, due_date. Closure requires retest_evidence; waiver requires named accepted_risk_by; issues are anchored to workflow+phase+workstream. status values not enumerated.

structures.name: Experiment lifecycle
structures.detail: hypothesis -> control -> variant -> primary_metric + guardrails -> baseline -> minimum_detectable_effect + sample_size_method -> start/end dates + traffic_allocation -> qa_status -> result -> decision -> learning -> follow_up. Statistically disciplined A/B framework; no v1 counterpart exists.

structures.name: Report run record
structures.detail: report_id, project_id, tool, report_export, domain_property, region_language_location, device, date_range, comparison_range, configuration, run_timestamp, operator, raw_file_location, known_gaps, issues_created, next_run_date. Reproducibility-oriented (configuration + operator + raw file) with a feedback hook (issues_created) and cadence (next_run_date). Missing R3's monitor/reject+reason/implement triage and versioned-chain linkage.

steps: Fill charter project-identity block (13 fields incl. business model, workflow file binding, risk level, accountable owner vs release owner)
Record phase-0 approval row (evidence location, open P0/P1 counts, approver, decision, date)
Populate V1_MASTER_URL_INVENTORY (full old-site URL inventory with performance/value/canonical/link data)
Populate V1_KPI_BASELINE_GUARDRAILS baseline_period/baseline_value per metric
Log every tool run in V1_REPORT_RUN_REGISTER
Phase approval row
Populate V1_SITEMAP_CHANGE_REGISTER (current-vs-proposed with action/reason/owner/approval/qa_status)
Populate V1_REDIRECT_MAP
Populate V1_PAGE_BRIEF rows to approval_status
Phase approval row
Execute briefs; log defects in V1_ISSUE_REGISTER (severity, evidence, acceptance criteria)
Phase approval row gated on open P0/P1 counts
Run V1_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST prelaunch_status column per test with evidence
Verify redirect prelaunch_test + chain_loop_test
Phase approval row
Run launch_status and postlaunch_status columns; link incidents (incident_id) and retests
Verify inventory post_launch_status and redirect postlaunch_status; confirm internal_links_updated and ads_email_offline_updated
Phase approval row
Monitor KPI comparison_period against warning_threshold / stop_rollback_threshold
Close or accept remaining issues (accepted_risk_by + expiry per charter accepted-risks section)
Run V1_EXPERIMENT_REGISTER cycles as applicable
Final phase approval row

overlaps.package_item: Charter 7-phase gate chain (0 Classification..6 Stabilisation exit)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 FRONT GATES (brief -> strategy -> design_source -> golden_page -> full build) in launches/<domain>/approvals.yaml + human DNS flip at launch
overlaps.note: Adopt the 0-6 macro skeleton as the outer frame; nest the five v1 front gates inside phases 2-3 (design_source and golden_page have NO package counterpart and must be inserted, per R8). Phase 1 Baseline before 2 Strategy natively satisfies R6 ordering.

overlaps.package_item: Charter 'Approver'/'Decision' columns and per-register 'approval'/'approval_status' fields
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 doctrine: owner signs approvals.yaml rows; agent NEVER self-approves or self-merges (HARD GATE)
overlaps.note: Adopt the columns but bind them: approver values must be named humans (owner or delegate); CI keeps failing PRs with unsigned rows. The templates themselves impose no such constraint.

overlaps.package_item: Charter accepted-risks section + issue register accepted_risk_by/expiry
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 rule: gates are added never weakened; gate removal/waiver needs owner ruling logged in DECISIONS.md
overlaps.note: Adopt the richer structure (consequence, expiry/review date, mitigation) but require every accepted risk to be an owner ruling cross-logged in DECISIONS.md; otherwise it becomes a gate-weakening side door.

overlaps.package_item: Open P0 / Open P1 phase-blocking counts in charter
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 merge-blocking CI lints (registry lint, unsigned-approval fail)
overlaps.note: New severity-count gate at phase level; complements (does not replace) v1 per-PR CI blocking. Needs the full severity scale defined (only P0/P1 named).

overlaps.package_item: V1_MASTER_URL_INVENTORY.csv
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 BUILD DECISION MATRIX 'MINE FIRST' full live-site inventory + immutable raw in content-mined/
overlaps.note: Adopt the 37-column schema as the structured layer over the immutable content-mined/ raw; performance/revenue/margin cells come only from real tool exports (never invented; gaps ASKED per HARD GATE).

overlaps.package_item: V1_REDIRECT_MAP.csv + inventory migration_action/redirect_target columns
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 PROTECTION MAP (every legacy URL: KEEP/MERGE/301)
overlaps.note: Package version is a superset (variants, value weighting, intent_match, chain/loop tests, offline propagation). Map v1's KEEP/MERGE/301 vocabulary into migration_action/redirect_type enumerations so the classification survives verbatim.

overlaps.package_item: V1_SITEMAP_CHANGE_REGISTER.csv
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 strategy front gate (fat approval: sitemap + keywords + competitor map + integrations in ONE owner approval)
overlaps.note: Register becomes the evidence artifact behind the strategy approval; its per-row 'approval' column supplements, not replaces, the single fat approvals.yaml signature. current_performance_value column enforces R6 baseline-informed sitemap decisions.

overlaps.package_item: V1_PAGE_BRIEF.csv
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 brief front gate + golden_page gate (one page approved first, all others match)
overlaps.note: Adopt as the per-page brief schema (protected_elements, performance_budget, analytics_events are valuable additions) but the golden-page mechanic is absent — add a golden/derived flag or keep golden_page as a separate approvals.yaml gate above the briefs.

overlaps.package_item: V1_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.csv
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 GATE REGISTRY gates/registry.yaml (63 gates, three site classes, required|adapted|n_a, checklists GENERATED, lint merge-blocks)
overlaps.note: Keep registry.yaml as the single source of truth and generator (R8); adopt the CSV's row shape — release_version + prelaunch/launch/postlaunch triple + incident_id + retest + evidence — as the generated-checklist output format. Never let the flat CSV become an independently-edited parallel gate list.

overlaps.package_item: V1_KPI_BASELINE_GUARDRAILS.csv
overlaps.existing_mechanism: R6 old-vs-new benchmark inputs for the owner's separate monitoring tool; v1 has no formal KPI guardrail table
overlaps.note: Directly implements R6 (baseline_period vs comparison_period, per-metric source_of_truth and cadence); becomes the before/after input feed. Definitions column also serves R2 provenance for metric choices.

overlaps.package_item: stop_rollback_threshold semantics (KPI guardrails)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATES: no production writes, no DNS/robots changes by agent, production DNS flips always human
overlaps.note: Threshold breach may TRIGGER a stop/rollback recommendation, but execution (DNS revert, production change) must remain human-only; adopting any automated rollback would violate HARD GATES. Needs explicit wording in the merged doc.

overlaps.package_item: V1_ISSUE_REGISTER.csv
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 unattended rule (blocked -> QUESTIONS.md) + evidence law + fix-one≠done (grep all instances)
overlaps.note: Adopt as the formal defect register (affected_urls_count/export operationalizes fix-one≠done; retest_evidence operationalizes proof-of-work). QUESTIONS.md stays for owner-input gaps — different purpose (asks vs defects).

overlaps.existing_mechanism: none in v1 (no experimentation framework)
overlaps.note: Net-new capability. Experiments on live pages must ship via normal PR flow (no production writes) and their guardrails column should reference the KPI guardrail table.

overlaps.package_item: V1_REPORT_RUN_REGISTER.csv

overlaps.note: Adopt schema but extend for R3: add what-to-monitor / what-to-reject+reason / what-to-implement triage fields and version-chain linkage (prior_report_id); raw_file_location must resolve inside the repo per 'if it isn't in the repo, it didn't happen'.

overlaps.package_item: Charter 'Evidence location' column
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 EVIDENCE LAW: everything under launches/<domain>/, committed to git
overlaps.note: Fix evidence locations to the launches/<domain>/ convention rather than leaving a free-text path per phase.

overlaps.package_item: Charter identity fields Workflow file / Risk level / Accountable owner vs Release owner / release_version (launch checklist)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: no v1 counterpart (v1 has sites/<domain> + STATUS.yaml but no per-project charter or release versioning)
overlaps.note: New formalization; STATUS.yaml fleet pulse should reference charter Project ID and current phase to avoid dual bookkeeping.

overlaps.package_item: Inventory metric columns (organic_clicks..revenue, margin) and source_of_truth fields
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE: never invent facts/IDs/prices — gaps are ASKED, not filled
overlaps.note: Template invites numeric fill-in; merged doctrine must state cells are populated only from named tool exports logged in V1_REPORT_RUN_REGISTER, blanks escalate to owner.

new_capabilities: Per-release phase-gate charter with P0/P1-count gating and a 7th post-launch phase (6 Stabilisation exit) — v1 gates stop at launch
Accepted-risk ledger with expiry/review dates and mitigation (time-boxed waivers rather than permanent rulings)
Two-tier KPI guardrails: warning_threshold + stop_rollback_threshold per metric with named source_of_truth and cadence (implements R6 monitoring inputs)
Statistical experiment register (hypothesis, MDE, sample_size_method, traffic_allocation, decision/learning chain) — no v1 equivalent
Per-URL migration verification triple (content_migrated / metadata_migrated / schema_migrated) plus redirect chain/loop testing and ads_email_offline propagation flags
Dual-canonical audit column pair (current_canonical vs google_canonical) and crawl_depth/internal_inlinks in the URL inventory
Page-brief fields absent from v1: protected_elements, performance_budget, analytics_events, journey_stage, split content_owner/design_owner
Reproducible report-run manifest (configuration + operator + raw_file_location + known_gaps + issues_created + next_run_date) — skeleton for R3
release_version keying of launch tests (versioned re-launch of the same site)
Formal issue register with affected_urls_count/export (operationalizes v1's fix-one≠done rule as data)
conflicts: Gate-list dilution risk (R8): the charter's phase table and the flat V1_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST contain NO beauty gate, go-science gate, design external AI review, design_source or golden_page gates, and no commerce/organic/landing class or required|adapted|n_a dimension. Adopting them as the authoritative gate surface would silently drop the 63-gate registry's structure — they must remain generated outputs of gates/registry.yaml, with the v1 gates inserted into the phase skeleton.

Approver fields are unconstrained: charter Approver, checklist approval, sitemap-register approval, page-brief approval_status nowhere state human-only approval; without binding to approvals.yaml signers this weakens the HARD GATE 'agent never self-approves/self-merges'.

stop_rollback_threshold implies rollback execution; any automated rollback (DNS revert, production write, robots change) violates HARD GATES — breach must only page a human; execution stays human-only.

Accepted-risks mechanism can waive failing gates by design; v1 doctrine says gates are added never weakened and removal needs an owner ruling in DECISIONS.md — accepted risks must be owner-signed and cross-logged there or this becomes a standing bypass.

Inventory revenue/margin/conversion columns invite estimation; HARD GATE forbids invented facts/figures — merged doctrine must mandate tool-export provenance (via V1_REPORT_RUN_REGISTER row) for every numeric cell and ASK on gaps.

V1_REPORT_RUN_REGISTER as shipped does not satisfy R3 (no monitor/reject/implement triage, no reject-reason, no versioned chain linkage) — adopting it unmodified would under-deliver an owner requirement while appearing to cover it.
open_questions: What does the V1_ filename prefix denote — release version 1 of a project instance (supported by release_version column in V1_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST) or version 1 of the template set? Determines whether the merge creates per-release copies (V2_, V3_) or one living register per site.

No value enumerations exist anywhere in these templates: allowed values for migration_action, redirect_type, implementation_layer, severity scale beyond P0/P1, priority_score formula, phase Decision values, qa_status, approval_status chain, and the three status columns (prelaunch/launch/postlaunch) are all undefined. Should v1 vocabularies (KEEP/MERGE/301, gate statuses) be canonized into them, or does another package file define them (check 01/02 sections readers)?

Who may occupy 'Approver', 'accountable approver' and 'accepted_risk_by' — owner only, or delegable (e.g., Dr. Deepu John for clinical rows)? And does phase approval subsume or duplicate the existing approvals.yaml front-gate signatures?

Is Phase 1 Baseline the designated home for the R6 DataForSEO PDF of the old site (evidence location = launches/<domain>/baseline/?), and is that PDF a P0-blocking prerequisite for opening Phase 2 Strategy?

Should V1_REPORT_RUN_REGISTER be extended in place with R3 triage fields (monitor/reject+reason/implement, prior_report_id chain) or should R3 live in a separate report-store register that references report_id?

Where do these registers physically live after merge — launches/<domain>/ per evidence law (recommended), a new 07_TEMPLATES-derived per-project folder, or both with generation? Owner should rule to avoid dual bookkeeping with STATUS.yaml.
Phase 6 'Stabilisation exit' duration and exit criteria are undefined (no thresholds, no time window) — owner must define when a project formally leaves stabilisation and who signs it.

readings.summary: The metrics/benchmarks layer of the v2 package is a quantitative measurement OS the v1 factory largely lacks: (1) a 63-row metric dictionary (coincidentally the same count as v1's 63-gate registry — they are NOT 1:1) with per-metric formula, mandatory dimensions, source-of-truth, target method, red flag, diagnosis, improvement action, and a per-metric prohibited-shortcut ('do_not') column; (2) a 6-class benchmark taxonomy (HARD / OWN baseline / PEER percentile / INDUSTRY study / ECONOMIC requirement / EXPERIMENT) plus a 13-row benchmark register whose rows carry classes HARD(8)/INDUSTRY(3)/PLATFORM(1)/ACADEMIC(1) with source-ID citations; (3) an 18-stage tool-stack register with an agent_automation column (directly serves R7); (4) a seven-question report discipline, gap-calculation formulas, and a 7-link diagnostic chain (observation→segment→evidence→mechanism→intervention→acceptance test→commercial guardrail) that concretizes R2/R3. Nothing here violates a HARD GATE on its face — the fabrication bans (BMK-012 'mark not available rather than fabricate', AI-004, do_not entries) actively reinforce HARD GATE f — but three merge risks exist: the agent_automation column and several improvement actions imply production-write paths (GTM API, sitemap fixes, redirects, rollback) that must be routed through v1's PR/owner-merge flow; BMK-005's 'formal approval' authority is unspecified (must map to owner + DECISIONS.md); and the package has no site-class (commerce/organic/landing) dimension or clinical sign-off overlay, both of which must be layered on per R8. No prompt-injection content found in these four files.

structures.name: Seven-question report discipline
structures.detail: Every report and issue must answer, in order: (1) metric and exact formula; (2) mandatory dimensions (region, domain, language, page/template, device, source, cohort, period — not optional when they materially change interpretation); (3) source of truth (third-party estimate cannot overrule finance, CRM, Search Console or server evidence); (4) applicable benchmark class; (5) absolute + percentage gap with confidence and comparability; (6) diagnosis to perform before recommending change; (7) exact improvement, acceptance test, and monitoring period.

structures.name: Benchmark class taxonomy (6 classes)
structures.detail: Hard standard | own baseline | peer percentile | industry study | economic requirement | experiment. Target-setting protocol (7 rules): hard threshold only where an authoritative standard defines one; client seasonal/cohort baseline is the DEFAULT comparator; peer percentiles built from the named competitor set with identical definitions; industry benchmarks context-only (record sample, year, sector, conversion definition); commercial targets derived from contribution economics, capacity, payback; experiments for uncertain causal changes with minimum detectable effect + guardrails defined BEFORE launch; record `not comparable` rather than forcing a misleading benchmark.

structures.name: 63 core metric controls (metric ID scheme)
structures.detail: Exactly 63 metrics across 11 workstream prefixes: COM-001..010 (Commercial/Market: Revenue, Contribution margin, Revenue/session, Qualified lead rate, Lead-to-win, CAC, LTV, Actual market share, Share of search, Digital traffic share); SEO-001..014 (GSC clicks/impressions/CTR, Weighted organic SOV, Top-3/Top-10 coverage, Indexable URL count, Priority indexation rate, Canonical agreement rate, Sitemap hygiene rate, Crawl waste ratio, Internal link coverage, Content decay rate, Referring domain gap, Broken backlink value); AI-001..004 (Google generative impressions, Prompt mention share, Citation share, AI factual accuracy rate); TEC-001..010 (Critical status error rate, Redirect chain rate, Rendering parity, LCP/INP/CLS/TTFB P75, Page weight+requests, Third-party script cost, Uptime/transaction success); UX-001..005 (Task success, Time on task, Critical error rate, Onsite search success, Accessibility conformance); CRO-001..008 (Primary CVR, Landing page CVR, CTA CTR, Form completion, Add-to-cart, Checkout completion, Cart abandonment, Return/refund rate); B2B-001..003 (MQL-to-SQL, Pipeline sourced/influenced, Lead response time); LOC-001..002 (Local pack visibility share, Review health); INT-001..003 (Hreflang validity, Wrong-market session rate, Translation QA defect rate); SEC-001..002 (Critical vulnerability count, Backup restore success); OPS-001..002 (Evidence completeness, Change failure rate). NOTE: 63 metrics = same count as v1's 63-gate registry — coincidence to verify, not an intended mapping.

structures.name: Metric definition fields (12 columns)
structures.detail: metric_id, workstream, metric, definition_formula, required_dimensions, source_of_truth, secondary_tools, target_method, red_flag, diagnosis, improvement_action, do_not. The dictionary MD §7 declares the CSV as the complete row-level authority ('The complete row-level definitions, required dimensions, red flags, diagnosis, recommended actions and prohibited shortcuts are in 07_TEMPLATES/METRIC_DICTIONARY.csv').

structures.name: Per-metric prohibited shortcuts (do_not column, all 63)
structures.detail: Notable entries: 'Use GA4 revenue as sole finance truth' (COM-001); 'Optimize ROAS or revenue without margin' (COM-002); 'Present traffic share as actual market share' (COM-008); 'Compare GSC clicks directly to GA4 sessions' (SEO-001); 'Use one global CTR benchmark' (SEO-003); 'Maximize indexed pages' (SEO-006); 'Demand instant indexing or use Indexing API improperly' (SEO-007); 'Change publication date without substantive update' (SEO-012); 'Bulk outreach, paid link schemes, chase DA' (SEO-013); 'Redirect everything to homepage' (SEO-014/TEC-001); 'Assume report is available for all properties' (AI-001); 'Treat stochastic runs as stable rankings' (AI-002); 'Manufacture inauthentic mentions or special Google AI files' (AI-003); 'Spam AI systems or fabricate sources' (AI-004); 'Install tools/apps without owner or expiry' (TEC-009); 'Monitor homepage only' (TEC-010); 'Claim conformance from automated score alone' (UX-005); 'Apply generic 2-3% benchmark to every funnel' (CRO-001); 'Redesign and overwrite control' (CRO-002); 'Create spam locations or fake addresses' (LOC-001); 'Buy, gate or fabricate reviews' (LOC-002); 'Publish raw machine translation for high-risk content' (INT-003); 'Treat backup job success as restore proof' (SEC-002); 'Accept screenshot alone for hidden configuration' (OPS-001); 'Hide failed releases from denominator' (OPS-002).

structures.name: Tool stack by stage (18 stages)
structures.detail: Exact stage order: Commercial truth (CRM+finance/backend) → Google organic (GSC) → Analytics and tags (GA4+GTM) → Technical crawling (Screaming Frog) → Automated SEO data (DataForSEO APIs, 'agent-agnostic data acquisition at scale') → SEO/competitor suite (Semrush; secondary Ahrefs+Similarweb) → Market/channel intelligence (Similarweb) → Performance field (CrUX/PSI+RUM) → Performance diagnosis (WebPageTest or GTmetrix) → Behaviour/UX (Microsoft Clarity) → Usability research (moderated/unmoderated testing) → Accessibility (axe-core + manual WCAG protocol) → Visual/functional QA (Playwright) → Security (OWASP ZAP + dependency scanner) → Commerce feeds (Google Merchant Center + Shopify) → Local (GBP + local rank tool) → Paid competitor creative (Google Ads Transparency Center + Meta Ad Library) → Evidence/versioning (GitHub + immutable object storage; secondary S3 Object Lock/Drive Vault). Every stage carries a 'limitations' guard, e.g. 'Estimated traffic/volume/authority are not business truth' (Semrush), 'Paid estimates; validate critical findings with first party/live checks' (DataForSEO).

structures.name: Benchmark register (13 rows, 4 register classes)
structures.detail: BMK-001 LCP P75 good<=2.5s/NI 2.5-4s/poor>4s [G12, HARD]; BMK-002 INP P75 good<=200ms/NI 200-500ms/poor>500ms [G12, HARD, 'TBT is not field INP']; BMK-003 CLS P75 good<=0.1/NI 0.1-0.25/poor>0.25 [G12, HARD]; BMK-004 WCAG 2.2 AA unless stricter law/contract [W01,W02, HARD]; BMK-005 security release gate: 0 open confirmed critical vulnerabilities, high-risk exceptions require formal approval [O01, HARD]; BMK-006 critical conversion path: 100% pass for production release test, 0 unowned P0 failures [Internal control, HARD]; BMK-007 sitemap hygiene: 100% intended canonical indexable 200 URLs, 0 unintended redirects/noindex/4xx/5xx [G04, HARD]; BMK-008 redirect control: one hop where controllable, no loops, closest intent match [G06,SF03,A01, HARD]; BMK-009 6.6% median landing-page CVR Q4-2024 context-only [UB01, INDUSTRY]; BMK-010 ~70% cart abandonment context-only [BM02, INDUSTRY]; BMK-011 62% mobile PDPs mediocre-or-worse Baymard 2026 [BM01, INDUSTRY]; BMK-012 GSC generative reports subset-rollout — 'Mark not available rather than fabricate data' [G15, PLATFORM]; BMK-013 ~15% Wikipedia AIO traffic-decline preprint — 'Do not generalize to commerce/lead-gen without evidence' [A02, ACADEMIC]. All 8 HARD rows are release-gate/stop-launch grade; INDUSTRY/PLATFORM/ACADEMIC rows are explicitly context-only, never targets.

structures.name: Gap calculation + competitor-percentile storage schema
structures.detail: Higher-is-better: Gap = target - current; Relative gap = (target - current) / target. Lower-is-better: Gap = current - target. Competitor percentiles must store: competitor set, values, median, upper quartile, leader, collection date, market, method. Rule: do not compare values created by different tools without normalization.

structures.name: Diagnostic rule (7-link issue chain)
structures.detail: 'A metric crossing a threshold creates an investigation, not an automatic solution.' Every issue record must connect: observation -> affected segment -> corroborating evidence -> likely mechanism -> proposed intervention -> acceptance test -> commercial guardrail. This is the package's decision-provenance schema.

structures.name: Source-ID citation scheme
structures.source: BENCHMARK_REGISTER.csv source_ids col; bracket tags in dictionary/CSV rows
structures.detail: Benchmark and metric rows cite external sources by short IDs: G04, G06, G12, G15 (Google docs), W01/W02 (WCAG), O01 (OWASP 2025), UB01 (Unbounce), BM01/BM02 (Baymard), SF03, A01, A02 (academic preprint), plus 'Internal control'. The resolving source register is NOT in these four files — it must exist elsewhere in the package and must survive the merge for R2 provenance to work.

structures.name: Embedded stop-launch / release-gate conditions
structures.detail: Zero-tolerance-at-release conditions scattered across rows: 0 open critical vulnerabilities (SEC-001/BMK-005); 100% critical conversion success in release tests (TEC-010/BMK-006); 0% P0/P1 status errors (TEC-001); 0 redirect chains on internal links (TEC-002); 100% rendering parity on priority elements (TEC-003); 100% sitemap hygiene (SEO-009/BMK-007); 100% canonical agreement on priority URLs (SEO-008); 100% hreflang validity (INT-001); 0 critical translation defects (INT-003); 0 severe UX errors (UX-003); WCAG 2.2 AA (UX-005/BMK-004); 100% scheduled restore tests (SEC-002); 100% evidence completeness for P0/P1 closures with 'Reopen until definition of done is met' (OPS-001).

registers.name: METRIC_DICTIONARY.csv
registers.columns: metric_id, workstream, metric, definition_formula, required_dimensions, source_of_truth, secondary_tools, target_method, red_flag, diagnosis, improvement_action, do_not
registers.purpose: Row-level authority for all 63 metric controls; declared canonical by the dictionary MD §7. Dimensions inside cells are semicolon-delimited.

registers.name: TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv
registers.columns: stage, primary_recommended, secondary_or_enterprise, mandatory_reports, agent_automation, decision_supported, limitations
registers.purpose: 18-stage tool map; the agent_automation column (API/warehouse export, Search Console API, GA4 Data API, GTM API, CI tests, REST APIs/scheduled jobs, CLI/scheduler, axe-in-Playwright/CI, archive scripts) is the machine-readable automation surface R7 asks for — it is DESCRIPTIVE capability, not authorization to write to production.

registers.name: BENCHMARK_REGISTER.csv
registers.columns: benchmark_id, workstream, metric, value_or_rule, applicability, class, source_ids, caveat
registers.purpose: 13 benchmarks BMK-001..013; class values used: HARD (8), INDUSTRY (3), PLATFORM (1), ACADEMIC (1). Every row carries a caveat; HARD rows are release-gate grade, all others explicitly context-only.

steps: Q1 metric + exact formula
Q2 mandatory dimensions
Q3 source of truth (third-party estimates cannot overrule finance/CRM/GSC/server)
Q4 benchmark class
Q5 absolute + % gap with confidence and comparability
Q6 diagnosis before recommendation
Q7 exact improvement + acceptance test + monitoring period
Hard threshold only where authoritative standard exists
Own seasonal/cohort baseline as default comparator
Peer percentiles from named competitor set, identical definitions
Industry benchmarks context-only with sample/year/sector/definition recorded
Commercial targets from contribution economics, capacity, payback
Experiments: MDE + guardrails defined before launch
Record 'not comparable' rather than force a misleading benchmark
Apply directional gap formulas
Store competitor set/values/median/upper-quartile/leader/date/market/method for percentiles
No cross-tool comparison without normalization
Threshold crossing opens an investigation, never an automatic fix
Issue record chain: observation -> affected segment -> corroborating evidence -> likely mechanism -> proposed intervention -> acceptance test -> commercial guardrail
Consult per-metric red_flag/diagnosis/improvement_action/do_not columns
OPS-001: reopen closed items until evidence complete (100% P0/P1)

new_capabilities: 63-row quantitative metric dictionary (formula + mandatory dimensions + source-of-truth + red-flag + diagnosis + prohibited shortcut per metric) — v1 has gates but no metric layer
6-class benchmark taxonomy (HARD/OWN/PEER/INDUSTRY/ECONOMIC/EXPERIMENT) + 13-row benchmark register with 4 register classes (HARD/INDUSTRY/PLATFORM/ACADEMIC) and per-row caveats
'Record not comparable' convention — explicit anti-forcing rule for benchmarks
Gap-calculation formulas (directional) + competitor-percentile storage schema (set/values/median/upper-quartile/leader/date/market/method) + no-cross-tool-comparison rule
7-link diagnostic issue chain (observation→segment→evidence→mechanism→intervention→acceptance test→commercial guardrail) — a ready-made R2 decision-provenance schema
Seven-question report discipline — R3 report-body skeleton
18-stage tool-stack register with agent_automation and limitations columns — R7's machine-readable tool/skill map format
AI-search visibility workstream (AI-001..004: generative impressions, prompt mention share, citation share, AI factual accuracy with 100%-material-facts standard) — entirely absent from v1
Source-ID citation scheme ([G12], [W01], [O01], [UB01], [BM01/02], [A02]...) linking every benchmark to an external source register
OPS metrics quantifying the evidence law (OPS-001 evidence completeness 100% P0/P1; OPS-002 change failure rate)
Per-metric prohibited-shortcut ('do_not') doctrine — 63 named anti-patterns including anti-fabrication, anti-spam, anti-vanity-metric rules
Economic target derivation (contribution/capacity/payback) and experiment discipline (MDE + guardrails pre-launch)
conflicts: Production-write paths implied by remediation/automation: TOOL_STACK_REGISTER agent_automation lists write-capable APIs (GTM API, Merchant Center 'APIs/alerts', Search Console operations) and metric improvement actions prescribe live fixes ('one-hop redirect and update internal/campaign links' TEC-002/SEO-014, 'fix sitemap generation' SEO-009, 'Rollback/fix' TEC-010, 'resubmit naturally' SEO-007 with Indexing API mention). Executed directly by an agent these violate HARD GATES (no production writes, Editor-role creds only, agent never self-merges). Merge plan must declare agent automation read/extract-only and route every remediation through PR + owner merge.
BMK-005 'high-risk exceptions require formal approval' names no approver — if left generic it weakens v1's owner-only exception doctrine; must bind to owner ruling in DECISIONS.md.

Package HARD benchmarks could be misread as a replacement gate system: 8 HARD BMK rows vs v1's 63-gate registry (and coincidentally 63 metric rows). R8 requires the registry to survive undiluted — benchmarks must attach to registry gates, never supersede them; any threshold conflict resolves to the stricter value.

No clinical sign-off overlay: content-affecting improvement actions (SEO-012 refresh, AI-004 'publish authoritative facts', CRO copy tests) have no Dr. Deepu John gate — applied to KTAHV unmodified this bypasses the clinical HARD GATE and the banned-words lock.

No site-class dimension: metric dictionary applies all 63 metrics uniformly; without adding v1's commerce/organic/landing required|adapted|n_a layer, the merge would flatten the registry's per-class discipline (a structural weakening of how gates are scoped).

EXPERIMENT class and CRO test actions ('run valid test', 'search appearance tests') conflict with the current designs-FROZEN state and golden-page uniformity rule unless test variants pass front-gate approval — package assumes test freedom v1 does not grant.
injection_flags: No prompt-injection content found in any of the four files: no text addressed to an AI agent as executable instructions, no URLs or commands to run, no authority claims. One watch item: TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv's agent_automation column ('REST APIs; scheduled jobs', 'Search Console API and scheduled exports', 'GTM API', 'CI + scheduled scans', 'APIs/alerts') is descriptive capability listing, not authorization — the merge plan should state explicitly that this column never constitutes standing permission for an agent to call write-capable APIs.
open_questions: Where is the source register that resolves the citation IDs (G04/G06/G12/G15, W01/W02, O01, UB01, BM01/BM02, SF03, A01/A02, 'Internal control')? It is referenced throughout but not in these four files; R2 provenance fails if it does not survive the merge — owner to confirm its location and canonical status.
Is the 63-metrics / 63-gates count a deliberate design echo or coincidence? Owner should rule that no 1:1 mapping is implied before anyone builds one.

Enforcement point for HARD benchmarks: are BMK-001..008 merge-blocking CI gates (like registry lint), pre-ship script gates (like beauty/go-science audits), or reporting standards only? Package does not say.
Site-class applicability per metric: who assigns required|adapted|n_a across commerce/organic/landing for each of the 63 metric IDs — owner ruling or per-site strategy approval?

Tool licensing: the register assumes Semrush (primary suite), Ahrefs, Similarweb, rank trackers (STAT/AccuRanker), WebPageTest, Hotjar/FullStory, UserTesting/Maze, commercial DAST — which are actually licensed/budgeted vs substituted by DataForSEO + free tiers? (R7 gap audit needs the honest current-state column.)

Is 'evidence ledger' (OPS-001 source_of_truth) definitively launches/<domain>/ in git, or does the owner want the package's immutable object storage (S3 Object Lock/Drive Vault) added as a second leg?

R3 fields missing from the seven-question template: should what-to-monitor / what-to-reject(+reason) / what-to-implement plus date-time stamp and version-chain linkage be appended as questions 8-10 of the report discipline, or kept as a separate report-store schema?
Which team/agent owns the 'controlled prompt panel' for AI-002/003 (model versions, prompt set, cadence, panel stability), and is spend on repeated model runs approved?
TEC-009 do_not 'Install tools/apps without owner or expiry' implies a third-party script approval register with expiry dates — does the owner want that as a new register or a gate-registry row?

BMK-006/TEC-010 'production release test' for critical conversion paths: on Vercel preview or production? v1 forbids production writes — owner to define the canonical test environment for '100% pass for production release test'.

readings.summary: The spine of the package is a 9-phase gated lifecycle (Phases 0-8, each with a mandatory output and a stop condition), governed by 10 'Never' operating rules, a 6-tier evidence hierarchy, a 6-class benchmark/target algorithm (HARD/OWN/PEER/INDUSTRY/ECONOMIC/EXPERIMENTAL), a 10-type competitor taxonomy with a 7-way strategic decision (defend/match/flank/attack/create/partner/ignore), two opportunity-economics formulas with input-provenance labels, a 10-point definition-of-done chain, a 5-way exclusion classification (deferred/not-applicable/rejected/unknown/accepted-risk), and an 18-row capability/specialist map with explicit AI-role limits. It is broadly compatible with v1 doctrine (mine-first, proof-of-work, evidence law, agent restrictions) and strengthens it with benchmark classes, decision/exclusion registers and SHA-256 evidence manifests — but the spine files never mention v1's golden-page, beauty, go-science, dual external-AI review or the 63-gate registry, so wholesale adoption of the package lifecycle would silently drop them (R8 risk); the package's approval language ('without the required approval gate', 'a named owner accepts residual risk') is looser than v1's owner-only HARD GATES and must not be allowed to weaken them. No prompt injection detected in these four files; the README's operator imperatives and the bundled Python utilities are the only execute-shaped content and must be treated as data/reviewed code, never run blindly.

structures.name: Phase-gated lifecycle (Phases 0-8)
structures.detail: Exact phase names in order: 0 Classify and charter; 1 Baseline and discovery; 2 Diagnose and prioritize; 3 Strategy and specification; 4 Build and controlled implementation; 5 Pre-launch QA and rehearsal; 6 Launch command centre; 7 Stabilize and verify; 8 Monitor and improve. Each phase row carries: question answered, mandatory output, stop condition. Stop conditions verbatim: P0='Ambiguous scope, no accountable owner or no legal authority'; P1='Missing commercial truth, incomplete URL discovery or unrecorded data gaps'; P2='Recommendations without evidence, impact or acceptance criteria'; P3='Design without page purpose, measurement or protected elements'; P4='Untraceable changes or production edits without rollback'; P5='Open P0; unaccepted P1; failed conversion, tracking, redirect, security or rollback test'; P6='Guardrail breach or inability to roll back'; P7='Unexplained material regression'; P8='No owner, no evidence, no closed-loop learning'.

structures.name: 10 Non-negotiable operating rules (prohibited-shortcut list)
structures.detail: (1) Never begin with design — begin with business economics, market definition, evidence access, protected baseline. (2) Never remove/merge/rename a URL until traffic, queries, conversions, revenue, links, internal links, ads, emails, offline references and historical purpose checked. (3) Never replace a proven landing page without keeping the original as control or recoverable copy+baseline. (4) Never optimize a third-party score when first-party revenue/user evidence contradicts it. (5) Never call work complete because code written/ticket done — requires deployment, live retest, stored evidence. (6) Never use competitor copying as strategy. (7) Never use Reddit/YouTube/vendor benchmark as ONLY evidence for a high-impact decision. (8) Never let an AI agent autonomously publish, migrate, redirect, delete, disavow, change tracking, alter checkout or modify legal/medical claims without the required approval gate. (9) Never overwrite raw baseline files — immutable dated copies and hashes. (10) Never launch with unresolved P0; P1 exceptions require named accountable acceptance AND expiry date.

structures.name: Evidence hierarchy (6 tiers)
structures.detail: 1 Commercial truth (finance, backend orders, contribution margin, CRM, qualified calls, refunds, returns, repeat purchase); 2 First-party platform evidence (GSC, GA4, GTM, Google Ads, Merchant Center, Business Profile, server logs, Shopify Analytics, form/payment/email logs); 3 Controlled tests (usability, experiments, QA, browser/device, Playwright, accessibility, security); 4 Diagnostic platforms (Screaming Frog, Semrush, DataForSEO, Ahrefs, Similarweb, PageSpeed, CrUX, GTmetrix, WebPageTest, Clarity/Hotjar); 5 External benchmarks and estimates (industry medians, traffic estimates, volume, KD, DA/DR/AS, AI-visibility estimates); 6 Anecdotal discovery evidence (Reddit, forums, YouTube, practitioner case reports — generate questions/failure-mode checks only, never prove a universal rule). Precedence rule (README §Accuracy): platform documentation and standards outrank opinions; client commercial truth outranks tool estimates.

structures.name: Benchmark class algorithm (6 classes) + target validity fields
structures.detail: Classes: HARD (standards/zero-defect: valid HTTPS, no P0 broken conversion path, WCAG target, CWV thresholds); OWN (trailing 12-16 month seasonal baseline, cohort, device/region distribution); PEER (named competitor median, upper quartile and leader — same market/device/intent); INDUSTRY (large-sample published benchmark with year, sample, definition); ECONOMIC (minimum performance required by margin, CAC, sales capacity, payback); EXPERIMENTAL (hypothesis-specific target with minimum detectable effect and decision rule). A target is valid only when metric definition, source, segment, baseline period, benchmark date, confidence and owner are recorded. Generic industry-average targets rejected when conversion definition, market or traffic mix differs materially.

structures.name: Competitor taxonomy (10 types) + 7-way strategic decision
structures.detail: Types: direct commercial; organic SERP; paid-search/paid-social; marketplace/retailer; local/map; substitute solutions/category alternatives; content/publisher attention; AI-answer recommendation; reputation/review; aspirational design and experience benchmarks. Decision must be exactly one of: defend | match a mandatory parity factor | flank an underserved segment | attack a vulnerable demand pool | create a category | partner | deliberately ignore. NOTE: QA report §1 lists only six (defend/match/flank/attack/create/ignore — omits partner); internal inconsistency.

structures.name: Opportunity economics formulas + input provenance
structures.detail: Expected incremental contribution = addressable demand x attainable share x qualified conversion rate x contribution value x confidence - incremental cost. Priority score = incremental contribution x strategic importance x confidence x reach / (effort x time-to-value x risk). Every input must be labelled observed | calculated | estimated | assumed. Sensitivity range mandatory for high-value bets.

structures.name: Definition of done (10-point completion chain)
structures.detail: Complete only when ALL true: (1) requirement + acceptance criteria exist; (2) implementation linked to issue/change ID; (3) code/content/configuration committed or versioned; (4) automated and manual checks pass; (5) deployed to intended environment; (6) live output retested; (7) evidence archived with tool/version/configuration, timestamp and hash; (8) relevant KPI monitored for specified period; (9) no unexplained regression; (10) reviewer approves OR a named owner accepts residual risk.

structures.name: Workflow selector matrix
structures.detail: 4 business models (B2C, B2B, D2C, Shopify) x 4 asset situations (New asset / Existing asset i.e. upgrade-migration / Organic programme new-or-existing / Landing page new-or-existing). QA report states 24 granular execution workflows exist: six per business model (so organic and landing each split new vs existing). Landing flavors: B2C lead/booking, B2B demand/ABM, D2C product/offer, Shopify landing page.

structures.name: Governing outcomes (7)
structures.detail: Every project must protect or improve: (1) qualified market visibility across conventional search, generative search, local, shopping, marketplaces, paid media, referrals; (2) revenue, contribution margin, qualified pipeline, CLV; (3) URL, content, ranking, link, review, tracking and audience equity; (4) user task success, accessibility, trust, brand positioning; (5) technical reliability, security, privacy, recoverability; (6) regional, language, currency, inventory, fulfilment, legal correctness; (7) measurement integrity and proof work was actually completed.

structures.name: Exclusion classification (5-way) + change control
structures.detail: Every omitted recommendation must be classified as deferred | not applicable | rejected | unknown | accepted risk, with reason and review date (Decision/Exclusion Register). Every new source must enter through the Source Register and change-control process. Source priority: (1) primary standards + platform docs; (2) large-sample/academic findings labelled with applicability+limitations; (3) vendor data authoritative only for vendor's own tool/dataset; (4) Reddit/forums/YouTube/expert opinion = failure-mode discovery only.

structures.name: Known intentional exclusions (9 anti-patterns)

APPROVAL DILUTION RISK: Master OS rule 8 says agent may not publish/migrate/redirect/delete/etc. 'without the required approval gate' — implying any gate approval suffices. v1 HARD GATES prohibit production writes, deletions and DNS/robots changes OUTRIGHT (human performs them; owner-only bypass, logged). RESIDUAL-RISK ACCEPTANCE: DoD point 10 ('reviewer approves, or a named owner accepts residual risk') and rule 10 P1 exceptions ('named accountable acceptance') allow any named person to waive; in v1 only the owner approves front gates and bypasses, and the agent never self-approves. ESTIMATED/ASSUMED INPUTS: package permits labeled 'estimated' and 'assumed' inputs in the opportunity model; v1 HARD GATE bans inventing facts/IDs/prices — gaps are ASKED (R4).
