readings.summary: The evidence/QA/agent-execution layer of the v2 package defines: (a) a three-layer evidence model (RAW immutable / PROCESSED / PUBLISHED) with a fixed 11-folder client-project storage tree; (b) SHA-256 artifact manifests (schema + archive_artifact.py + validate_project_evidence.py); (c) an 11-status proof-of-completion state machine (OPEN→...→CLOSED, plus ACCEPTED_RISK in the schema) with no-skip and independent-review rules; (d) a 13-item automated release-check list; (e) an AI-agent operating contract — 11 required job-spec inputs, 10 evidence labels for every agent statement, 9 prohibited autonomous actions; (f) a 6-status decision/exclusion register; (g) a 10-item "what must not count as proof" negative list; and (h) five fixed-column CSV registers plus three JSON Schemas. It is largely a formalization and strengthening of v1's Evidence Law and Proof-of-Work doctrine and directly serves R2/R3/R4; the main friction points are storage location (Drive/object storage vs v1 "if it isn't in the repo, it didn't happen"), CONDITIONAL_GO/ACCEPTED_RISK escape hatches vs v1's binary owner-signed gates, UTC vs IST timestamps, and a prohibited-actions list that overlaps but does not fully contain HARD GATES 1–9 (merge must be a union, never a replacement). No prompt-injection content found in these files; both Python scripts were statically reviewed and are benign.

structures.name: Three evidence layers
structures.detail: 1 RAW (immutable exports exactly as collected: CSV, JSON, crawl files, HAR, screenshots, videos, PDFs, logs, platform exports) → 2 PROCESSED (normalized tables, joins, calculated metrics, notebooks/scripts; every processed artifact references its raw inputs) → 3 PUBLISHED (client reports, dashboards, issue summaries, decisions; reference processed calculations and raw evidence IDs). Rule: never edit or overwrite RAW; corrections create a NEW run ID.

structures.name: Required storage path (11 numbered folders)
structures.detail: clients/{client_id}/projects/{project_id}/ → 00_governance/ · 01_raw/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/{source}/{report_type}/{run_id}/ · 02_processed/{dataset}/{version}/ · 03_findings/{issue_id}/ · 04_specifications/ · 05_implementation/{release_id}/ · 06_qa/{release_id}/{environment}/ · 07_launch/{release_id}/ · 08_monitoring/{cadence}/{period}/ · 09_published_reports/{version}/ · 10_archive/. Storage split: large binary raw reports → durable object/document storage or Google Drive; code, schemas, manifests, small text evidence → version control. Sensitive data follows access/retention/deletion policies.

structures.name: Artifact manifest required content (13 bullets)
structures.detail: Prose list: artifact ID + run ID; client/project/release/issue IDs; source/tool + version; exact configuration/API endpoint/query/crawl settings; domain/property, environment, URL scope; market, country, location, language, currency, device, user agent; date range, comparison range, timezone, collection timestamp; operator or agent identity + model/version; raw file names, MIME types, sizes, SHA-256 hashes; known exclusions/sampling/failures/data gaps; upstream input IDs + downstream issue/report IDs; review and approval status. Explicitly modeled on W3C PROV (entities/activities/agents) [W03]. JSON Schema required: artifact_id, run_id, project_id, source_tool, collected_at_utc (date-time), files (minItems 1; each file requires path, sha256 matching ^[a-f0-9]{64}$, bytes ≥0; optional mime_type); optional release_id, issue_id, tool_version, configuration, scope, date_range, operator_agent, known_gaps; additionalProperties:false.

structures.name: Historical report policy (8 rules)
structures.detail: 1 Save each human-readable report as PDF when supported; 2 also save the CSV/JSON/API response and settings — PDF alone insufficient; 3 never overwrite a monthly or pre-launch report (new timestamp/version); 4 generate a checksum manifest after collection; 5 store baseline screenshots + critical-page full-page captures; 6 for dynamic dashboards export underlying data + dashboard definition/query; 7 record tool plan/licence limitations and unavailable dimensions; 8 retain pre-migration evidence and redirect maps for the approved retention period (at least useful life of migration + legal/contractual).

structures.name: Issue evidence bundle (11 numbered items)
structures.detail: Every issue folder contains: 1 issue record + severity; 2 raw evidence or artifact-ID pointers; 3 affected URL/entity export; 4 business consequence + confidence; 5 recommendation + acceptance criteria; 6 implementation link (commit, PR, CMS revision, tag version, configuration or vendor ticket); 7 staging test evidence; 8 live deployment evidence; 9 post-deployment retest; 10 KPI monitoring result; 11 final reviewer decision or accepted risk.

structures.name: Proof-of-completion state machine (status chain)
structures.detail: OPEN → EVIDENCED → APPROVED → IMPLEMENTING → STAGING_QA → READY_FOR_RELEASE → DEPLOYED → LIVE_VERIFIED → MONITORED → CLOSED. Rules: a ticket may NOT skip directly from IMPLEMENTING to CLOSED; a failed live test returns it to IMPLEMENTING or triggers rollback; P0/P1 closure requires INDEPENDENT review. The JSON schema adds an 11th status ACCEPTED_RISK not present in the prose chain.

structures.name: Automated release checks (13 items)
structures.detail: build/unit/integration tests; Playwright critical journeys + traces; visual snapshot comparison under controlled environment [PW01]; redirect-map tests + no-loop checks; internal broken-link scan; robots/noindex/canonical/hreflang/schema tests; analytics event + ecommerce payload tests; axe-core accessibility scan plus manual critical-journey checks; Lighthouse CI/performance budgets; security/dependency scans; sitemap validation; market/language/currency/inventory tests; backup + rollback verification. Plus: protect release branch, require reviews/checks; build provenance/artifact attestations may verify where/how release artifacts were produced [GH01-GH02].

structures.name: AI-agent operating contract (11 required job inputs)
structures.detail: Agent must receive: workflow ID + phase; client/project/release IDs; exact domain/market/language/device/date scope; authorized tools + credentials boundaries; input artifact IDs + freshness requirements; required output schema; evidence + citation requirements; prohibited actions; approval gate + escalation owner; retry/timeout/cost limits; definition of done. YAML example fields: workflow_id (SHOPIFY_EXISTING_STORE_UPGRADE), project_id, phase, scope{production_domain, staging_domain, markets[], languages[], devices[]}, inputs{artifact_ids[], freshness_days:7}, authorized_tools[] (all read-suffixed: google_search_console_read, ga4_read, screaming_frog_cli, dataforseo_read, shopify_analytics_read), prohibited_actions[] (production_publish, redirect_change, robots_change, delete_content, disavow_submit), outputs{schema: agency_issue.schema.json, evidence_manifest: artifact_manifest.schema.json}, gate{required: BASELINE_APPROVAL, approver_role: accountable_business_owner}, definition_of_done[] (all mandatory reports archived with hashes; master URL inventory reconciled; competitor baseline completed; unknowns and exclusions logged).

structures.name: Agent evidence labels (10, exact)
structures.detail: OBSERVED_FIRST_PARTY · OBSERVED_LIVE_TEST · CALCULATED · THIRD_PARTY_ESTIMATE · USER_PROVIDED · EXTERNAL_BENCHMARK · ANECDOTAL_SIGNAL · ASSUMPTION · RECOMMENDATION · UNKNOWN. Every agent statement must carry exactly one label internally.

structures.name: Prohibited autonomous agent actions (9, without specified human gate)
structures.detail: 1 publish or delete production content; 2 change domains, DNS, robots, canonicals, hreflang or redirects; 3 submit disavow files; 4 change analytics definitions, consent or payment logic; 5 install/uninstall Shopify apps or alter checkout; 6 make regulated medical, legal or financial claims; 7 send competitor outreach, reviews or public communications; 8 expose secrets or customer data; 9 approve its own P0/P1 evidence. Plus mandate: threat-model agentic systems for prompt injection, tool misuse, insecure memory/context, excessive autonomy [O02].

structures.name: Exclusion and decision register statuses (6, exact)
structures.detail: INCLUDED_NOW (applicable and scheduled) · DEFERRED (applicable but delayed, with risk + reconsideration date) · NOT_APPLICABLE (reason tied to business model/technology/market/absence of feature) · REJECTED (evidence or economics do not support) · UNKNOWN (evidence/access missing; owner + next step required) · ACCEPTED_RISK (accountable owner accepts consequence until expiry). Each record: source, rationale, risk, owner, approval, expiry, reconsideration trigger. Stated purpose: prevents future reviewers or AIs from re-proposing an already-evaluated idea, while allowing reopen when assumptions change (directly serves R2).

structures.name: What must NOT count as proof (10 items)
structures.detail: task status without live retest; screenshot without URL/timestamp/environment/expected result; AI-generated summary without raw exports; tool health score without issue-level evidence; PDF without machine-readable data/configuration; code committed but not deployed; deployment completed but conversion/indexation not verified; improved rankings without qualified conversion/revenue analysis; benchmark without source/date/segment/definition; 'not applicable' without rationale.

structures.name: agency_issue.schema.json shape
structures.detail: Required: issue_id, project_id, phase (integer 0–8), severity (P0|P1|P2|P3), observation (minLength 1), evidence_ids (minItems 1), business_consequence, recommendation, acceptance_criteria (minItems 1), status (11-value enum incl. ACCEPTED_RISK). Optional: evidence_label (10-value enum), affected_entities[], owner, confidence (0–1), implementation_reference, retest_evidence_ids[]. additionalProperties:false — extending with v1 gate references requires a schema edit. Phase bounded 0–8 → hard-codes a 9-phase workflow model.

structures.name: phase_gate.schema.json shape
structures.detail: Required: gate_id, project_id, phase (integer 0–8), decision (GO | CONDITIONAL_GO | NO_GO), evidence_ids, approver. Optional: open_p0 (≥0), open_p1 (≥0), conditions[], approved_at (date-time). additionalProperties:false. Note: evidence_ids has no minItems, so an empty evidence array validates — weaker than the prose standard.

structures.name: archive_artifact.py behavior
structures.detail: CLI: --project-id --run-id --artifact-id --source-tool [--tool-version] --operator --out-dir files... Copies each file (shutil.copy2) into out-dir, computes SHA-256 in 1 MiB chunks, writes manifest.json with collected_at_utc = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() (UTC, not IST), known_gaps:[] and files[{path,sha256,bytes,mime_type}], prints manifest path. No validation against the schema, no release_id/issue_id/scope/date_range fields emitted.

structures.name: validate_project_evidence.py behavior
structures.detail: Recursively finds manifest.json under a project root; errors if none; per manifest checks JSON parses, six required keys present (artifact_id, run_id, project_id, source_tool, collected_at_utc, files), each referenced file exists and its recomputed SHA-256 matches. Prints JSON {project_root, manifest_count, errors, pass}; exit 1 on any error. Self-declares 'Basic project evidence validator. It does not replace professional QA.' — hash integrity only, far weaker than v1's 63-gate lint.

registers.name: EVIDENCE_LEDGER.csv
registers.purpose: Master per-artifact evidence ledger implementing the three-layer model with hashes and lineage
registers.columns: artifact_id, run_id, project_id, release_id, issue_id, layer_raw_processed_published, source_tool, tool_version, configuration, domain_property, environment, market_language_device, date_range, collected_at_utc, operator_agent, file_path, mime_type, bytes, sha256, upstream_artifacts, downstream_issues_reports, known_gaps, review_status, retention_until (24 columns; header-only template)

registers.name: IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION.csv
registers.purpose: Per-issue staging→live verification trail backing the state machine (STAGING_QA → DEPLOYED → LIVE_VERIFIED → MONITORED → CLOSED)
registers.columns: verification_id, issue_id, requirement, acceptance_criteria, implementation_type, commit_pr_revision_config_ticket, staging_url, staging_test, staging_evidence, release_id, deployed_at, production_url, live_test, live_evidence, monitoring_metric, monitoring_window, result, reviewer, closure_status (19 columns)

registers.name: DECISION_EXCLUSION_REGISTER.csv
registers.purpose: Every proposal/control gets one of the 6 decision statuses with rationale, owner, expiry and reconsideration trigger — the anti-re-proposal memory (R2)
registers.columns: decision_id, project_id, workflow_phase, proposal_or_control, status_included_deferred_not_applicable_rejected_unknown_accepted_risk, rationale, evidence_ids, risk_if_wrong, owner, approver, decision_date, expiry_or_review_date, reconsideration_trigger (13 columns)

registers.name: PHASE_GATE_APPROVAL.csv
registers.purpose: Phase-gate sign-off record with GO/CONDITIONAL_GO/NO_GO decision, open P0/P1 counts and accepted-risk carve-outs
registers.columns: gate_id, project_id, phase, required_evidence, evidence_ids, open_p0, open_p1, accepted_risk_ids, automated_checks_result, reviewer, accountable_approver, decision_go_conditional_no_go, conditions, approved_at, expires_at (15 columns; note: has reviewer AND accountable_approver + accepted_risk_ids/expires_at beyond phase_gate.schema.json fields)

registers.name: REPORT_AND_TOOL_RUN_MANIFEST.csv
registers.purpose: Per tool-run/report provenance record (which tool, exact query/config, scope, timing, gaps, resulting issues) — the R3 report-store substrate
registers.columns: run_id, project_id, phase, tool, tool_version, report_name, api_endpoint_or_query, configuration_file, domain_scope, url_scope, market, language, device_user_agent, date_range, comparison_range, timezone, started_at, completed_at, operator_agent, raw_artifact_ids, failures_gaps, issue_ids_created, next_run (23 columns; lacks R3's 'what to monitor / what to reject+reason / what to implement' fields)

steps: Collect → store immutable RAW under 01_raw/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/{source}/{report_type}/{run_id}/
Generate SHA-256 checksum manifest immediately after collection (archive_artifact.py)
Derive PROCESSED under 02_processed/{dataset}/{version}/ referencing raw input IDs
PUBLISH reports under 09_published_reports/{version}/ referencing processed + raw IDs
Corrections never overwrite — new run_id/version; validator (validate_project_evidence.py) recomputes hashes and fails on any mismatch
OPEN
EVIDENCED (raw evidence or artifact-ID pointers attached)
APPROVED
IMPLEMENTING (implementation link: commit/PR/CMS revision/config/ticket)
STAGING_QA (staging test evidence in 06_qa/{release_id}/{environment}/)
READY_FOR_RELEASE (13 automated release checks where technically possible)
DEPLOYED (live deployment evidence)
LIVE_VERIFIED (post-deployment retest; failed live test → back to IMPLEMENTING or rollback)
MONITORED (KPI monitoring result over monitoring_window)
CLOSED (P0/P1 require independent review; no skip from IMPLEMENTING to CLOSED) — or ACCEPTED_RISK with accountable owner + expiry
Assemble required_evidence + evidence_ids
Count open_p0 / open_p1; list accepted_risk_ids
Record automated_checks_result
Reviewer review, then accountable_approver decision: GO | CONDITIONAL_GO (with conditions[]) | NO_GO
Record approved_at / expires_at in PHASE_GATE_APPROVAL.csv
Issue job spec: workflow_id, phase, IDs, exact scope (domains/markets/languages/devices), input artifact_ids + freshness_days
Bound the agent: authorized_tools (read-only pattern), prohibited_actions, retry/timeout/cost limits
Agent labels every statement with one of the 10 evidence labels; outputs conform to agency_issue.schema.json + artifact_manifest.schema.json
Gate: named approval gate (e.g. BASELINE_APPROVAL) by approver_role accountable_business_owner; agent never approves its own P0/P1 evidence
Definition of done checked (reports archived with hashes, inventory reconciled, unknowns/exclusions logged)

overlaps.package_item: Three-layer evidence model (RAW immutable / PROCESSED / PUBLISHED, corrections = new run ID)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 EVIDENCE LAW: launches/<domain>/ evidence committed to git; content-mined/ raw immutable; append-only audit passes
overlaps.note: Package formalizes what v1 already practices; adopt the layer labels and new-run-ID correction rule inside the existing launches/<domain>/ tree.

overlaps.package_item: Storage path clients/{client_id}/projects/{project_id}/ with 00–10 folders, large binaries in Drive/object storage
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 monorepo layout sites/<domain> + launches/<domain>/, doctrine 'if it isn't in the repo, it didn't happen'
overlaps.note: Drive/object-storage as evidence home contradicts repo-is-truth doctrine; also client_id is degenerate (single owner, multiple entities). Needs owner ruling on taxonomy mapping and any off-repo storage carve-out with repo-committed manifests as the pointer of record.

overlaps.package_item: Artifact manifest + SHA-256 hashes (schema, archive_artifact.py, validate_project_evidence.py)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 evidence committed to git with second-precision IST timestamps; no hash manifests
overlaps.note: Net-new tamper-evidence capability; wire the validator into CI alongside existing lints. UTC-vs-IST timestamp standard must be ruled (see conflicts).

overlaps.package_item: Proof-of-completion state machine OPEN→…→CLOSED with no-skip + failed-live-test regression + independent P0/P1 review
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 PROOF-OF-WORK: no 'done' without working URL/output/passing spec; post-push live-fetch diff vs intent; fix-one ≠ done
overlaps.note: State machine formalizes v1 doctrine; map v1 live-fetch diff to the LIVE_VERIFIED transition requirement; keep v1's grep-all-instances rule as a closure precondition.

overlaps.package_item: 13 automated release checks + protected release branch + provenance attestations
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 GATE REGISTRY (63 gates, 3 site classes, merge-blocking lint) + design-review/beauty/go-science audit scripts + branch protection
overlaps.note: Map each of the 13 checks to existing registry gates; any check with no counterpart is ADDED as a new registry row (gates added, never weakened); the checklist never replaces the registry as source of truth.

overlaps.package_item: AI-agent operating contract + AGENT_JOB_SPEC_EXAMPLE.yaml (scope, authorized_tools, prohibited_actions, gate, definition_of_done)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 boot contract (boot-contract.mjs → state/boot.json), HARD GATES 1–9, unattended rule
overlaps.note: Per-task machine-readable job envelope is new and useful; generate it from the gate registry + HARD GATES so its prohibited_actions can never be a narrower list than v1's.

overlaps.package_item: 10 agent evidence labels (OBSERVED_FIRST_PARTY … UNKNOWN)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 HARD GATE 6: never invent facts/IDs/prices, gaps are ASKED not filled; R4 ask-when-in-doubt
overlaps.note: Operationalizes the never-invent gate; must add a binding rule that ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN-labeled statements TRIGGER an ask (label alone must not launder an assumption into shipped content).

overlaps.package_item: 9 prohibited autonomous actions (no production publish/delete, no DNS/robots/redirects/canonicals/hreflang, no disavow, no analytics/consent/payment changes, no Shopify app/checkout changes, no regulated claims, no outreach, no secret exposure, no self-approval of P0/P1)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 HARD GATES 1–9 (no prod writes, no deletions, no DNS/robots, Editor creds only, --force-with-lease only, never invent, clinical sign-off Dr. Deepu John, no staging→prod DB copies, never self-merge PRs)
overlaps.note: UNION only: package adds disavow/Shopify-checkout/analytics-consent-payment/outreach/secrets/regulated-claims (adopt as new gates); package list OMITS no-self-merge, Editor-creds, force-with-lease, clinical sign-off — those v1 gates must survive verbatim.

overlaps.package_item: Exclusion and decision register (6 statuses + rationale/owner/expiry/reconsideration trigger) + DECISION_EXCLUSION_REGISTER.csv
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 DECISIONS.md (owner rulings, incl. gate removal) — free-text, not statused
overlaps.note: Adopt the structured register as the R2 decision-provenance store; keep DECISIONS.md as the owner-ruling channel that feeds it; gate-removal rulings remain DECISIONS.md-only per v1 rule.

overlaps.package_item: Phase gate schema + PHASE_GATE_APPROVAL.csv (GO/CONDITIONAL_GO/NO_GO, open_p0/p1, accepted_risk_ids)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 FRONT GATES: launches/<domain>/approvals.yaml signed rows, CI fails PRs touching site pages with unsigned rows; agent never self-approves
overlaps.note: Keep approvals.yaml + CI block as the enforcement layer; adopt the richer gate record (evidence_ids, P0/P1 counts) as its payload. CONDITIONAL_GO must never unblock CI or substitute for a signed row (see conflicts).

overlaps.package_item: 'What must not count as proof' 10-item negative list
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 PROOF-OF-WORK doctrine (no done without URL; screenshot standards implicit)
overlaps.note: Strict superset of v1's negatives; adopt verbatim as a fail-closed checklist referenced by proof-of-work.

overlaps.package_item: Issue evidence bundle (11 items) + agency_issue.schema.json
overlaps.existing_mechanism: No v1 per-issue tracker (v1 uses QUESTIONS.md, DIRECTIVES.md, gate evidence folders)
overlaps.note: Net-new capability; clarify boundary with QUESTIONS.md (blocked asks) and DIRECTIVES.md (chat directives) so nothing is double-tracked.

overlaps.package_item: IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION.csv (staging→live→monitoring trail per issue)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 post-push live-fetch diff vs intent + gate evidence in launches/<domain>/
overlaps.note: Adopt the register; the v1 live-fetch diff artifact becomes the required live_evidence entry.

overlaps.package_item: REPORT_AND_TOOL_RUN_MANIFEST.csv + historical report policy (PDF + machine-readable + never overwrite)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: R3 report store requirement; v1 auto-handover reports in docs/reports/ (undated-schema markdown)
overlaps.note: Strong substrate for R3 but missing R3's per-report 'what to monitor / what to reject+reason / what to implement' and notes fields — extend columns; also feeds R6 baseline-before-sitemap (DataForSEO PDF + underlying data, never overwritten).

overlaps.package_item: archive_artifact.py / validate_project_evidence.py (Python)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 script ecosystem is Node .mjs (boot-contract.mjs, doctor.mjs, design-review.mjs, beauty-audit.mjs, go-science-audit.mjs)
overlaps.note: Adopt the behavior; owner decides port-to-mjs vs accepting a Python dependency; either way wire into CI and Monday lints. archive_artifact.py emits no scope/date_range/release_id — below its own manifest standard, needs extension.

overlaps.package_item: 06_qa/{release_id}/{environment} staging evidence + staging_domain in job spec
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 Vercel preview deploys; HARD GATE 8 no staging→prod DB copies; production DNS flips always human
overlaps.note: Compatible; map environment=preview to Vercel preview URLs; HARD GATE 8 and human DNS survive verbatim.

overlaps.package_item: Phase integer 0–8 hard-coded in issue + gate schemas
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 front-gate chain brief → strategy (fat) → design_source (MODE A/B) → golden_page → full build
overlaps.note: R8: front gates must be relocated into the 9-phase model undiluted — every v1 front gate needs an explicit phase-number home; golden-page-first must remain a blocking gate, not a phase note.

overlaps.package_item: approver_role: accountable_business_owner + independent P0/P1 review + agent never approves own evidence
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1: owner-only approvals, agent never self-approves/self-merges (owner-only bypass, logged)
overlaps.note: Same intent; v1 wording is stricter (never self-merge, logged bypass) — keep v1 as governing text, cite package as corroboration.

overlaps.package_item: Retention policy (retention_until, expires_at, pre-migration evidence + redirect maps retained)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 PROTECTION MAP (every legacy URL KEEP/MERGE/301) + MINE FIRST
overlaps.note: Complements protection map with explicit retention horizons; net-new fields.

overlaps.package_item: Agent security threat-modeling mandate (prompt injection, tool misuse, insecure memory/context, excessive autonomy) [O02]
overlaps.existing_mechanism: No explicit v1 counterpart
overlaps.note: New governance item; schedule as a recurring audit (fits R1 self-evolution channel list).

new_capabilities: SHA-256 checksum manifests for every evidence bundle + CI-runnable integrity validator (tamper-evidence; v1 has git commits but no content hashes)
Formal 11-status proof-of-completion state machine with no-skip rule, failed-live-test regression, and independent P0/P1 closure review
10-label evidence-epistemology taxonomy applied to every agent statement (operationalizes HARD GATE 6 / R4)
6-status decision/exclusion register with owner, expiry and reconsideration trigger — institutional memory that stops AIs re-proposing rejected ideas (directly satisfies R2)
Machine-readable per-task agent job-spec envelope (YAML) declaring scope, read-only authorized_tools, prohibited_actions, gate, approver_role, and definition_of_done
Three JSON Schemas (issue, artifact manifest, phase gate) enabling automated validation of evidence records
Five fixed-column CSV registers (evidence ledger, implementation verification, decision/exclusion, phase-gate approval, report/tool-run manifest)
Historical report policy: PDF + machine-readable pair, never-overwrite versioning, dashboard-definition export, tool-licence-limitation logging (substrate for R3 and R6)
Explicit 'what must not count as proof' negative list (10 items) extending v1 proof-of-work
Retention-horizon fields (retention_until, expiry/review dates) and pre-migration evidence retention rule
Agent-security threat-modeling requirement (prompt injection, tool misuse, insecure memory/context, excessive autonomy)
W3C PROV-style provenance framing (entities/activities/agents) with upstream/downstream lineage columns
conflicts: Storage location: §3 permits evidence in Google Drive/object storage; v1 Evidence Law is 'if it isn't in the repo, it didn't happen'. Any off-repo storage must at minimum keep the hash manifest committed to git as the record of truth — owner ruling required before adopting the clients/ tree.

CONDITIONAL_GO (phase_gate.schema.json / PHASE_GATE_APPROVAL.csv) is a softer decision than v1's binary signed front-gate approval; if it can unblock CI or stand in for a signed approvals.yaml row it weakens FRONT GATES. Must be constrained: CONDITIONAL_GO never releases a merge-block; conditions become tracked issues.

ACCEPTED_RISK appears as an issue status (agency_issue.schema.json) and as gate carve-out (accepted_risk_ids in PHASE_GATE_APPROVAL.csv), allowing a gate to pass with open items. Under v1 'gates are added, never weakened; removal needs owner ruling in DECISIONS.md', ACCEPTED_RISK must be owner-only and logged in DECISIONS.md, or it becomes a self-service gate bypass.

Prohibited-autonomous-actions list (§9) overlaps but does NOT contain all of HARD GATES 1–9: missing never-self-merge-PR, Editor-role-creds-only, --force-with-lease-only, clinical sign-off by Dr. Deepu John, no staging→prod DB copies. Adopting the package list as-is would silently narrow the gates — merge must be a strict union with v1 gates verbatim.
Timestamps: package standard is UTC (collected_at_utc, archive_artifact.py uses timezone.utc); v1 mandates second-precision IST. Pick one canonical (or store both) before registers fork.

agency_issue.schema.json and artifact_manifest.schema.json set additionalProperties:false — v1 extensions (registry gate IDs, entity/site-class, IST timestamps, beauty/go-science references) cannot be added without editing the schemas; adopting them frozen would block gate continuity (R8).

phase 0–8 integer bound hard-codes a 9-phase workflow; v1 front gates (brief/strategy/design_source/golden_page/full-build) have no phase numbers — relocation without an explicit mapping risks diluting golden-page-first, violating R8.

validate_project_evidence.py checks only manifest presence + hash integrity; if positioned as 'the QA gate' it would be far weaker than the 63-gate registry + beauty/go-science/design-review audits. The script itself disclaims this ('does not replace professional QA') — it must be additive, never a substitute.
phase_gate.schema.json evidence_ids lacks minItems, so a GO decision with zero evidence validates — weaker than both the package's own prose (§7/§11) and v1 evidence law; tighten before adoption.

archive_artifact.py emits manifests missing most of §4's required content (no scope, date_range, release_id, issue_id, configuration, review status) — the tool as shipped cannot produce a compliant manifest; extend before it becomes the standard.
injection_flags: None found in the 12 assigned files. §9 of EVIDENCE_STORAGE_QA_AND_AI_AGENT_EXECUTION_STANDARD_2026.md describes contracts FOR agents (procedure description, not directed instructions); AGENT_JOB_SPEC_EXAMPLE.yaml uses placeholder example.com domains and read-only tools; no URLs, endpoints, or commands are presented for blind execution. Citation keys [W03], [PW01], [GH01-GH02], [O02] are bare references with no embedded links in these files (their bibliography lives elsewhere in the package — whoever reads that file should verify the targets).

Both Python scripts were statically reviewed before any consideration of use: archive_artifact.py only copies named local files and writes a manifest; validate_project_evidence.py only reads and hashes. No network calls, no shell-outs, no destructive operations. Safe to adopt after normal code review; do not execute against production paths until the storage-location conflict is ruled.
open_questions: Storage ruling: does ALL evidence stay in the git monorepo (v1 doctrine), or is the package's Drive/object-storage split for large binaries accepted with repo-committed hash manifests as the pointer of record? Which artifact types, if any, may live off-repo?

Taxonomy mapping: how do clients/{client_id}/projects/{project_id} map onto the single-owner multi-entity fleet (entity → client_id? domain → project_id?), and do the 00–10 numbered folders replace or nest inside launches/<domain>/?
Timezone canon: keep v1 second-precision IST, adopt package UTC, or record both (e.g. collected_at_utc + collected_at_ist)?
Who may grant CONDITIONAL_GO and set ACCEPTED_RISK/DEFERRED — owner only? Must every ACCEPTED_RISK also be logged in DECISIONS.md, and what happens at expiry (auto-reopen)?
Independent review for P0/P1 closure: who is 'independent' in a one-owner + one-agent operation — the external AI auditors (ChatGPT/Perplexity), Dr. Deepu John for clinical, or the owner himself?
Script ecosystem: port archive/validate scripts to Node .mjs to match the v1 toolchain, or accept a Python runtime dependency in CI?
Does the issue register (agency_issue.schema.json + 03_findings/) replace QUESTIONS.md and parts of DIRECTIVES.md, or run alongside with a defined boundary?

R3 gap: extend REPORT_AND_TOOL_RUN_MANIFEST.csv with 'what to monitor / what to reject (+reason) / what to implement' and free-text notes columns, or keep those in a companion report-decision register?

Schema ownership: the schemas carry example.org $id placeholders and additionalProperties:false — who hosts/renames them, and is editing them to admit v1 fields (gate registry IDs, site class, IST timestamps) authorized?
Severity vocabulary: adopt P0–P3 fleet-wide, and how does it map to existing gate-failure semantics (merge-blocking vs advisory)?

Phase mapping for R8: which of phases 0–8 house each v1 front gate (brief, fat strategy, design_source MODE A/B, golden_page, full build) and the beauty/go-science/design-review checkpoints, so gate continuity is explicit rather than implied?
Where do the beauty-audit, go-science-audit and design-review evidence folders land in the 00–10 taxonomy — 03_findings, 06_qa, or a preserved launches/<domain>/design-review path?

readings.summary: Master OS file (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kairalimacmini-Claude/d81b3f6b-c18e-4430-a22c-d47fbdad6a32/scratchpad/os2026/Digital_Growth_Agency_OS_2026/01_MASTER_OS/MASTER_AGENCY_OPERATING_SYSTEM_COMPLETE_2026.md, v2.0, issued 2026-07-19) is a 7-document concatenation: (1) Master OS core (purpose, 7 governing outcomes, 10 non-negotiable rules, 4x4 workflow selector, 9-phase gated lifecycle 0-8 with stop conditions, 6-level evidence hierarchy, 6 benchmark classes, competitive doctrine with 7-way decision, opportunity economics formulas, 10-condition definition of done); (2) Capability map (18 specialist workstreams + AI role limits); (3) Competitive Intelligence Playbook (10-step lifecycle, 12 deep-dive modules with prohibited-shortcut columns, 9-list roster taxonomy, defend/match/flank/attack/create/partner/ignore strategy, 13-field opportunity scorecard, 4-tier monitoring cadence, ethical red lines); (4) Metrics/Tools/Benchmarks Dictionary (7 mandatory report questions, target-setting protocol, 63-row core metric register COM/SEO/AI/TEC/UX/CRO/B2B/LOC/INT/SEC/OPS — numerically coincident with but distinct from v1's 63-gate registry — 19-stage tool stack, 13-row benchmark register BMK-001..013, gap formulas, diagnostic rule chain); (5) Evidence/Storage/QA/AI-Agent Standard (RAW/PROCESSED/PUBLISHED layers, clients/{client_id}/projects/{project_id}/00-10 storage tree, artifact manifest with SHA-256, 11-item issue evidence bundle, 10-state proof-of-completion machine OPEN→CLOSED, 13 automated release checks, AI-agent operating contract with 11 required inputs, 10 agent evidence labels, 9 prohibited autonomous actions, 6-status exclusion/decision register, 10-item not-proof list); (6) International/Localization manual; (7) Monitoring manual (5 layers, 6-row cadence table, P0/P1 alert catalogs, 9-way regression comparison, 24h/72h/7d/28d stabilization, 10-step improvement loop, experiment governance, executive scorecard) + Research/Evidence Library (5 evidence classes, 60-source register G/W/O/S/SF/SE/DF/SW/GT/PW/GH/BM/UB/CXL/YT/A/R). Core merge tension: the package uses a gated-permission model for agent production actions ("must not ... without the required approval gate") where v1 HARD GATES are absolute bans; and its evidence storage tree + off-repo object storage conflicts with v1 launches/<domain>/ Evidence Law. Beauty gate, GO-science, design external AI review, and golden_page have NO counterpart in this file and must be inserted into Phase 3/5 per R8. No prompt-injection content found.

structures.name: Phase-gated lifecycle (0-8)
structures.detail: 9 phases, each with question/mandatory-output/stop-condition: 0 Classify and charter (stop: ambiguous scope, no accountable owner, no legal authority); 1 Baseline and discovery (stop: missing commercial truth, incomplete URL discovery, unrecorded data gaps); 2 Diagnose and prioritize (stop: recommendations without evidence/impact/acceptance criteria); 3 Strategy and specification (stop: design without page purpose, measurement or protected elements); 4 Build and controlled implementation (stop: untraceable changes or production edits without rollback); 5 Pre-launch QA and rehearsal (stop: open P0; unaccepted P1; failed conversion/tracking/redirect/security/rollback test); 6 Launch command centre (stop: guardrail breach or inability to roll back); 7 Stabilize and verify (stop: unexplained material regression; outputs 24h/72h/7d/28d comparison); 8 Monitor and improve (stop: no owner, no evidence, no closed-loop learning)

structures.name: 10 non-negotiable operating rules
structures.detail: All 'Never' rules: (1) never begin with design — begin with business economics, market definition, evidence access, protected baseline; (2) never remove/merge/rename a URL until traffic, queries, conversions, revenue, links, internal links, ads, emails, offline references, historical purpose checked; (3) never replace a proven landing page without control/recoverable copy+baseline; (4) never optimize a third-party score against first-party revenue/user evidence; (5) never call work complete on code-written/ticket-done — requires deployment, live retest, stored evidence; (6) never use competitor copying as strategy; (7) never use Reddit/YouTube/vendor benchmark as ONLY evidence for high-impact decision; (8) never let an AI agent autonomously publish, migrate, redirect, delete, disavow, change tracking, alter checkout or modify legal/medical claims WITHOUT THE REQUIRED APPROVAL GATE (note: gated, not absolute); (9) never overwrite raw baseline files — immutable dated copies and hashes; (10) never launch with unresolved P0; P1 exceptions require named accountable acceptance and expiry date

structures.name: Benchmark class taxonomy
structures.detail: Six classes: HARD (standards/zero-defect, e.g. HTTPS, no P0 broken conversion, WCAG target, CWV thresholds); OWN (trailing 12-16 month seasonal baseline, cohort, device/region distribution); PEER (named competitor median, upper quartile, leader — same market/device/intent); INDUSTRY (large-sample published benchmark with year/sample/definition); ECONOMIC (minimum required by margin, CAC, sales capacity, payback); EXPERIMENTAL (minimum detectable effect + decision rule). Target valid ONLY when recorded: metric definition, source, segment, baseline period, benchmark date, confidence, owner. NOTE: the benchmark register (§5 of dictionary) additionally uses classes PLATFORM (BMK-012) and ACADEMIC (BMK-013) not declared in the six-class taxonomy — internal inconsistency

structures.name: Evidence hierarchy (6 levels)
structures.detail: 1 Commercial truth (finance, backend orders, contribution margin, CRM, qualified calls, refunds, returns, repeat purchase); 2 First-party platform evidence (GSC, GA4, GTM, Google Ads, Merchant Center, Business Profile, server logs, Shopify Analytics, form/payment/email logs); 3 Controlled tests (usability, experiments, QA, Playwright, accessibility, security); 4 Diagnostic platforms (Screaming Frog, Semrush, DataForSEO, Ahrefs, Similarweb, PageSpeed, CrUX, GTmetrix, WebPageTest, Clarity/Hotjar); 5 External benchmarks/estimates; 6 Anecdotal discovery evidence (Reddit/forums/YouTube — generate questions and failure-mode checks, never prove a universal rule)

structures.name: Proof-of-completion state machine
structures.detail: OPEN -> EVIDENCED -> APPROVED -> IMPLEMENTING -> STAGING_QA -> READY_FOR_RELEASE -> DEPLOYED -> LIVE_VERIFIED -> MONITORED -> CLOSED. May not skip IMPLEMENTING->CLOSED. Failed live test returns to IMPLEMENTING or triggers rollback. P0/P1 closure requires independent review

structures.name: Definition of done (10 conditions)
structures.detail: (1) requirement+acceptance criteria exist; (2) implementation linked to issue/change ID; (3) code/content/config committed or versioned; (4) automated and manual checks pass; (5) deployed to intended environment; (6) live output retested; (7) evidence archived with tool/version/configuration, timestamp, hash; (8) KPI monitored for specified period; (9) no unexplained regression; (10) reviewer approves OR named owner accepts residual risk

structures.name: Exclusion and decision register statuses
structures.detail: Six statuses: INCLUDED_NOW (applicable and scheduled); DEFERRED (delayed, with risk and reconsideration date); NOT_APPLICABLE (reason tied to business model/technology/market/absent feature); REJECTED (evidence or economics do not support); UNKNOWN (evidence/access missing; owner and next step required); ACCEPTED_RISK (accountable owner accepts consequence until expiry). Each record: source, rationale, risk, owner, approval, expiry, reconsideration trigger. Purpose: prevent re-proposing evaluated ideas while allowing reopening — directly serves R2

structures.name: Agent evidence labels (10)
structures.detail: OBSERVED_FIRST_PARTY, OBSERVED_LIVE_TEST, CALCULATED, THIRD_PARTY_ESTIMATE, USER_PROVIDED, EXTERNAL_BENCHMARK, ANECDOTAL_SIGNAL, ASSUMPTION, RECOMMENDATION, UNKNOWN — every agent statement must carry one internally

structures.name: Prohibited autonomous agent actions (9)
structures.detail: Without the specified human gate, an agent must not: publish or delete production content; change domains, DNS, robots, canonicals, hreflang or redirects; submit disavow files; change analytics definitions, consent or payment logic; install/uninstall Shopify apps or alter checkout; make regulated medical/legal/financial claims; send competitor outreach, reviews or public communications; expose secrets or customer data; approve its own P0/P1 evidence. Plus: threat-model agentic systems for prompt injection, tool misuse, insecure memory/context, excessive autonomy per OWASP Agentic Top 10 2026 [O02]

structures.name: AI-agent operating contract (11 required inputs)
structures.detail: Agent must receive: workflow ID and phase; client/project/release IDs; exact domain/market/language/device/date scope; authorized tools and credential boundaries; input artifact IDs and freshness requirements; required output schema; evidence and citation requirements; prohibited actions; approval gate and escalation owner; retry/timeout/cost limits; definition of done

structures.name: Evidence storage tree
structures.detail: clients/{client_id}/projects/{project_id}/ with 00_governance, 01_raw/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/{source}/{report_type}/{run_id}/, 02_processed/{dataset}/{version}/, 03_findings/{issue_id}/, 04_specifications/, 05_implementation/{release_id}/, 06_qa/{release_id}/{environment}/, 07_launch/{release_id}/, 08_monitoring/{cadence}/{period}/, 09_published_reports/{version}/, 10_archive/. Three layers: RAW (immutable, never edited — corrections create new run ID), PROCESSED (references raw inputs), PUBLISHED (references processed + raw IDs). Storage may be object storage, Google Drive AND/OR Git repo depending on artifact type — large binaries off-repo, code/schemas/manifests/small text in version control

structures.name: Artifact manifest fields
structures.detail: artifact ID + run ID; client/project/release/issue IDs; source/tool + version; exact configuration/API endpoint/query/crawl settings; domain/property/environment/URL scope; market, country, location, language, currency, device, user agent; date range, comparison range, timezone, collection timestamp; operator or agent identity + model/version; raw file names, MIME types, sizes, SHA-256 hashes; known exclusions/sampling/failures/data gaps; upstream input IDs + downstream issue/report IDs; review and approval status. Modeled on W3C PROV [W03]

structures.name: Issue evidence bundle (11 items)
structures.detail: 1 issue record+severity; 2 raw evidence or artifact-ID pointers; 3 affected URL/entity export; 4 business consequence+confidence; 5 recommendation+acceptance criteria; 6 implementation link (commit/PR/CMS revision/tag/config/vendor ticket); 7 staging test evidence; 8 live deployment evidence; 9 post-deployment retest; 10 KPI monitoring result; 11 final reviewer decision or accepted risk

structures.name: Automated release checks (13)
structures.detail: build/unit/integration tests; Playwright critical journeys+traces; visual snapshot comparison [PW01]; redirect-map tests + no-loop checks; internal broken-link scan; robots/noindex/canonical/hreflang/schema tests; analytics event + ecommerce payload tests; axe-core scan + manual critical-journey checks; Lighthouse CI/performance budgets; security/dependency scans; sitemap validation; market/language/currency/inventory tests; backup and rollback verification. Protected release branch + required reviews/checks; build provenance/artifact attestations [GH01-GH02]

structures.name: What must not count as proof (10)
structures.detail: task status without live retest; screenshot without URL/timestamp/environment/expected result; AI summary without raw exports; tool health score without issue-level evidence; PDF without machine-readable data/config; code committed but not deployed; deployment without conversion/indexation verification; improved rankings without qualified conversion/revenue analysis; benchmark without source/date/segment/definition; 'not applicable' without rationale

structures.name: Competitive strategy decision set
structures.detail: Decision must be one of: defend, match a mandatory parity factor, flank an underserved segment, attack a vulnerable demand pool, create a category, partner, deliberately ignore. Playbook §5 details 5.1 Defend / 5.2 Match mandatory parity / 5.3 Flank / 5.4 Attack / 5.5 Create category or moat / 5.6 Ignore deliberately (with reconsideration trigger) — 'partner' named in the decision lists but has no §5 subsection

structures.name: Competitive intelligence lifecycle (10 steps)
structures.detail: 1 define exact market and denominator; 2 build multi-channel competitor universe; 3 capture evidence same period/market/language/device; 4 separate facts, estimates, calculations, assumptions; 5 diagnose parity gaps, weaknesses, defendable advantages; 6 quantify opportunity and cost; 7 select defend/match/flank/attack/create/partner/ignore; 8 build page/product/channel changes + acceptance criteria; 9 test or launch with commercial guardrails; 10 monitor competitor reactions, market share, profitability

structures.name: Competitor roster taxonomy (9 lists) + 12 deep-dive modules
structures.detail: Per-market lists: commercial, substitutes, organic-search, paid, marketplaces/retailers/aggregators, publishers/forums/YouTube/creators, AI-recommended businesses, local/map, aspirational references. Roster records competitor TYPE and market, never one undifferentiated list. 12 modules (Market definition/denominator; Competitor universe; Demand and share of search; Organic and SERP ownership; AI-answer visibility; Content and topical advantage; Backlinks PR reputation; Offer product pricing; Paid media and creative; UX CRO performance; Local regional localization; Retention and lifecycle) each with Metrics/Tools/Exact capture/Target logic/'Do not' prohibited-shortcut columns (e.g. no DA/DR chasing, no fake reviews, no copying competitor word count, no redesign because competitor looks newer, no llms.txt reliance for Google)

structures.name: Opportunity economics formulas
structures.detail: Expected incremental contribution = addressable demand x attainable share x qualified conversion rate x contribution value x confidence - incremental cost. Priority score = incremental contribution x strategic importance x confidence x reach / (effort x time-to-value x risk). Every input labeled observed/calculated/estimated/assumed; sensitivity range mandatory for high-value bets

structures.name: Opportunity scorecard (13 fields)
structures.detail: market/region/language/location; customer segment + job-to-be-done; demand size + source; current own share + competitor shares; attainable share range; conversion and contribution assumptions; capacity constraint; time to value; confidence class; legal/brand/platform risk; required pages/products/content/links/ads/localization/operations; expected incremental contribution downside/base/upside; owner + next evidence required

structures.name: Seven mandatory report questions + target-setting protocol
structures.detail: Every report/issue answers: metric+exact formula; mandatory dimensions (region/domain/language/page-template/device/source/cohort/period); source of truth (third-party estimate cannot overrule finance/CRM/GSC/server); benchmark class; gap (absolute+percentage, confidence, comparability); diagnosis before recommendation; exact improvement + acceptance test + monitoring period. Protocol: hard threshold only from authoritative standard; client seasonal/cohort baseline default; peer percentiles from named set with identical definitions; industry benchmarks context-only with sample/year/sector/definition; commercial targets from contribution economics; experiments with MDE+guardrails; record 'not comparable' rather than force a misleading benchmark

structures.name: Diagnostic rule chain
structures.detail: A metric crossing a threshold creates an investigation, not an automatic solution. Issue record connects: observation -> affected segment -> corroborating evidence -> likely mechanism -> proposed intervention -> acceptance test -> commercial guardrail. Row-level definitions live in 07_TEMPLATES/METRIC_DICTIONARY.csv (companion file)

structures.name: Gap calculation
structures.detail: Higher-is-better: Gap = target - current; Relative gap = (target - current)/target. Lower-is-better: Gap = current - target. Competitor percentiles must store competitor set, values, median, upper quartile, leader, collection date, market, method; never compare values from different tools without normalization

structures.name: Capability map (18 workstreams) + AI role
structures.source: Agency Capability and Specialist Workstream Map section
structures.detail: 18 capabilities each with core outputs and when-specialist-mandatory triggers: Business/market strategy; Competitive intelligence; Technical SEO; Content strategy/editorial; Digital PR/link/reputation; UX research/service design; UI/design system; CRO/experimentation; Analytics/data engineering; Development/architecture; QA/DevOps/SRE (mandatory for migrations); Accessibility; Security/privacy/legal; Localization/transcreation (every new language/market); Local SEO/reputation; Merchant/feed/marketplace; CRM/lifecycle/sales ops; Clinical/legal subject expert (health/medical/legal/finance sign-off). AI role: accelerates research/extraction/comparison/issue drafting/code gen/test gen/report assembly; does NOT replace accountable domain experts, user research participants, legal/clinical approval, security testing, or independent release authorization; every AI output retains sources, evidence labels, uncertainty

structures.name: Monitoring architecture + cadence + alerts
structures.detail: 5 layers: availability/revenue protection; search eligibility/migration protection; experience/conversion; commercial quality; competitive position. 6 cadences: real-time/hourly (ops); daily during launch (launch command centre, daily launch log); weekly for 8-12 weeks (stabilization scorecard); monthly (operating review); quarterly (growth plan, steering group); annual/pre-rebuild (approved roadmap or rebuild charter). Alert record fields: metric, scope, baseline method, threshold, minimum duration, owner, notification channel, diagnostic runbook, rollback authority. Default P0 alerts (7): production unavailable/critical conversion fails twice independently; payment/form/booking zero or backend delivery fails; homepage/major template noindex/blocked/canonical elsewhere; widespread 5xx or DNS/SSL failure; material revenue/lead collapse beyond guardrail; critical security finding/data exposure; wrong-market pricing/claims/availability with material impact. P1 examples (7): priority-page indexation loss/redirect failure; unexplained GSC decline; CWV priority template poor; Merchant disapproval spike; checkout/form abandonment or error rise; review sentiment/local visibility deterioration; competitor captures strategic demand cluster

structures.name: Regression comparison + stabilization windows
structures.detail: Compare: last vs previous run; post-release vs pre-release baseline; current vs seasonally comparable period; actual vs target/guardrail; own vs named peers identical methodology; mobile vs desktop; each market/language/domain/location; each page template + traffic source; new vs returning + cohorts. Stabilization checkpoints: 24h/72h/7d/28d. Regression report lists added/removed/changed URLs; status/canonical/directive/title/H1/schema/internal-link diffs; performance changes; conversion changes; unexplained gaps

structures.name: Continuous improvement loop (10 steps) + experiment governance + executive scorecard
structures.detail: Loop: observe -> validate data+segment -> diagnose mechanism (multiple sources) -> quantify impact+confidence -> prioritize with opportunity score -> define hypothesis/change/primary metric/guardrails/acceptance -> implement controlled change -> QA tracking+UX before interpreting -> adopt/iterate/revert/reject -> store learning, update decision/exclusion register, refine standard. Experiments: stable assignment, exposure logging, sample-size/power method, pre-defined primary metric, guardrails, stopping rule, data-quality check; no peeking/cherry-picking; label quasi-experimental designs. Executive scorecard: max 10-15 decision metrics (revenue/contribution or pipeline; RPS; conversion+quality; CAC/payback/LTV; organic/paid/AI/local visibility; indexation/technical health; CWV pass rate; customer/review/return/service health; market-share proxy; open P0/P1+accepted risks; strategic attack progress)

structures.name: International/localization structures
structures.detail: Market matrix: one row per country/region x language x currency x legal entity x fulfilment model x location, 12 recorded fields incl. domain/canonical policy, hreflang relationship, translation owner/glossary/reviewer, fallback experience. Localization workflow 9 steps (source content approved -> glossary/prohibited claims -> translate with context -> localize keyword demand (never translate keyword lists) -> adapt proof/imagery/offers/payment/legal -> linguistic/functional/SEO/accessibility/visual QA -> validate URLs/canonicals/hreflang/selectors/analytics -> market owner + legal/clinical approval -> monitor wrong-market landings). Technical: stable crawlable locale URLs, self-canonical, reciprocal hreflang + optional x-default, no opaque forced IP redirect, local sitemaps/GSC properties. Local workflow: GBP/NAP/categories/hours/booking/photos/reviews/local page/schema/rank grid; no doorway pages or fake locations. 10 commonly missed edge controls (deep links bypassing market selectors; currency display vs charge mismatch; untranslated validation/error/email messages; structured-data/feed inconsistency; legal/medical claims copied across jurisdictions; phone consent; hreflang to redirects/noindex; non-crawlable locale selector; sold-out products advertised; non-lawful testimonials per market)

structures.name: Ethical and legal red lines
structures.detail: Prohibited: unauthorized access, personal-data collection, evasion of technical restrictions, negative SEO, fake reviews, impersonation, trademark misuse, content theft, price coordination, fabricated comparisons, undisclosed sponsored advocacy. Only public/licensed/client-owned/consented evidence. Legal review mandatory for comparative claims, regulated categories, sensitive data

structures.name: Historical report policy
structures.detail: PDF per report where supported + corresponding CSV/JSON/API response + settings (PDF alone insufficient); never overwrite monthly/pre-launch reports (new timestamp/version); checksum manifest after collection; baseline + critical-page full-page screenshots; dashboards export underlying data + definition/query; record tool plan/licence limits; retain pre-migration evidence + redirect maps at least the useful life of the migration + legal requirement. Directly serves R3 report store

structures.name: Workflow selector matrix
structures.detail: 4 business models (B2C, B2B, D2C, Shopify) x 4 asset situations (New asset, Existing asset=upgrade/migration, Organic programme, Landing page). Package's classification axis — differs from v1's three site classes (commerce/organic/landing)

structures.name: Research/Evidence Library + 5 evidence classes
structures.source: Research and Evidence Library section (end of file)
structures.detail: Snapshot 2026-07-19. Classes: 1 primary standards/first-party platform docs (highest authority); 2 large-sample independent research (context only); 3 academic (preprints labelled); 4 vendor docs/datasets (authoritative for tool only); 5 Reddit/forums/YouTube/expert opinion (failure-mode discovery only, never alone sets a target). Future research admitted ONLY through Source Register + change-control. 60 sources: G01-G22 (Google incl. G12 CWV thresholds, G14 AI optimization, G15 generative AI reports), W01-W04 (W3C WCAG 2.2/PROV/JSON Schema 2020-12), O01-O02 (OWASP Top 10 2025 + Agentic 2026), S01-S05 (Shopify), SF01-SF03 (Screaming Frog), SE01-SE02 (Semrush), DF01-DF02 (DataForSEO), SW01, GT01, PW01 (Playwright visual), GH01-GH02 (GitHub attestations/protected branches), BM01-BM03 (Baymard), UB01 (Unbounce 6.6% median), CXL01, YT01-YT04, A01-A03 (academic preprints), R01-R03 (Reddit anecdotal)

structures.name: Governing outcomes (7)
structures.detail: Every project protects/improves: 1 qualified market visibility (conventional search, generative search, local, shopping, marketplaces, paid, referrals); 2 revenue, contribution margin, qualified pipeline, LTV; 3 URL, content, ranking, link, review, tracking, audience equity; 4 user task success, accessibility, trust, brand positioning; 5 technical reliability, security, privacy, recoverability; 6 regional, language, currency, inventory, fulfilment, legal correctness; 7 measurement integrity + proof work was completed

registers.name: Core metric controls register
registers.columns: ID | Metric | Formula/definition | Source | Target/benchmark | If weak
registers.purpose: 63 rows (numerically coincident with v1's 63-gate registry but a DIFFERENT register): COM-001..010 (revenue, contribution margin, RPS, qualified lead rate, lead-to-win, CAC, LTV, actual market share, share of search, digital traffic share); SEO-001..014 (GSC clicks/impressions/CTR, weighted SOV, top-3/10 coverage, indexable URL count, priority indexation rate, canonical agreement rate, sitemap hygiene, crawl waste, internal link coverage, content decay, referring domain gap, broken backlink value); AI-001..004 (generative impressions, prompt mention share, citation share, AI factual accuracy — 100% material facts); TEC-001..010 (status errors, redirect chains, rendering parity, LCP/INP/CLS/TTFB P75, page weight, third-party script cost, uptime/transaction success); UX-001..005 (task success, time on task, critical errors, onsite search success, WCAG 2.2 AA conformance); CRO-001..008 (primary CVR, landing CVR, CTA CTR, form completion, add-to-cart, checkout completion, cart abandonment, return/refund); B2B-001..003 (MQL-to-SQL, pipeline sourced/influenced, lead response time); LOC-001..002 (local pack visibility share, review health); INT-001..003 (hreflang validity, wrong-market session rate, translation QA defect rate); SEC-001..002 (critical vulnerability count 0-at-release, backup restore success 100%); OPS-001..002 (evidence completeness 100% P0/P1, change failure rate). Full row-level detail in companion 07_TEMPLATES/METRIC_DICTIONARY.csv

registers.name: Benchmark register
registers.columns: ID | Metric | Rule/value | Applicability | Class | Caveat
registers.purpose: 13 rows BMK-001..013: BMK-001 LCP P75 good<=2.5s/NI 2.5-4s/poor>4s (HARD); BMK-002 INP P75 <=200ms/200-500/>500 (HARD); BMK-003 CLS P75 <=0.1/0.1-0.25/>0.25 (HARD); BMK-004 WCAG 2.2 AA unless stricter law/contract (HARD); BMK-005 0 open confirmed critical vulnerabilities at release (HARD); BMK-006 100% critical conversion path pass, 0 unowned P0 (HARD); BMK-007 sitemap hygiene 100% canonical indexable 200s (HARD); BMK-008 redirect one hop, no loops, closest intent (HARD); BMK-009 6.6% median CVR Q4 2024 Unbounce context-only (INDUSTRY); BMK-010 ~70% cart abandonment context-only (INDUSTRY); BMK-011 62% mobile product pages mediocre-or-worse Baymard 2026 (INDUSTRY); BMK-012 GSC generative reports subset availability — mark not-available rather than fabricate (PLATFORM); BMK-013 ~15% Wikipedia AIO traffic-decline preprint — do not generalize (ACADEMIC). Note PLATFORM/ACADEMIC classes exceed the declared six-class taxonomy

registers.name: Tool stack by stage
registers.columns: Stage | Primary | Secondary | Mandatory reports | Decision | Limit
registers.purpose: 19 stages mapping tools to lifecycle stages (serves R7): Commercial truth (CRM+finance); Google organic (GSC); Analytics/tags (GA4+GTM); Technical crawling (Screaming Frog); Automated SEO data (DataForSEO APIs — 'agent-agnostic data acquisition at scale'); SEO/competitor suite (Semrush, secondary Ahrefs+Similarweb); Market intelligence (Similarweb); Performance field (CrUX/PSI+RUM); Performance diagnosis (WebPageTest/GTmetrix); Behaviour/UX (Microsoft Clarity); Usability research; Accessibility (axe-core+manual); Visual/functional QA (Playwright); Security (OWASP ZAP+dependency scanner); Commerce feeds (Merchant Center+Shopify); Local (GBP+rank tool); Paid competitor creative (ad transparency libraries); Evidence/versioning (GitHub+immutable object storage e.g. S3 Object Lock/Drive Vault). Every row carries an explicit Limit caveat

registers.name: Source register
registers.columns: ID | Publisher | Class | Title | Use
registers.purpose: 60 curated sources with evidence classes; future research admitted only via this register + change control (serves R1/R5 partially)

registers.name: Exclusion and decision register
registers.columns: status (INCLUDED_NOW|DEFERRED|NOT_APPLICABLE|REJECTED|UNKNOWN|ACCEPTED_RISK) + source, rationale, risk, owner, approval, expiry, reconsideration trigger
registers.purpose: Every suggested control/finding/opportunity gets exactly one status; prevents re-litigating evaluated ideas; reopenable when assumptions change — package's decision-provenance mechanism (R2)

registers.name: Artifact manifest
registers.columns: artifact ID, run ID, client/project/release/issue IDs, source/tool+version, exact config/query/crawl settings, domain/property/environment/URL scope, market/country/location/language/currency/device/user-agent, date range/comparison range/timezone/collection timestamp, operator-or-agent identity + model/version, raw file names/MIME/sizes/SHA-256, exclusions/sampling/failures/gaps, upstream input IDs + downstream issue/report IDs, review/approval status
registers.purpose: Mandatory per report run or evidence bundle; W3C PROV-based reproducibility (extends v1 Evidence Law with hashes and provenance chains; serves R2/R3)

STOP: ambiguous scope, no accountable owner, no legal authority
Output: commercial, URL, sitemap, content, ranking, backlink, UX, tracking, technical and competitor baselines

conflicts: GATED-AUTONOMY vs ABSOLUTE BANS: package rule 8 and Evidence Standard §9 frame agent production actions (publish, migrate, redirect, delete, change tracking, DNS/robots/canonicals) as permitted WITH 'the required approval gate'; v1 HARD GATES ban several of these for the agent absolutely (no production writes, no deletions, no DNS/robots changes — humans perform them). Adopting package wording verbatim would weaken HARD GATES; v1 absolutes must be declared supreme in the merged text.

EVIDENCE LOCATION: package §3 allows evidence in 'approved object storage, Google Drive and/or a Git repository' with large binaries off-repo; v1 EVIDENCE LAW says evidence is committed to git in launches/<domain>/ — 'if it isn't in the repo, it didn't happen'. Off-repo storage without an in-repo manifest+hash rule would violate v1 doctrine.

STORAGE ROOT: package mandates clients/{client_id}/projects/{project_id}/00-10 tree; v1 uses launches/<domain>/ (+ content-mined/, docs/reports/). Wholesale adoption would break existing CI, evidence law paths and append-only history.

ACCEPTED_RISK / P1-exception-with-expiry (rules §3.10, DoD condition 10, register status): creates a formal mechanism for shipping with a known deficiency. If applicable to registry gates or HARD GATES it directly violates v1 rule 'gates are added, never weakened; removal needs owner ruling in DECISIONS.md'. Must be constrained to non-gate findings or routed through DECISIONS.md owner rulings.

PHASE 5 QA OMITS v1 GATES: the package launch-certificate checklist contains no beauty-conformance, GO-science, dual external-AI design review, golden-page conformance or 63-gate registry execution. Treating the package's Phase 5 list as the complete launch gate set would silently drop R8-protected gates.

ASSUMPTION LABEL vs NEVER-INVENT: package permits agent outputs carrying ASSUMPTION/THIRD_PARTY_ESTIMATE labels; v1 HARD GATE f says gaps in facts/IDs/prices are ASKED, not filled (R4 reinforces). A labelled assumption must not be an accepted substitute for asking the owner on factual/commercial gaps.

CLASSIFICATION SCHEME: package workflow selector (B2C/B2B/D2C/Shopify x asset type) vs v1 registry's lint-enforced commerce/organic/landing site classes — unreconciled dual taxonomy would break registry lint or produce ambiguous gate applicability.

readings.summary: Six B2B workflow files (all Version 1.0, Issued 2026-07-19; absolute base path /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kairalimacmini-Claude/d81b3f6b-c18e-4430-a22c-d47fbdad6a32/scratchpad/os2026/Digital_Growth_Agency_OS_2026/05_WORKFLOWS/02_B2B/). Workflow IDs: B2B-NEW_WEBSITE (01), B2B-EXISTING_WEBSITE (02), B2B-NEW_ORGANIC (03), B2B-EXISTING_ORGANIC (04), B2B-NEW_LANDING (05), B2B-EXISTING_LANDING (06). All six share: an identical Phase 0-8 lifecycle with Gate 0-5 evidence lines + stabilisation exit; identical commercial objective/audiences/conversions (qualified pipeline, multi-person buying); 7 inherited shared standards (00_MASTER_OPERATING_SYSTEM through 06_2026_STANDARDS); identical mandatory tool list (15 items), 13-item B2B KPI scorecard, 9-role sign-off table, 7 stop-launch conditions, 9 AI-agent execution rules; and an identical V2 overlay (phase control/proof matrix, 12-field finding format, competitor/market-share requirements, SHA-256 evidence rules, B2B competitive-edge controls, 9-metric required panel COM-004/COM-005/B2B-001..003/SEO-004/AI-002/CRO-001/UX-001, TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv runs, 6-item do-not-do register). NEW variants (01/03/05) use Phase 1 'Research and launch baseline' (document assumptions, no invented history); EXISTING variants (02/04/06) use Phase 1 'Discovery and protected baseline' (frozen raw exports, master URL inventory, 6-way URL classification protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire, preservation register, old-vs-new comparison, regression vs protected baseline, redirect/change map + rollback triggers). Track deltas: website (template inventory, all-states, every-template QA), organic (12-month roadmap, cannibalisation resolution, editorial standard, decay/cannibalisation monthly reports), landing (message-match chain, control/variant + sample-size before traffic, indexability class SEO-indexable/paid-only-noindex/evergreen/temporary/test-variant, paid-social mobile speed, daily spend monitoring, experiment learning register). Core merge tension: the package's phase gates are compatible with v1 but its design track omits beauty gate, go-science gate, golden-page, dual-AI design review, and clinical sign-off (must be re-inserted per R8); its 9-role human team and instructions like 'complete a real conversion', 'submit GSC sitemaps', and AI rule 9 (agent amends shared standards) need re-routing to respect HARD GATES 1/3/7/9 and owner-only doctrine changes.
