structures.name: Benchmark classes
structures.source: all six files, overlay 'Required metric panel' + 'Competitor and market-share requirements'
structures.detail: Target methods use OWN (own baseline/cohort/seasonal) vs PEER (median → upper quartile → leader values, identical market/device/language/period) vs external benchmark (only when definition/segment comparable — do-not-do item 3). Third-party estimates must be marked as estimates (Phase 1, NEW variants). Peer percentiles are Phase 2 overlay evidence.

structures.name: Competitor set taxonomy (9 types) + opportunity classifications (7)
structures.source: all six files, overlay 'Competitor and market-share requirements'
structures.detail: Competitor sets built separately: direct, SERP, paid, marketplace, local, publisher, substitute, AI-answer, aspirational. Opportunity classes: defend, mandatory parity, flank, attack, category-creation, partner, deliberate-ignore. Cadence: priority competitor panel monthly, complete market map quarterly. Archive competitor pages/ads/offers/reviews/SERPs with date+region+source; never infer spend/performance from an ad library.

structures.name: 12-field exact finding format
structures.source: all six files, overlay 'Exact finding format'
structures.detail: 1 issue ID+phase+severity; 2 exact metric/formula+dimensions; 3 current value+period+source of truth; 4 own baseline+peer values/percentiles+external benchmark; 5 absolute/relative gap+confidence; 6 affected URLs/products/locations/campaigns/cohorts; 7 likely mechanism with corroborating evidence; 8 exact recommendation+owner+dependency; 9 acceptance criteria+automated/manual test; 10 business guardrail+monitoring window+rollback condition; 11 what must not be done; 12 excluded alternatives and why.

structures.name: B2B required metric panel (9 rows, identical)
structures.source: all six files, overlay 'Required metric panel'
structures.detail: Columns: ID | Metric | Source | Target method | Red flag | Improvement path. Rows: COM-004 Qualified lead rate (CRM); COM-005 Lead-to-win rate (CRM); B2B-001 MQL-to-SQL rate (CRM); B2B-002 Pipeline sourced/influenced (CRM, model clearly labelled); B2B-003 Lead response time (CRM/call system, SLA by lead value/urgency); SEO-004 Weighted organic SOV (Semrush/STAT/AccuRanker, PEER median then upper quartile); AI-002 Prompt mention share (controlled prompt panel, PEER same prompt/model, confidence intervals); CRO-001 Primary conversion rate (backend/CRM+analytics, OWN seasonal+industry+experiment); UX-001 Task success rate (usability test, per critical task).

structures.name: Stop-launch conditions (7, identical)
structures.source: all six files, 'Do not launch or close the release if'
structures.detail: 1 primary conversion/CRM-order/payment path fails; 2 production indexability/canonicals/sitemap/priority redirects wrong; 3 analytics cannot measure primary outcome or duplicates material events; 4 target market gets wrong language/currency/availability/price/shipping/contact route; 5 critical security/privacy/accessibility/legal issue remains; 6 protected high-value content/links/URLs/proof removed without approved evidence; 7 rollback, owners or command-centre coverage unavailable for a material release.

structures.name: AI-agent execution rules (9, identical)
structures.detail: 1 select correct workflow before acting; 2 never infer an existing URL/page has no value without checking all discovery+commercial sources; 3 label every finding (5-way classification); 4 attach evidence+affected URLs to every issue; 5 no issue closed without retest evidence; 6 escalate commercial-truth vs third-party-SEO-score conflicts, do not optimise for the score; 7 preserve immutable pre-change exports and screenshots; 8 stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval, do not silently bypass; 9 add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow rather than keeping them only in chat.

structures.name: Mandatory do-not-do register (6, identical)
structures.detail: 1 no redesign for visual novelty without measurable user/brand/search/commercial purpose; 2 no delete/redirect of an existing page without master URL and preservation checks; 3 no benchmark whose definition/segment is not comparable; 4 no copying competitor content/claims/creative/dark patterns; 5 no closing work before live evidence and monitoring; 6 no unexplained ignored recommendations (Decision/Exclusion Register).

structures.name: Phase control and proof matrix (overlay, identical)
structures.detail: Columns: Phase | Required work | Evidence | Do not proceed when. Key stop conditions per phase: P0 no owner/unclear market denominator/missing commercial source/unauthorized scope; P1 incomplete URL discovery, baseline overwritten, estimates presented as truth; P2 recommendation lacking metric/cause/economics/acceptance criteria/evidence; P3 design changes without purpose or protected-elements list; P4 production-only edits, untraceable app/plugin/config changes; P5 open P0, unaccepted P1, broken conversion/redirect/tracking/backup; P6 guardrail breach or unverifiable live commercial path; P7 unexplained material revenue/conversion/indexation/ranking loss; P8 vanity reporting, no owner, repeated recommendations with no learning. Phase 7 comparison windows: 24h/72h/7d/28d vs pre-release and seasonal baselines.

structures.name: Evidence rules (overlay, identical)
structures.source: all six files, overlay 'Evidence and completion requirements'
structures.detail: Archive raw PDF plus CSV/JSON/crawl/log and configuration; generate SHA-256 manifest; never overwrite baseline evidence; closed issue links to implementation reference + staging proof + live proof + monitored result; P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review.

structures.name: Roles and sign-off table (9 roles, identical)
structures.detail: Columns: Role | Minimum responsibility. Rows: Accountable business owner; Project/product owner; SEO/content; Design/UX/CRO; Development/DevOps; Analytics/data; CRM/sales/ecommerce operations; Market/legal/privacy owner; QA (independent test execution, evidence and retest). No clinical/medical reviewer role exists.

structures.name: KPI and guardrail scorecard (13 B2B KPIs, identical)
structures.detail: marketing-qualified accounts/leads; sales acceptance; meeting rate; pipeline value; opportunity velocity; win rate; revenue influenced; cost per opportunity/account; organic clicks/impressions + priority rankings; indexation and crawl health; Core Web Vitals by important template; technical error and redirect rate; accessibility/security/privacy closure. Segmentation: market, domain/subfolder, language, location, device, source/campaign, page/product/service type.

structures.name: Monitoring cadence (Phase 7, common)
structures.detail: Daily during stabilisation: uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives. Weekly for 8-12 weeks: GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, qualified lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links. Monthly: executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog. Quarterly: full technical/content/UX-CRO/accessibility/security/competitor/architecture review. Standing alerts: content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change. Deltas: 03/04 add monthly content-decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor-change reports; 05/06 add daily spend/sessions/conversion/qualified-outcome/revenue-margin/speed/errors while campaigns run.

structures.name: Stabilisation timings
structures.source: all six files, Phases 6-7 + overlay P7
structures.detail: Full production crawl within 24 hours vs final staging/production baseline; overlay windows 24h/72h/7d/28d; NEW variants (01/03/05): establish first stable 4-8 week operating baseline before normalising targets; EXISTING variants (02/04/06): compare vs recent AND seasonal baselines, investigate losses by page/segment. All: review sales acceptance/meeting quality/pipeline/opportunity velocity, not only form conversion. Stabilisation exit (verbatim, identical): critical paths stable, P0/P1 regressions closed or accepted, performance understood against the correct baseline.

structures.name: B2B trust controls + content controls (identical blocks in all six)
structures.detail: Trust (5): legal entity/leadership/team/market experience; case studies with context+method+outcomes; client/partner proof and references WITH PERMISSION; security/compliance/service-levels/procurement info; clear contact ownership and response process. Content (5): industry/vertical pages; role/persona pages; solution/use-case pages; capabilities and implementation/process pages; case studies/research/technical resources/comparison/procurement content. Note: these items also appear duplicated inline in the Phase 1 checklist of every file (apparent generation artifact).

structures.name: B2B competitive edge controls + attack patterns (overlay, identical)
structures.detail: Capture and test: ICP and account segmentation; buying committee roles; long sales cycle and assisted content; CRM attribution and response SLA; case-study/proof governance. Market-share attack patterns: own high-value problem/industry/use-case clusters; build comparison/alternative/integration pages with factual proof; improve MQL-to-SQL, account engagement and sales enablement.

structures.name: Delta: 01_NEW_WEBSITE specifics
structures.detail: Phase 1 B2B inserts: CRM/marketing-automation integration; lead scoring/routing/SLA; account/company enrichment where lawful; gated/ungated resource strategy; calendar/webinar/event/sales-enablement integration; validate demand/proposition before producing entire asset (prototypes/limited campaign tests where risk is high); document assumptions since no history exists. Phase 2: full page/template inventory + launch-critical vs phased; design components as reusable governed templates; map content/CTA by buying role and stage incl. sales handoff. Phase 3: build all priority templates with real content early; custom 404/search-zero/loading/error/success/unavailable states; integrate CRM campaign/member status + opportunity-source preservation. Phase 4: sample and test EVERY template, not only homepage; verify all nav/breadcrumb/footer/contextual-link destinations. Deliverable deltas: proposed business sitemap; proposed XML sitemap specification; content/template inventory.

structures.name: Delta: 02_EXISTING_WEBSITE specifics
structures.detail: Phase 1: freeze dated raw exports (GSC, GA4, GTM, CRM/backend, paid media, crawlers, backlinks, server logs, performance tools); pre-change KPI baselines + launch guardrail thresholds from comparable periods. Phase 2: preservation specification + change-impact register per protected asset; avoid simultaneous changes to URL+intent+content+layout+offer+tracking unless necessary and approved. Phase 3: maintain old-vs-new comparison; preserve existing production asset until new version passes. Phase 4: regression checks vs protected baseline; resolve every unexplained loss. Phase 5: release with redirect/change map, control metrics and rollback triggers active. Deliverable deltas: master URL inventory; current sitemap/architecture audit; preservation register; redirect/change map; proposed business sitemap; proposed XML sitemap spec; content/template inventory.

structures.name: Delta: 03_NEW_ORGANIC specifics
structures.detail: Phase 1 inserts: ICP and account-intent keyword mapping; industry/problem/solution architecture; thought leadership and expert entity building; digital PR/partner/association links; content-to-pipeline attribution; query-topic-page map by intent/funnel/market/language/location; benchmark direct/SERP/publisher/marketplace/local competitors; identify technical/content/authority/internal-link/reputation/SERP-feature gaps. Phase 2: 12-month technical/content/authority roadmap; ONE primary owning page per intent cluster, resolve cannibalisation before expansion; editorial standards (originality, experience, expertise, claims, sourcing, refresh cadence); digital PR/link-earning, local/partner/reputation and internal-link plans. Phase 3: fix technical/indexation constraints BEFORE scaling content; publish only after editorial+SEO+factual-claims+link+conversion QA; dashboards branded/non-branded, page type, topic, market, commercial outcome. Phase 4: validate every published template's indexability/rendered content/canonicals/schema/internal links; check differentiation vs actual competing results, reject thin/repetitive production. Phase 5: record publication and discovery dates. Phase 8: feed winning queries/objections/sales questions back. Deliverable deltas: keyword/topic/intent map; technical/content/authority roadmap; editorial and link-earning standard.

structures.name: Delta: 04_EXISTING_ORGANIC specifics
structures.detail: Exact union of 02's protected-baseline mechanics (frozen exports, master URL inventory, 6-way URL classification, preservation spec, old-vs-new, regression vs protected baseline, redirect/change map + rollback triggers) and 03's organic mechanics (keyword/topic map, 12-month roadmap, cannibalisation, editorial standard, decay/cannibalisation/lost-link monthly reports, publication/discovery dates). Deliverables = union: master URL inventory, current sitemap/architecture audit, preservation register, redirect/change map, keyword/topic/intent map, roadmap, editorial and link-earning standard.

structures.name: Delta: 05_NEW_LANDING specifics
structures.detail: Phase 1 inserts: one audience/problem/offer/next-step per page; align copy with campaign/account segment and sales stage; capture company/role/need/market without excessive friction; traffic-source and audience map (campaign, keyword/ad, creative, email/referrer, region, device, expected intent); page indexability class: SEO indexable | paid-only noindex | evergreen | temporary | controlled test variant; record offer economics/availability/qualification/fulfilment/sales-response capacity. Phase 2 ('Offer, message, page and experiment specification'): message-match chain ad/query/referrer → headline → proof → offer → CTA; ONE primary conversion + minimum qualification data; mobile sticky actions; define control/variant, experiment design, sample-size approach and guardrail metrics BEFORE traffic starts. Phase 3: fast focused page with limited navigational leakage; campaign-safe URL/canonical/OG metadata. Phase 4: click every ad/email/referral destination; run real submissions/purchases with downstream confirmation; validate speed under paid-social mobile network conditions. Phase 5: launch with previous page/control preserved; confirm traffic allocation. Phase 6: review lead/order quality + sales/fulfilment feedback before declaring a conversion winner. Phase 8: one clear hypothesis at a time; maintain experiment learning register. Deliverable deltas: traffic-source/message-match matrix; control/variant and experiment register.

structures.name: Delta: 06_EXISTING_LANDING specifics
structures.detail: Union of 02-style protected-baseline mechanics and 05's landing mechanics. Phase 5 carries BOTH landing extra ('previous page/control preserved + confirm traffic allocation') and migration extra ('redirect/change map, control metrics and rollback triggers active'). Phase 4 adds regression vs protected baseline on top of ad-destination clicks and real submissions. Deliverables = union: master URL inventory, current sitemap/architecture audit, preservation register, redirect/change map, traffic-source/message-match matrix, control/variant and experiment register.

structures.name: Mandatory tools (identical 15-item list)
structures.source: all six files, 'Mandatory tools and reports'
structures.detail: GSC; GA4+GTM; CRM/backend commercial data; Screaming Frog HTML+JS crawls; Semrush Site Audit and visibility; DataForSEO APIs where automation/scale required; Ahrefs or equivalent backlink verification; PageSpeed Insights/CrUX plus GTmetrix or WebPageTest; Clarity/Hotjar behavioural; accessibility/browser-device/security/uptime tools; CRM/marketing automation; ABM/ad platforms; company enrichment; webinar/event tools; sales engagement and call intelligence. Rule: add tools only when they have a defined decision or operational use (feeds R7). Overlay adds: run/archive exact reports per TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv, record tool/version/configuration/market/device/date and known gaps.

structures.name: Common required deliverables (10) shared by all six
structures.detail: Project Charter + classification record; market/domain/location matrix; baseline or research pack; KPI baseline/target/guardrail sheet; page/query/audience map; issue register + prioritised backlog; analytics/event/attribution specification; QA evidence + signed gate records; launch/post-launch report; monitoring dashboard + continuous-improvement backlog. Per-track extras listed in delta structures.

registers.name: Preservation register
registers.purpose: Protected URLs, copy, layouts, CTAs, proof, forms, links and tracking that must survive the change (existing variants 02/04/06); paired with preservation specification + change-impact register per protected asset (Phase 2).
registers.columns: Not specified in these files (protected element, source page, evidence capture implied)

registers.name: Redirect/change map
registers.purpose: Required deliverable where URLs change (02/04/06); active with control metrics and rollback triggers at release (Phase 5).
registers.columns: Not specified

registers.name: Master URL inventory
registers.purpose: Every URL from every discovery source (existing variants); basis for 6-way classification protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire.
registers.columns: Not specified

registers.name: Issue register / implementation backlog
registers.purpose: All findings and work items (Phase 2 all files).
registers.columns: issue ID, priority, owner, dependencies, acceptance criteria (per Phase 2 checklist); full 12-field schema per overlay 'Exact finding format'

registers.name: Decision/Exclusion Register
registers.purpose: Every ignored/rejected recommendation with reason (do-not-do item 6); decision statuses: included, deferred, not applicable, rejected, unknown, accepted-risk (overlay evidence rules). Direct feed for owner requirements R2/R3.
registers.columns: decision status + reason (columns otherwise unspecified)

registers.name: Control/variant and experiment register + experiment learning register
registers.purpose: Landing workflows (05/06): control/variant design, sample-size approach, guardrail metrics defined before traffic; Phase 8 learning capture.
registers.columns: Not specified

registers.name: Access register / access-risk register
registers.purpose: Gate 0 evidence: confirmed access to all first-party systems and identified missing data; overlay Phase 0 adds authorized tools and prohibited actions.
registers.columns: Not specified

registers.name: Competitor roster / competitor evidence matrix
registers.purpose: Overlay Phase 0/1 evidence; 9 competitor set types, archived pages/ads/offers/reviews/SERPs with date+region+source; monthly panel, quarterly full map.
registers.columns: Not specified

registers.name: TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv
registers.purpose: Referenced (not included) in overlay 'Required tool/report runs' of all six files: exact first-party/crawl/competitor/performance/behavioural/commercial reports to run and archive.
registers.columns: Unknown — lives elsewhere in package

registers.name: Required metric panel
registers.purpose: Per-workflow mandatory metric table (identical across the six B2B files).
registers.columns: ID | Metric | Source | Target method | Red flag | Improvement path

registers.name: Roles and sign-off table
registers.purpose: Minimum responsibilities for 9 roles.
registers.columns: Role | Minimum responsibility

registers.name: Phase control and proof matrix
registers.purpose: Overlay per-phase gating.
registers.columns: Phase | Required work | Evidence | Do not proceed when

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 0 — Classification, authority and readiness (identical in all six)
steps: Assign project ID, accountable owner, workflow file, approvers, evidence folder
Classify business model, asset type, new/existing status, project risk
Record production/staging/legacy/campaign domains, subdomains, subfolders
Record target regions, languages, currencies, locations, legal entities, fulfilment, traffic-source routing
Define primary commercial outcome, qualified conversion, secondary conversions, guardrails
Record budget, release date, dependencies, blackout periods, rollback authority
Confirm access to all first-party systems; identify missing data BEFORE recommendations
GATE 0: approved Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, project risk classification

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 1 — NEW: Research and launch baseline (01/03/05) / EXISTING: Discovery and protected baseline (02/04/06)
steps: NEW: demand/opportunity baselines from market research, competitor SERPs, paid data, sales/customer research, business economics; select domain+regional architecture before content/design; proposed business sitemap + URL policy + page inventory + XML sitemap spec; mark third-party estimates as estimates; validate demand before producing entire asset; document assumptions (no history)

EXISTING: freeze dated raw exports (GSC/GA4/GTM/CRM/paid/crawlers/backlinks/server logs/performance); master URL inventory from every discovery source; audit current XML sitemap index + visual architecture; classify every URL protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire; capture protected-page evidence; pre-change KPI baselines + guardrail thresholds; record defects separately from redesign preferences; interview operators/sales/support
All: B2B trust controls (5) + B2B content controls (5); track-specific inserts (CRM/ABM for website, keyword/entity/PR for organic, message-match/source-map/indexability-class for landing)
GATE 1: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet
Approve business requirements, audience, message, offer, differentiation, success measures
Approve IA, proposed sitemap, URL naming rules, navigation, search/filter, internal-linking model
Map ONE primary search intent + ONE primary conversion objective per important page
Page briefs: protected content, proof, CTA, schema, media, localisation, analytics, owner
Design system, accessibility, components, all loading/error/empty/success states; performance budgets by template; third-party script governance; privacy/consent/security/backup/incident-response
Implementation backlog with issue IDs, priority, owner, dependencies, acceptance criteria

Track extras: website=template inventory + launch-critical vs phased; organic=12-month roadmap + one-owning-page-per-cluster + editorial standards + link-earning plans; landing=message-match chain + control/variant + sample-size before traffic; existing variants add preservation spec + avoid simultaneous URL/intent/content/layout/offer/tracking changes
GATE 2: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page or topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog
Build ONLY on controlled staging, production indexing blocked, access restricted

Semantic HTML, crawlable links, status codes, canonicals, directives, schema, responsive media; analytics events, consent, CRM/backend integrations, QA logging; performance budgets, caching, CDN; accessibility behaviours
Release notes; map every change to a requirement or issue ID

Track extras: website=all priority templates with real content + custom error states; organic=fix technical constraints before scaling content + publish only after editorial/SEO/claims/link/conversion QA; landing=focused page, limited navigational leakage, campaign-safe URL/canonical/OG; existing variants=old-vs-new comparison, preserve production asset until new passes; all=integrate CRM campaign/member status, lead scoring, routing, SLA, opportunity-source preservation
GATE 3: build complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 4 — Pre-launch or pre-release QA (common core in all six)
steps: Run HTML crawl, JavaScript crawl, XML sitemap crawl, all-known-URL list crawl
Compare staging vs approved page inventory (and vs production baseline for existing assets)
Validate robots.txt, meta robots, X-Robots-Tag, canonicals, status codes, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data
Test every primary user task on target devices/browsers/languages/currencies/network conditions; forms/calls/WhatsApp/booking/CRM/checkout/payments/email/error recovery
Validate GA4/GTM/pixels, consent, attribution, ecommerce values, backend reconciliation; field/lab performance, accessibility, security, privacy, visual regression
Migration rehearsal, redirect tests, DNS/SSL/CDN plan, backup + rollback rehearsal where applicable

Track extras: website=every template sampled; organic=per-template indexability + differentiation vs competing results; landing=click every ad/email/referral destination + real submissions + paid-social mobile speed; existing=regression vs protected baseline, resolve every unexplained loss
GATE 4: completed test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1, SIGNED Launch Readiness certificate — unresolved P0 stops launch

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 5 — Launch or controlled release (common core)
steps: Open launch command centre; record exact release time/version and responsible participants
Deploy via approved sequence; preserve rollback path
Immediately validate availability, SSL, robots/noindex, canonicals, priority URLs, redirects, sitemap, analytics
Complete a REAL primary conversion; verify in frontend, backend/CRM, analytics, notifications
Check target markets/languages/currencies/locations/availability/traffic-source destinations
Submit/update Search Console sitemaps + platform/feed destinations (submission ≠ guaranteed indexing)
Record incidents, owner, resolution, retest evidence

Track extras: organic=record publication+discovery dates; landing=previous page/control preserved + traffic allocation confirmed; existing=redirect/change map + control metrics + rollback triggers active
GATE 5: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision
Within 24h: full production crawl vs final staging/production baseline
Inspect priority URLs, redirect sources, sitemap processing, 404/5xx, canonicals, schema, rendering

Monitor transactions/forms, qualified conversions, revenue, paid destinations, feeds, support incidents; organic clicks/impressions, rankings, indexed priority pages, crawl activity, backlink destinations
Compare performance/conversion by template, device, region, language, source, location
Fix P0/P1 regressions immediately; record root cause + preventive control
Stabilisation review + approval before closing the launch project

NEW: establish first stable 4-8 week operating baseline before normalising targets; EXISTING: compare vs recent AND seasonal baselines; B2B all: review sales acceptance/meeting quality/pipeline/opportunity velocity, not only form conversion
STABILISATION EXIT: critical paths stable, P0/P1 closed or accepted, performance understood against the correct baseline
Daily during stabilisation: uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives
Weekly for 8-12 weeks: GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, qualified lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links
Monthly: executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog
Quarterly: full technical, content, UX/CRO, accessibility, security, competitor, architecture review
Standing alerts: content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change
Track extras: organic=monthly decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor-change reports; landing=daily spend/sessions/conversion/qualified-outcome/revenue-margin/speed/errors while campaigns run
Collect evidence from users, sales/support, commercial systems, search, crawls, competitors
Diagnose constraint + affected segment; never jump from metric to cosmetic solution
Prioritise by business impact, reach, confidence, risk, effort
Write hypothesis, acceptance criteria, primary metric, guardrails, owner, rollback
Implement ONE controlled change or clearly documented batch; QA implementation and data before evaluating performance
Adopt, iterate, revert or retire on evidence; record the learning
Track extras: organic=feed winning queries/objections/sales questions back into pages; landing=one hypothesis at a time + experiment learning register

overlaps.package_item: Phase 0-5 gate chain with owner-approved evidence per gate (all six files)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 FRONT GATES: brief → strategy (fat) → design_source → golden_page → full build in launches/<domain>/approvals.yaml, CI-enforced
overlaps.note: Package gives the macro lifecycle spine; v1 front gates map into it (Gate 0≈brief, Gate 1-2≈fat strategy approval) but package has NO design_source or golden_page gate — those must be inserted into package Phases 2-3 undiluted per R8.

overlaps.package_item: 'Build only on controlled staging with production indexing blocked' + overlay P4 'Do not proceed: production-only edits' (Phase 3, all six)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE 1 no production writes; Vercel staging; human DNS flips
overlaps.note: Fully consistent; package adds explicit indexing-blocked and untraceable-config-change prohibitions.

overlaps.package_item: 6-way URL classification protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire + preservation register + do-not-do item 2 (02/04/06)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 PROTECTION MAP: every legacy URL KEEP/MERGE/301; HARD GATE 2 no deletions
overlaps.note: Adopt the richer 6-way taxonomy on top of PROTECTION MAP; 'retire' and 'archive/noindex' execution remains owner-approved because HARD GATE 2 bars agent deletions.

overlaps.package_item: Freeze dated raw exports; immutable baseline; SHA-256 manifest; never overwrite baseline evidence (02/04/06 Phase 1 + overlay all six)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 EVIDENCE LAW: launches/<domain>/ committed to git, content-mined/ immutable, append-only audit passes, IST timestamps
overlaps.note: Same doctrine; adopt SHA-256 manifests as an addition to git-committed evidence (git hashes already give integrity, manifest adds portable proof).

overlaps.package_item: Master URL inventory from every discovery source + operator/sales interviews + offline URL uses (02/04/06 Phase 1)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 BUILD DECISION MATRIX: MINE FIRST full inventory before design decisions
overlaps.note: Identical intent; package adds server logs, interviews and offline-reference discovery — extend mine-first checklist.

overlaps.package_item: Pre-change KPI baselines + guardrail thresholds from comparable periods; overlay 24h/72h/7d/28d old-vs-new comparisons (02/04/06)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: Owner R6: DataForSEO PDF baseline of OLD site BEFORE new sitemap; old-vs-new benchmark values feed continuous monitoring
overlaps.note: Package supports R6 but does not mandate the DataForSEO-PDF-before-sitemap ordering; write R6's explicit ordering into Phase 1 of the merged workflow.

overlaps.package_item: 'Mark third-party estimates as estimates' + 5-way finding labels + overlay stop 'estimates presented as truth' (all six)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE 6: never invent facts/IDs/prices — gaps are ASKED, not filled; R4 ask-when-in-doubt
overlaps.note: Adopt labeling discipline; keep v1's stricter rule that real-world gaps must be ASKED of the owner, not merely labelled as assumptions.

overlaps.package_item: 7 'Do not launch or close the release if' conditions (all six)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 GATE REGISTRY (63 gates, merge-blocking) + go-science pre-ship blocking audit
overlaps.note: Add as stop-launch rows in gates/registry.yaml with per-class required/adapted/n_a; they extend, not replace, beauty/go-science gates (gates added, never weakened).

overlaps.package_item: AI rule 8 'Stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval; do not silently bypass' + overlay 'P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review' (all six)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE 9 agent never self-merges; front-gate agent-never-self-approves; owner-only bypass logged
overlaps.note: Reinforces v1 doctrine verbatim-compatible; keep both statements.

overlaps.package_item: 'Complete a real primary conversion and verify in frontend/backend/CRM/analytics' (Phase 5) + 'run real submissions/purchases' (05/06 Phase 4)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 PROOF-OF-WORK: no done without working URL/real output; post-push live-fetch diff vs intent
overlaps.note: Same proof philosophy, but real conversions write to production CRM/payment systems — execution must be human or explicitly flagged test-mode to respect HARD GATE 1; see conflicts.

Executor must be human or an owner-approved test-mode convention; the agent performing these would breach no-production-writes. (all six Phase 5; 05/06 Phase 4)

injection_flags: Each of the six files contains a section titled 'AI-agent execution rules' — 9 numbered imperatives addressed directly to an AI agent (e.g. 'Select the correct workflow before taking action', 'Stop at phase gates', 'Add new learnings to the shared standard'). Content is benign/procedural, but it is instruction-to-agent text embedded in data and must be adopted only via the owner-approved merge, not obeyed as live instructions. Rule 9 in particular directs an agent to modify shared standards documents — if executed blindly this would have an agent writing to doctrine files without owner approval. (all six files)

Overlay 'Required tool/report runs' directs execution of 'the exact ... reports specified in TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv' — a pointer to an external file whose contents were not reviewed here; nothing should be run from that CSV until it is read and owner-approved. (all six files)

AI-002 'Prompt mention share' requires running a 'controlled prompt panel' against LLMs — procedural measurement, not injection, but it involves feeding constructed prompts to models and should be owner-designed. (all six files, overlay metric panel)
No URLs, shell commands, credentials requests, hidden text, or urgency/authority framing found in any of the six files; relative links point only to in-package shared-standards paths.

readings.summary: Six B2C workflow files (B2C-NEW_WEBSITE, B2C-EXISTING_WEBSITE, B2C-NEW_ORGANIC, B2C-EXISTING_ORGANIC, B2C-NEW_LANDING, B2C-EXISTING_LANDING; all Version 1.0, issued 2026-07-19) share one common skeleton: 7 inherited shared standards, Phases 0-8 with Gate 0-5 evidence blocks, a stabilisation-exit condition, a 4-tier monitoring cadence, a 7-step continuous-improvement loop, a 14-item mandatory tool list, a 12-item KPI/guardrail scorecard, a 9-role sign-off table, 7 stop-launch conditions, 9 AI-agent execution rules, and a byte-identical 'Version 2 Agency-OS Overlay' (phase control/proof matrix, 12-field finding format, competitor/market-share requirements, SHA-256 evidence rules, 10-metric panel with OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC target methods, 6-item do-not-do register). Deltas per file sit in Phase 1 (new-asset 'Research and launch baseline' vs existing-asset 'Discovery and protected baseline' with 6-class URL disposition and protected-baseline freeze), Phase 2/3 titles and asset-specific steps, and per-workflow deliverables (URL inventory/preservation register/redirect map for existing; sitemap/XML spec for website; keyword map/12-month roadmap/editorial standard for organic; message-match matrix/experiment register for landing). The package is highly compatible with v1 doctrine (staging-only builds, immutable baselines, evidence law, protection map, ask-don't-assume) but contains ZERO mention of v1's front gates (design_source/golden_page), beauty gate, go-science gate, dual-AI design review, or Dr. Deepu John clinical sign-off — R8 relocation must be an explicit merge action, not assumed. Main conflicts: AI-agent rule 9 authorizes agent self-editing of shared standards; the 9-role table distributes approval authority v1 reserves to the owner and omits the clinical sign-off role; Phase 5 launch steps (DNS/SSL/robots validation, GSC sitemap submission, real conversion/payment completion) need explicit human-executes annotations to preserve HARD GATES 1/3. Each file also contains an authoring defect: trust/content-control checklists duplicated inline in Phase 1 and again as subsections.

structures.name: Six B2C workflow IDs and selectors
structures.detail: B2C-NEW_WEBSITE (no production site exists / genuinely new domain-brand); B2C-EXISTING_WEBSITE (operating site redesigned, replatformed, restructured, moved, consolidated or materially changed); B2C-NEW_ORGANIC (organic search established from zero or not yet an operating capability with baseline+owner); B2C-EXISTING_ORGANIC (rankings/traffic exist and must be protected, repaired, expanded or recovered); B2C-NEW_LANDING (new campaign/offer/product-service/evergreen page with no historical control URL); B2C-EXISTING_LANDING (live landing page already receives traffic, conversions, links or campaign references). All Version 1.0, Issued 2026-07-19. Selection matrix = {new|existing} x {website|organic|landing}.

structures.name: Shared-standards inheritance list (7 docs, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: ../00_SHARED_STANDARDS/: 00_MASTER_OPERATING_SYSTEM.md, 01_TOOL_AND_REPORT_REGISTER.md, 02_REGIONAL_DOMAIN_LOCATION_FRAMEWORK.md, 03_URL_SITEMAP_MIGRATION_STANDARD.md, 04_MEASUREMENT_ATTRIBUTION_STANDARD.md, 05_QA_LAUNCH_MONITORING_LOOP.md, 06_2026_STANDARDS.md. Overlay additionally inherits: Master Agency OS, Competitive Intelligence Playbook, Metric Dictionary, Evidence/Agent Standard, Localization Manual, Monitoring Manual.
structures.source: all 6 files, 'Mandatory inherited standards' + overlay intro

structures.name: Common commercial objective block (identical in all 6)
structures.detail: Objective: generate qualified consumer enquiries, bookings, calls, visits or purchases while building trust and reducing uncertainty. Primary audiences: individual consumers, family decision-makers, local visitors, patients/guests where applicable, influencers/referrers. Primary conversions: qualified enquiry, consultation/appointment, booking, call/WhatsApp connection, store/location visit, direct purchase.

structures.name: Gate 0-5 evidence definitions (exact, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: Gate 0: approved Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, project risk classification. Gate 1: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet. Gate 2: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page or topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog. Gate 3: build/publishing complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps. Gate 4: completed test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1 issues, signed Launch Readiness certificate (unresolved P0 issues stop launch). Gate 5: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision.
structures.source: all 6 files, per-phase 'Gate N evidence' lines

structures.name: Stabilisation exit condition (identical in all 6)
structures.detail: 'Critical paths are stable, P0/P1 regressions are closed or accepted, and performance is understood against the correct baseline.' Plus: establish first stable 4-8 week operating baseline after launch before normalising targets (new-asset files); compare with recent AND seasonal baselines and investigate losses by page/segment (existing-asset files); review connected calls, qualified enquiries, bookings and no-show/cancellation, not only button clicks (all).

structures.name: Monitoring cadence ladder (Phase 7, identical core)
structures.detail: Daily during stabilisation: uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives. Weekly for 8-12 weeks: GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, qualified lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links. Monthly: executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing-page performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog. Quarterly: full technical, content, UX/CRO, accessibility, security, competitor and architecture review. Standing alerts: content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change. Organic files add: content-decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor-change reports monthly. Landing files add: monitor spend, sessions, conversion, qualified outcome, revenue/margin, page speed and errors daily while campaigns run.

structures.name: Continuous improvement loop (Phase 8, 7 steps identical)
structures.detail: 1 collect evidence (users, sales/support, commercial systems, search, crawls, competitors); 2 diagnose constraint and affected segment (no metric-to-cosmetic jumps); 3 prioritise by business impact, reach, confidence, risk, effort; 4 write hypothesis + acceptance criteria + primary metric + guardrails + owner + rollback; 5 implement ONE controlled change or clearly documented batch; 6 QA implementation and data before evaluating performance; 7 adopt/iterate/revert/retire on evidence; record the learning. Organic files add: feed winning queries/objections/sales questions back into pages. Landing files add: one hypothesis at a time; maintain experiment learning register.

structures.name: Stop-launch conditions (7, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: 'Do not launch or close the release if': 1 primary conversion, CRM/order or payment path fails; 2 production indexability, canonicals, sitemap or priority redirects are wrong; 3 analytics cannot measure primary outcome or duplicates material events; 4 a target market receives wrong language/currency/availability/price/shipping/contact route; 5 a critical security, privacy, accessibility or legal issue remains; 6 protected high-value content/links/URLs/proof were removed without approved evidence; 7 rollback, owners or command-centre coverage unavailable for a material release.
structures.source: all 6 files, 'Do not launch or close the release if'

structures.name: AI-agent execution rules (9, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: 1 select correct workflow before acting; 2 never infer an existing URL/page has no value without checking all discovery and commercial sources; 3 label every finding as: observed fact | calculated result | tool estimate | user-provided assumption | recommendation; 4 attach evidence and affected URLs to every issue; 5 do not close an issue without retest evidence; 6 escalate conflicts between commercial truth and third-party SEO scores, do not optimise for the score; 7 preserve immutable pre-change exports and screenshots; 8 stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval, never silently bypass; 9 add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow rather than keeping them only in chat.

structures.name: Roles and sign-off table (9 roles, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: Accountable business owner (commercial outcome, scope, priority, budget, acceptance); Project/product owner (requirements, dependencies, backlog, gates, evidence); SEO/content; Design/UX/CRO; Development/DevOps (implementation, performance, security, deployment, rollback); Analytics/data; CRM/sales/ecommerce operations (revenue truth); Market/legal/privacy owner (localisation, claims, policy, consent, market approval); QA (independent test execution, evidence, retest). NOTE: no clinical/medical reviewer role exists.

structures.name: Mandatory tools list (14, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: Google Search Console; GA4 + GTM; CRM/backend commercial data; Screaming Frog HTML and JavaScript crawls; Semrush Site Audit + visibility; DataForSEO APIs where automation/scale required; Ahrefs or equivalent backlink verification; PageSpeed Insights/CrUX plus GTmetrix or WebPageTest; Clarity/Hotjar behavioural; accessibility/browser-device/security/uptime tools; Google Business Profile; call tracking; booking platform; local rank/citation tools. Rule: 'Add tools only when they have a defined decision or operational use.'

structures.name: Common deliverables (10) + per-workflow deltas
structures.detail: Common: Project Charter + classification record; market/domain/location matrix; baseline or research pack; KPI baseline/target/guardrail sheet; page/query/audience map; issue register + prioritised backlog; analytics/event/attribution specification; QA evidence + signed gate records; launch/post-launch report; monitoring dashboard + continuous-improvement backlog. Deltas — 01 NEW_WEBSITE: + proposed business sitemap, proposed XML sitemap specification, content/template inventory. 02 EXISTING_WEBSITE: + master URL inventory, current sitemap/architecture audit, preservation register, redirect/change map where URLs change, proposed business sitemap, proposed XML sitemap spec, content/template inventory. 03 NEW_ORGANIC: + keyword/topic/intent map, technical/content/authority roadmap, editorial and link-earning standard. 04 EXISTING_ORGANIC: + master URL inventory, sitemap/architecture audit, preservation register, redirect/change map, keyword/topic/intent map, roadmap, editorial standard. 05 NEW_LANDING: + traffic-source/message-match matrix, control/variant and experiment register. 06 EXISTING_LANDING: + master URL inventory, sitemap/architecture audit, preservation register, redirect/change map, traffic-source/message-match matrix, control/variant and experiment register.

structures.name: KPI and guardrail scorecard (12 items + segmentation, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: qualified leads; booking/appointment rate; lead-to-sale rate; revenue per session; call connection and qualification; cost per qualified lead; repeat/revisit/referral; organic clicks/impressions and priority rankings where applicable; indexation and crawl health; Core Web Vitals by important template; technical error and redirect rate; accessibility/security/privacy closure. Segment by: market, domain/subfolder, language, location, device, source/campaign, page/product/service type.

structures.name: Overlay: phase control and proof matrix (columns Phase | Required work | Evidence | Do not proceed when; identical in all 6)
structures.detail: Do-not-proceed conditions per phase: P0 no owner / unclear denominator / missing commercial source / unauthorized scope. P1 incomplete URL discovery / baseline overwritten / estimates presented as truth. P2 recommendation lacks metric, cause, economics, acceptance criteria or evidence. P3 design changes without purpose or protected-elements list. P4 production-only edits, untraceable app/plugin/config changes. P5 open P0, unaccepted P1, broken conversion/redirect/tracking/backup. P6 guardrail breach or inability to verify live commercial path. P7 unexplained material revenue/conversion/indexation/ranking loss. P8 vanity reporting, no owner, repeated recommendations with no learning. P7 comparison windows: 24h/72h/7d/28d vs pre-release and seasonal baselines.
structures.source: all 6 files, overlay 'Phase control and proof matrix'

structures.name: Overlay: exact finding format (12 mandatory fields, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: 1 issue ID, phase, severity; 2 exact metric/formula + affected dimensions; 3 current value, period, source of truth; 4 comparable own baseline + competitor peer values/percentiles + applicable external benchmark; 5 absolute/relative gap + confidence; 6 affected URLs/products/locations/campaigns/cohorts; 7 likely mechanism with corroborating evidence; 8 exact recommendation + owner + dependency; 9 acceptance criteria + automated/manual test; 10 business guardrail + monitoring window + rollback condition; 11 what must not be done; 12 excluded alternatives and why.

structures.name: Overlay: competitor and market-share requirements (identical in all 6)
structures.detail: 9 competitor set types built separately: direct, SERP, paid, marketplace, local, publisher, substitute, AI-answer, aspirational. Peer benchmark classes: median / upper-quartile / leader, on identical market+device+language+period. 7-way opportunity classification: defend, mandatory parity, flank, attack, category-creation, partner, deliberate-ignore. Quantify addressable demand, attainable share, qualified conversion, contribution, confidence. Archive competitor pages/ads/offers/reviews/SERPs with date+region+source; NEVER infer spend or performance from an ad library. Cadence: priority competitor panel monthly, complete market map quarterly. Market-share attack patterns (B2C): win problem+location demand competitors under-serve; use proof and service design to improve qualified conversion; build referral/revisit/review loops.
structures.source: all 6 files, overlay 'Competitor and market-share requirements' + 'Market-share attack patterns'

structures.name: Overlay: evidence and completion requirements (identical in all 6)
structures.detail: Archive raw PDF where useful plus CSV/JSON/crawl/log and configuration. Generate SHA-256 manifest; NEVER overwrite baseline evidence. Link each closed issue to: implementation reference, staging proof, live proof, monitored result. Decision classes (6): included, deferred, not applicable, rejected, unknown, accepted-risk. P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review.
structures.source: all 6 files, overlay 'Evidence and completion requirements'

structures.name: Overlay: required metric panel (10 metrics, benchmark classes OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: COM-001 Revenue (Finance/backend; OWN seasonal baseline + ECONOMIC plan); COM-003 Revenue per session (backend+analytics joined; OWN, peer/context only); COM-004 Qualified lead rate (CRM; OWN + sales capacity/economics); COM-005 Lead-to-win rate (CRM; OWN cohort + sales target); SEO-001 GSC clicks (GSC; OWN seasonal baseline + opportunity forecast); SEO-004 Weighted organic SOV (Semrush/STAT/AccuRanker; PEER median then upper quartile in priority clusters); AI-001 Google generative impressions (GSC Generative AI report; OWN trend, availability caveat); UX-001 Task success rate (usability test; per critical task vs baseline/peer test); CRO-001 Primary conversion rate (backend/CRM+analytics; OWN seasonal + industry context + experiment); LOC-001 Local pack visibility share (local rank tracker/DataForSEO; PEER by location). Numbering non-contiguous (COM-002, SEO-002/003 absent — full dictionary presumably in Metric Dictionary file).

structures.name: Overlay: mandatory do-not-do register (6 prohibited shortcuts, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: 1 no redesign for visual novelty without measurable user/brand/search/commercial purpose; 2 never delete or redirect an existing page without master URL and preservation checks; 3 never apply a benchmark whose definition or segment is not comparable; 4 never copy competitor content, claims, creative or dark patterns; 5 never close work before live evidence and monitoring; 6 never leave ignored recommendations unexplained — use the Decision/Exclusion Register.

structures.name: URL disposition classification (6 classes, existing-asset workflows)
structures.detail: Classify every URL: protect | refresh | consolidate | redirect | archive/noindex | retire. Companion rule: identify pages with rankings, conversions, backlinks, paid traffic, referral traffic or offline references that must be protected; capture screenshots, copy, metadata, schema, internal links and conversion components for protected pages; build master URL inventory from EVERY discovery source, never navigation/sitemap alone; interview operators/sales/support for hidden dependencies and offline URL uses.

structures.name: Landing-page indexability classification (5 classes, landing workflows)
structures.detail: Define whether the page is: SEO indexable | paid-only noindex | evergreen | temporary | controlled test variant. Plus traffic-source and audience map (campaign, keyword/ad, creative, email/referrer, region, device, expected intent) and offer economics record (availability, qualification, fulfilment, sales-response capacity).

structures.name: B2C-specific trust controls (5) and content controls (5) — duplicated in-file
structures.detail: Trust: clear identity/address/contact/team/credentials; service scope/process/price-range/eligibility/limitations; authentic testimonials+independently verifiable proof; privacy/cancellation-refund/safety/support info; local credibility/directions/response-time promise. Content: problem-need pages mapped to service solutions; service/programme/location/practitioner/proof pages; decision content (process, comparison, suitability, FAQs, pricing, next steps); post-service support and retention content; YMYL/health content reviewed and claims controlled where relevant. AUTHORING DEFECT: these items appear TWICE in each file — inline inside Phase 1 checklist AND again as dedicated subsections.
structures.source: all 6 files, Phase 1 + 'B2C-specific trust controls' / 'B2C-specific content controls'

structures.name: B2C-specific competitive edge controls (5, overlay, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: Capture and test: urgent vs considered journey; call/WhatsApp/booking routing; location/service eligibility; trust, credentials and reviews; lead response and no-show/cancellation.
structures.source: all 6 files, overlay 'B2C-specific competitive edge controls'

structures.name: Phase-title variants by asset type
structures.detail: Phase 1: 'Research and launch baseline' (01, 03, 05 — new) vs 'Discovery and protected baseline' (02, 04, 06 — existing). Phase 2: 'Site strategy, architecture and specification' (01, 02) / 'Organic strategy, architecture and roadmap' (03, 04) / 'Offer, message, page and experiment specification' (05, 06). Phase 3: 'Design, content, development and integration' (01, 02) / 'Technical, content, authority and conversion implementation' (03, 04) / 'Landing-page build and integration' (05, 06). Phases 0, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 titles identical across all six.

structures.name: Existing-asset delta steps (02, 04, 06)
structures.detail: Phase 1: freeze dated raw exports (GSC, GA4, GTM, CRM/backend, paid media, crawlers, backlinks, server logs, performance tools); set pre-change KPI baselines and launch guardrail thresholds using comparable periods; record current defects separately from redesign preferences. Phase 2: preservation specification + change-impact register for every protected asset; avoid simultaneous changes to URL, intent, content, layout, offer and tracking unless necessary and approved. Phase 3: maintain old-versus-new comparison; preserve existing production asset until the new version passes. Phase 4: regression checks against protected baseline; resolve every unexplained loss. Phase 5: release with redirect/change map, control metrics and rollback triggers active. Phase 6: compare with recent AND seasonal baselines, investigate losses by page/segment.

structures.name: Organic delta steps (03, 04)
structures.detail: Phase 1: local/non-local query segmentation; service-location architecture without doorway duplication; Business Profile + review integration; branded/non-branded and symptom/problem-to-service mapping; referral and authority content; query-topic-page map segmented by intent/funnel/market/language/location; benchmark direct commercial competitors, SERP competitors, publishers, marketplaces, local results; identify technical/content/authority/internal-link/reputation/SERP-feature gaps. Phase 2: 12-month technical/content/authority roadmap; one primary owning page per intent cluster, resolve cannibalisation before expansion; editorial standards for originality/experience/expertise/claims/sourcing/refresh cadence; digital PR/link-earning, local/partner/reputation, internal-link plans. Phase 3: fix technical/indexation constraints BEFORE scaling content; upgrade priority commercial pages, connect supporting content; publish only after editorial, SEO, factual/claims, link and conversion QA; dashboards by branded/non-branded, page type, topic, market, outcome. Phase 4: validate indexability/rendered content/canonicals/schema/internal links for every published template; check content differentiation against actual competing results, reject thin or repetitive production. Phase 5: record publication and discovery dates. Phase 6: review query/page movement, indexation, leads/orders and assisted revenue by cohort of changes.

structures.name: Landing delta steps (05, 06)
structures.detail: Phase 1: match campaign/search promise exactly; CTA placement per urgency; proof near claims and forms; minimise form fields while qualifying sufficiently; track response time and sales outcome, not only submissions. Phase 2: message-match chain from ad/query/referrer to headline, proof, offer, CTA; ONE primary conversion + minimum qualification data; mobile sticky actions; control/variant, experiment design, sample-size approach and guardrail metrics defined BEFORE traffic starts. Phase 3: fast focused page with limited navigational leakage appropriate to traffic source; campaign-safe URL/canonical/indexability/Open Graph decisions. Phase 4: click every ad/email/referral destination and verify message/product/region/language/device/tracking; run real submissions/purchases and confirm source, campaign, value, lead/order status downstream; validate page speed under paid-social mobile network conditions. Phase 5: launch with previous page/control preserved, confirm traffic allocation. Phase 6: review lead/order quality and sales/fulfilment feedback before declaring a conversion winner.

structures.name: New-asset delta steps (01, 03, 05)
structures.detail: Phase 1: validate demand and proposition BEFORE producing the entire asset — use research, prototypes or limited campaign tests where risk is high; document assumptions because no historical site/page performance exists; select domain/regional architecture before content or design production; build proposed business sitemap, URL policy, page inventory, XML sitemap specification; mark third-party estimates as estimates. Overlay tool-run rule for new assets: create research baselines and explicit assumptions rather than inventing historical performance.

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 0 - Classification, authority and readiness (identical in all 6)
steps: Assign project ID, accountable owner, workflow file, approvers, evidence folder
Classify business model, asset type, new/existing status, project risk
Record production/staging/legacy/campaign domains, subdomains, subfolders
Record target regions, languages, currencies, locations, legal entities, fulfilment, traffic-source routing
Define primary commercial outcome, qualified conversion, secondary conversions, guardrails
Record budget, release date, dependencies, blackout periods, rollback authority
Confirm access to all first-party systems; identify missing data before recommendations
GATE 0: Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, risk classification

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 1 - Research and launch baseline (new: 01/03/05) OR Discovery and protected baseline (existing: 02/04/06)
steps: NEW: demand/opportunity baselines, customer journeys, domain selection before content/design, proposed sitemap + URL policy + XML spec, targets marked as estimates, document assumptions

EXISTING: freeze dated raw exports, master URL inventory from every discovery source, sitemap audit, 6-class URL classification (protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire), protected-page capture, pre-change KPI baselines and guardrail thresholds, defects recorded separately from preferences, operator interviews
ALL: B2C conversion infrastructure + trust controls (5) + content controls (5), asset-type specific controls (organic query maps / landing traffic-source maps)
GATE 1: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 2 - Strategy/architecture/specification (title varies by asset type)
steps: Approve business requirements, audience, message, offer, differentiation, success measures
Approve IA, proposed sitemap, URL naming rules, navigation, internal-linking model
One primary search intent + one primary conversion objective per important page
Page briefs: protected content, proof, CTA, schema, media, localisation, analytics, owner
Design system, accessibility, performance budgets by template, third-party governance, privacy/consent/security/backup/incident requirements
Implementation backlog with issue IDs, priority, owner, dependencies, acceptance criteria
Existing assets: preservation specification + change-impact register; avoid simultaneous URL/intent/content/layout/offer/tracking changes
Organic: 12-month roadmap, cannibalisation resolution, editorial + link-earning standards; Landing: message-match chain, experiment design before traffic
GATE 2: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page/topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 3 - Build/implementation (title varies by asset type)
steps: Build ONLY on controlled staging with production indexing blocked and access restricted
Semantic HTML, crawlable links, status codes, canonicals, directives, schema, responsive media
Analytics events, consent, CRM/backend integrations, QA logging; performance budgets, caching, CDN; accessibility behaviours
Release notes; every change mapped to a requirement or issue ID
Existing assets: old-vs-new comparison, preserve production asset until new version passes
GATE 3: build complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 4 - Pre-launch or pre-release QA (identical core in all 6)
steps: HTML crawl, JavaScript crawl, XML sitemap crawl, all-known-URL list crawl
Compare staging vs approved page inventory and (existing) production baseline
Validate robots.txt, meta robots, X-Robots-Tag, canonicals, status codes, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data
Test every primary user task on target devices/browsers/languages/currencies/network conditions; forms, calls, WhatsApp, booking, CRM, checkout, payments, error recovery
Validate GA4/GTM/pixels, consent, attribution, backend reconciliation; performance, accessibility, security, privacy, visual regression
Migration rehearsal, redirect tests, DNS/SSL/CDN plan, backup and rollback rehearsal where applicable
Existing: regression checks vs protected baseline, resolve every unexplained loss; Landing: click every ad destination, real submissions under paid-social mobile network conditions
GATE 4: completed test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1, SIGNED Launch Readiness certificate — unresolved P0 stops launch

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 5 - Launch or controlled release (identical core in all 6)
steps: Open launch command centre; record exact release time/version and responsible participants
Deploy via approved sequence; preserve rollback path
Immediately validate availability, SSL, robots/noindex, canonicals, priority URLs, redirects, sitemap, analytics
Complete a REAL primary conversion; verify in frontend, backend/CRM, analytics, notifications
Check markets, languages, currencies, locations, availability, traffic-source destinations
Submit/update Search Console sitemaps and feeds; submission is not guaranteed indexing
Existing: redirect/change map + control metrics + rollback triggers active; Landing: previous page/control preserved, traffic allocation confirmed
GATE 5: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 6 - Post-launch stabilisation (identical core in all 6)
steps: Within 24h: full production crawl vs final staging/production baseline
Inspect priority URLs, redirect sources, sitemap processing, 404/5xx, canonicals, schema, rendering
Monitor transactions/forms, qualified conversions, revenue, paid destinations, feeds, support incidents; organic clicks/rankings/indexation/crawl/backlinks
Fix P0/P1 regressions immediately; record root cause and preventive control
Stabilisation review + approval before closing launch project; 4-8 week operating baseline (new) / recent+seasonal comparison (existing)
EXIT: critical paths stable, P0/P1 closed or accepted, performance understood against the correct baseline
Daily during stabilisation; weekly for 8-12 weeks; monthly executive scorecard + recrawl; quarterly full review; standing decay/link/redirect/privacy/platform alerts
Organic: monthly decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor-change reports; Landing: daily spend/conversion/revenue monitoring while campaigns run

Collect evidence -> diagnose constraint -> prioritise (impact/reach/confidence/risk/effort) -> hypothesis with acceptance criteria + guardrails + rollback -> one controlled change -> QA before evaluation -> adopt/iterate/revert/retire + record learning
Landing: one hypothesis at a time, experiment learning register; Organic: feed winning queries back into pages

overlaps.package_item: Phase 0-8 gated lifecycle with Gate 0-5 owner-approval evidence blocks
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 FRONT GATES chain (brief -> strategy(fat) -> design_source -> golden_page -> full build) in launches/<domain>/approvals.yaml, CI-enforced
overlaps.note: Package Phases 0-2 absorb brief/strategy front gates; design_source (MODE A/B) and golden_page have NO package counterpart and must be inserted into Phase 2/3 per R8 — adopting the package skeleton alone would silently drop them.

overlaps.package_item: Gate evidence requirements + 'do not proceed when' proof matrix
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 EVIDENCE LAW: launches/<domain>/ filled checklists + gate evidence committed to git, append-only, IST timestamps
overlaps.note: Store package gate evidence inside launches/<domain>/; package adds SHA-256 manifests and artifact-manifest concept, which strengthens v1.

overlaps.package_item: Build only on controlled staging with production indexing blocked and access restricted (Phase 3, all 6)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE 1 (no production writes) + Vercel preview/staging flow
overlaps.note: Identical intent; v1 script/CI enforcement is the operative control — package line documents it.

overlaps.package_item: Phase 4 QA + signed Launch Readiness certificate, unresolved P0 stops launch
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 63-gate registry (gates/registry.yaml) generated per-site checklists + design-review Gate 2 + beauty-audit + go-science-audit (all merge-blocking)
overlaps.note: Package Phase 4 becomes the slot where all v1 blocking audits execute; Launch Readiness certificate = aggregate of registry passes + beauty + go-science + dual-AI review PASS. Package has no aesthetic or marketing-science gate of its own.

overlaps.package_item: Phase 5 launch command centre: deploy, DNS/SSL/CDN, robots/noindex validation, GSC sitemap submission
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1: production DNS flips are ALWAYS human; HARD GATE 3 no DNS/robots changes by agent; Editor-role creds only
overlaps.note: Adopt command-centre structure but annotate which steps are human-only (DNS flip, robots change, GSC submission); the package assigns these to a generic Development/DevOps role with no agent restriction.

overlaps.package_item: Phase 5 'complete a real primary conversion' / Phase 4 landing 'run real submissions/purchases'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 PROOF-OF-WORK (no done without real output) + agent payment/purchase restrictions
overlaps.note: Strengthens proof-of-work, but real payments/purchases must be executed by a human; assign explicitly in merged workflow.

overlaps.package_item: Phase 6 24h production crawl + stabilisation exit + 24h/72h/7d/28d comparison windows
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 post-push live-fetch diff vs intent (PROOF-OF-WORK)
overlaps.note: Extends v1's single post-push check into a timed stabilisation protocol; new capability, no dilution.

overlaps.package_item: Phase 7 monitoring cadence (daily/weekly 8-12wk/monthly/quarterly + alerts)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 STATUS.yaml fleet pulse at session end + Monday lints + R6 continuous monitoring (GSC/analytics/SERP before-after inputs for owner's separate tool)
overlaps.note: Package cadence supplies the R6 monitoring input structure; reconcile per-launch cadence with fleet-level STATUS.yaml so ~25 sites don't each demand separate weekly manual cycles.

overlaps.package_item: Phase 8 continuous improvement loop + AI rule 9 (add learnings to shared standard)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 DIRECTIVES.md same-session capture + 'gates are added, never weakened; removal needs owner ruling in DECISIONS.md' + HARD GATE 9 agent never self-merges
overlaps.note: Loop itself merges cleanly, but rule 9 as written authorizes the agent to edit governing standards directly; must be rewritten as 'propose via PR, owner approves' to preserve HARD GATE 9 and rule g.

overlaps.package_item: AI rule 3: label every finding as observed fact / calculated result / tool estimate / user-provided assumption / recommendation
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE 6 never invent facts/IDs/prices; gaps are ASKED not filled
overlaps.note: Richer 5-class labeling taxonomy; directly serves R2 (provenance) and R4 (ask-when-in-doubt); strengthens, never weakens.

overlaps.package_item: AI rule 8: stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval; never silently bypass
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 agent never self-approves front gates / never self-merges PRs (owner-only bypass, logged); CI fails unsigned rows
overlaps.note: Compatible restatement; v1 version is stronger (named owner + CI enforcement) and governs.

overlaps.package_item: Do-not-do: never delete/redirect an existing page without master URL and preservation checks
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE 2 (no deletions) + BUILD DECISION MATRIX PROTECTION MAP (every legacy URL KEEP/MERGE/301)
overlaps.note: Same doctrine; adopt the package's register format while keeping HARD GATE 2 absolute (agent never deletes, period).

overlaps.package_item: 6-class URL disposition taxonomy (protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 PROTECTION MAP 3-class (KEEP/MERGE/301)
overlaps.note: Superset: KEEP->protect, MERGE->consolidate, 301->redirect; adds refresh/archive-noindex/retire. 'Retire' needs owner ruling per case since HARD GATE 2 forbids agent deletions.

overlaps.package_item: Freeze dated raw exports; SHA-256 manifests; never overwrite baseline evidence
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 content-mined/ immutable raw content + append-only audit passes
overlaps.note: Adds cryptographic manifests to v1's immutability doctrine; direct upgrade.

overlaps.package_item: Master URL inventory from every discovery source (not navigation/sitemap alone) + operator interviews for offline URL uses
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 MINE FIRST (full inventory of live site before design decisions)
overlaps.note: Identical doctrine; adopt the package's explicit source list (GSC, GA4, logs, backlinks, paid, crawlers) into MINE FIRST.

overlaps.package_item: Pre-change KPI baseline + current sitemap audit BEFORE Phase 2 sitemap approval
overlaps.existing_mechanism: R6 BASELINE-BEFORE-SITEMAP (DataForSEO PDF of old site before new sitemap)
overlaps.note: Package sequencing already satisfies R6; name the DataForSEO PDF as a mandatory Gate 1 artifact in existing-asset workflows (DataForSEO is already on the package tool list).

overlaps.package_item: Required metric panel with OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC target methods + red flags + improvement paths
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 GO-SCIENCE GATE (ROI the key metric; rubric fail-closed)
overlaps.note: Adopt the panel as the measurement layer; go-science ROI remains the overriding commercial lens — AI rule 6 (escalate commercial truth vs third-party scores) actually supports this.

overlaps.package_item: 12-field exact finding format (incl. field 11 'what must not be done' and field 12 'excluded alternatives and why')
overlaps.existing_mechanism: R2 DECISION PROVENANCE + v1 DECISIONS.md / QUESTIONS.md
overlaps.note: Directly implements R2's 'scientific answer, historically retrievable'; wire outputs into R3 report store.

overlaps.package_item: Decision classes (included/deferred/not-applicable/rejected/unknown/accepted-risk) + Decision/Exclusion Register
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 DECISIONS.md owner rulings
overlaps.note: Extend DECISIONS.md schema with the 6 package classes; register itself defined elsewhere in package (another reader's scope).

overlaps.package_item: 9-role roles-and-sign-off table (identical in all 6 workflows)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 reality: owner (Abilash) approves everything; agent executes; Dr. Deepu John signs clinical content (HARD GATE 7)
overlaps.note: Distributes approval authority v1 reserves to the owner, and OMITS any clinical/medical reviewer role — mapping 'Market/legal/privacy owner' onto clinical sign-off would weaken HARD GATE 7. Owner must map all 9 roles to real people (most collapse to owner+agent) and add the clinical role explicitly.

overlaps.package_item: 'P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review' (overlay)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 owner-only approvals; HARD GATE 9 agent never self-merges
overlaps.note: Interpret 'independent human' as the owner (or owner-designated human); the agent can never satisfy this clause. Keep v1's stricter named-approver model.

overlaps.package_item: 7 stop-launch conditions ('Do not launch or close the release if')
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 merge-blocking registry gates + per-class checklists
overlaps.note: Add as registry rows (gates are added, never weakened) with required|adapted|n_a per commerce/organic/landing class; condition 6 (protected content removed without approved evidence) mirrors PROTECTION MAP.

overlaps.package_item: YMYL/health content reviewed and claims controlled where relevant (B2C content control)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE 7 Dr. Deepu John sign-off + KTAHV clinical language lock (banned words list)
overlaps.note: v1 named-reviewer, script-enforced gate is far stronger; package's generic line maps to it — do not replace.

overlaps.package_item: Mandatory tools list (14) + TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv runs with tool/version/config/date/gaps
overlaps.existing_mechanism: R7 TOOL/SKILL MAP + v1 audit tool stack (ChatGPT auditor, Perplexity auditor, Tavily, DataForSEO)
