overlaps.package_item: Six-workflow selection matrix ({new|existing} x {website|organic|landing}) + AI rule 1 (select correct workflow first)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 three site classes (commerce/organic/landing) in gates/registry.yaml + BUILD DECISION MATRIX for rebuilds
overlaps.note: Orthogonal dimensions: every project gets BOTH a workflow file (package) and a gate class (v1 registry). No B2C commerce/ecommerce workflow exists in this folder — mapping for KAPPL/Shopify unresolved (open question).

overlaps.package_item: Overlay layering doctrine ('The original checklist remains valid; this overlay adds the controls...')
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 rule: gates are added, never weakened
overlaps.note: Same additive doctrine; the package itself models the never-weaken pattern.

overlaps.package_item: Competitor intelligence: 9 competitor sets, peer percentiles, 7-way opportunity classification, monthly/quarterly cadence, archival with date/region/source
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 front-gate strategy approval includes competitor-map; R4 real-world inputs (competitors) ASKED from user, not assumed
overlaps.note: Adopt the intelligence structure but the competitor roster is confirmed by the owner at Gate 0 per R4; archives land in launches/<domain>/ per evidence law; 'do not infer spend from ad library' aligns with HARD GATE 6.

overlaps.package_item: Landing-page experimentation: control/variant, sample-size approach, guardrails before traffic, experiment learning register
overlaps.existing_mechanism: none in v1
overlaps.note: Net-new capability; requires infrastructure (traffic allocation, variant serving) the Next.js factory does not currently have — owner to sequence.

overlaps.package_item: Validate demand/proposition before producing the entire asset (new-asset workflows)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 lean-at-birth complete-at-launch + slow-beats-fast
overlaps.note: Compatible: package adds pre-build demand validation; v1 keeps launch-completeness bar.

overlaps.package_item: Old-vs-new comparison; preserve existing production asset until new version passes (existing-asset workflows)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 slow-beats-fast + human DNS flip as the final switch
overlaps.note: Consistent; the production-preservation rule reinforces HARD GATES 1-3.

overlaps.package_item: Finding field 4 benchmark comparability rule + do-not-do 3 (no non-comparable benchmarks)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: no v1 equivalent (v1 has no benchmark discipline)
overlaps.note: New rigor: every benchmark must state definition and segment comparability; supports R2.

new_capabilities: Structured competitor-intelligence programme: 9 distinct competitor set types, peer median/upper-quartile/leader percentile benchmarking on identical market/device/language/period, 7-way opportunity classification (defend/mandatory-parity/flank/attack/category-creation/partner/deliberate-ignore), monthly priority panel + quarterly full market map, dated/regioned archival

Required metric panel with stable metric IDs (COM/SEO/AI/UX/CRO/LOC) and three benchmark classes (OWN baseline / PEER percentile / ECONOMIC plan), each with red-flag and improvement-path definitions — including AI-001 Google generative-AI visibility tracking
12-field exact finding format including mandatory 'what must not be done' and 'excluded alternatives and why' fields (direct R2 implementation)

6-class URL disposition taxonomy (protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire) upgrading the 3-class PROTECTION MAP, plus preservation specification and change-impact register formalisms
5-class landing-page indexability classification (SEO indexable / paid-only noindex / evergreen / temporary / controlled test variant) and traffic-source/message-match matrix

Landing-page experimentation infrastructure: control/variant design, sample-size approach and guardrail metrics defined before traffic, previous-page/control preservation at launch, experiment learning register

Launch command centre protocol with recorded release time/version, responsible participants, rollback triggers, and real-conversion live verification across frontend/backend/CRM/analytics/notifications
Timed stabilisation windows (24h full production crawl; 24h/72h/7d/28d comparisons vs pre-release AND seasonal baselines) and 4-8 week post-launch operating baseline before target normalisation
SHA-256 evidence manifests over raw exports (PDF+CSV/JSON/crawl/log/config) with never-overwrite-baseline rule
Decision/Exclusion Register with 6 decision classes (included/deferred/not-applicable/rejected/unknown/accepted-risk) — every ignored recommendation must be explained

4-tier monitoring cadence ladder (daily stabilisation / weekly 8-12 weeks / monthly / quarterly) plus monthly content-decay, cannibalisation, lost-link and competitor-change reports for organic assets
5-class finding-provenance labeling (observed fact / calculated result / tool estimate / user-provided assumption / recommendation)

B2C operational conversion controls new to v1: call/WhatsApp tracking, CRM routing by service/location/language, response-time ownership, no-show/cancellation tracking, urgent-vs-considered journey mapping, connected-call quality review (not just button clicks)

Organic programme discipline: query-topic-page map, one primary owning page per intent cluster with cannibalisation resolution before expansion, 12-month technical/content/authority roadmap, editorial and link-earning standard, doorway-duplication prohibition
Message-match chain specification (ad/query/referrer -> headline -> proof -> offer -> CTA) and paid-social mobile-network page-speed validation
Interview-based discovery of hidden URL dependencies and offline URL uses (operators/sales/support)
conflicts: AI-agent execution rule 9 (all 6 files): 'Add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow' authorizes the agent to directly edit governing standards. Violates v1 doctrine that gate/standard changes require owner ruling in DECISIONS.md and HARD GATE 9 (agent never self-merges). Merge must rewrite as: agent PROPOSES standard changes via PR; owner approves and merges.

Roles-and-sign-off table (all 6 files) omits any clinical/medical reviewer role. Mapping KTAHV clinical content onto the generic 'Market/legal/privacy owner' role would weaken HARD GATE 7 (Dr. Deepu John sign-off). The merged role table must add the named clinical sign-off role explicitly.

The 9-role table distributes gate-approval authority ('approvers' assigned at Phase 0) across roles; v1 reserves all gate approvals to the owner with CI-enforced signature rows. If roles are staffed by the agent acting in multiple capacities, package language could be read as the agent approving its own gates — merged text must state the agent can hold execution roles only, never approval roles.

Phase 5 launch steps (deploy sequence, DNS/SSL/CDN, robots/noindex changes, Search Console sitemap submission) carry no human-only annotation. Unannotated adoption would erode HARD GATE 3 (no DNS/robots changes by agent) and the human-DNS-flip rule. Merge must mark these steps human-executed with agent verification only.

Phase 5 'complete a real primary conversion' and Phase 4 landing 'run real submissions/purchases': real payment execution cannot be an agent task; assign to a named human in the merged workflow (test-mode alternatives need owner ruling since the package demands REAL conversions).

Overlay 'independent human review' for P0/P1 closure and launch gates is weaker than v1's owner-only approval if read as 'any human'; merged text must pin the reviewer to the owner or an owner-designated named person.

Package workflows contain no design_source (MODE A/B), golden_page gate, beauty gate, go-science gate, or dual external-AI design review anywhere in Phases 2-4. Adopting this package as the replacement workflow layer without explicit relocation of those v1 mechanisms would violate R8 (gate continuity, undiluted). This is the largest structural risk in the whole B2C section.

Package 'archive/noindex' and 'retire' URL classes imply page removal; HARD GATE 2 forbids agent deletions. Retire/archive actions must be owner-executed or owner-approved per URL in the merged PROTECTION MAP.

Overlay proof-matrix Phase 4 'automated tests and human QA' plus role 'QA: independent test execution' presumes a QA person separate from builder; in v1's one-owner+agent operation this collapses — owner must rule on who constitutes independent QA, or the clause silently becomes self-review (a gate weakening).
injection_flags: 'AI-agent execution rules' section (identical in all 6 files, e.g. 01_NEW_WEBSITE.md lines 254-264): nine numbered imperatives addressed directly to an AI agent ('Select the correct workflow before taking action', 'Stop at phase gates', etc.). Content is benign/procedural, but it is instruction-to-agent text embedded in ingested data — adopt only through the merge plan, never obey directly from the package.

Rule 9 specifically ('Add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow rather than keeping them only in chat') is a self-modification directive: if obeyed literally it instructs the agent to edit its own governing documents. Flagged both as injection-shaped and as a conflict; must be gated behind owner-approved PRs.

Overlay 'do not proceed when' columns and 'Required tool/report runs' checklists are imperative but procedural; no URLs, shell commands, scripts, credentials or fetch targets appear anywhere in the six files. TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv is referenced as a data file, not an execution instruction. No hidden, encoded, or authority-claiming text observed.
open_questions: Authoring defect: in every file the B2C trust-control and content-control checklists appear twice (inline in Phase 1 AND as dedicated subsections), and conversion-infrastructure items are pasted un-headed into Phase 1. Should the merged versions dedupe, or preserve package text verbatim with an errata note?

Workflow-to-class mapping: package B2C folder has no commerce/ecommerce workflow, while v1's registry classes are commerce/organic/landing. Which package workflow governs KAPPL (Shopify/commerce track) — a B2B/ecommerce file elsewhere in the package, or does commerce need a new workflow file?

Who fills the 9 roles? Presumably most collapse to owner (Abilash) + agent, with Dr. Deepu John (clinical) and possibly Akshar (marketing science) as named humans — owner must publish the role->person map before any workflow runs, since Gate 0 requires naming approvers.
Does 'independent human review' for P0/P1 closure and launch gates mean the owner alone, or does the owner want a second human reviewer for material launches?

Metric panel numbering is non-contiguous (COM-002, SEO-002/003, CRO-002+ absent). Confirm the B2C subset is intentional and the full dictionary lives in the Metric Dictionary file (another reader's scope).

Cadence feasibility: weekly monitoring for 8-12 weeks per launch and 4-8 week baselines across ~25 sites — should cadence be per-launch as written, or consolidated into the fleet-level STATUS.yaml/monitoring-tool pulse the owner is building (R6)?

R8 relocation mapping: exactly where do golden_page, design_source MODE A/B, beauty gate, go-science gate and the dual-AI design review slot into Phases 2-4? (Proposed: design_source+golden_page in Phase 2/3; beauty+go-science+dual-AI review as named Phase 4 certificate components — needs owner ruling.)

Tool procurement: which of the package-mandated tools not in the v1 stack (Screaming Frog licence, Semrush, Ahrefs, GTmetrix/WebPageTest, Hotjar, call tracking, booking platform, local rank/citation tools) does the owner actually want to license now vs mark deferred in the Decision/Exclusion Register?

Experimentation infrastructure: control/variant serving and traffic allocation do not exist in the v1 Next.js factory. Build now for the landing workflows, or defer the experiment-register clauses until infrastructure exists?

Package requires REAL conversions (including purchases) at launch verification. For payment paths, does the owner accept designated-human test purchases, or sandbox/test-mode transactions as compliant evidence?

readings.summary: Six Shopify workflows (all Version 1.0, Issued 2026-07-19) form a 2x3 matrix: {new, existing} x {store, organic programme, landing page}, with IDs SHOPIFY-NEW_STORE, SHOPIFY-EXISTING_STORE, SHOPIFY-NEW_ORGANIC, SHOPIFY-EXISTING_ORGANIC, SHOPIFY-NEW_LANDING, SHOPIFY-EXISTING_LANDING. All share an identical 9-phase skeleton (Phase 0 Classification/authority -> 8 Continuous improvement) with per-phase gate evidence, an identical 7-item do-not-launch list, identical 9-role sign-off table, identical 9 AI-agent execution rules, and an identical appended "Version 2 Agency-OS Overlay" (phase control/proof matrix, 12-field finding format, competitor requirements, SHA-256 evidence rules, 10-metric panel, do-not-do register). Deltas are confined to: Phase 1 (Research-and-launch-baseline for new vs Discovery-and-protected-baseline for existing), Phase 2/3 names and track-specific steps, existing-asset preservation/regression steps, and per-track deliverables. The package maps cleanly onto v1's commerce/organic/landing site classes and MINE-FIRST/PROTECTION-MAP doctrine, but contains NO golden-page, beauty, go-science, or external-AI-design-review equivalents (keep_existing per R8), assumes a 9-person agency team (conflict with solo-owner ops), and its AI-agent rule 9 lets the agent edit shared standards (conflict with owner-only doctrine changes). Overlay proof-matrix phase numbering is off-by-one vs the base checklist phases — an internal inconsistency only the owner can rule on.

structures.name: Workflow taxonomy and IDs
structures.detail: 2x3 matrix, one file each: 01 SHOPIFY-NEW_STORE (new implementation / migration into Shopify before launch); 02 SHOPIFY-EXISTING_STORE (live store redesigned, re-themed, restructured, moved between stores/domains or materially reconfigured); 03 SHOPIFY-NEW_ORGANIC (organic search established from zero / not yet an operating capability with baseline+owner); 04 SHOPIFY-EXISTING_ORGANIC (rankings/traffic exist and must be protected, repaired, expanded or recovered); 05 SHOPIFY-NEW_LANDING (new campaign/offer/product/evergreen page, no historical control URL); 06 SHOPIFY-EXISTING_LANDING (live landing page with traffic, conversions, links or campaign references). All: Version 1.0, Issued 2026-07-19. Identical 'Commercial objective' block in all six: operate a technically controlled, internationally correct, commercially optimised Shopify store without losing URL, product, customer, feed or tracking equity; primary conversions: order/subscription, product discovery, cart/checkout progression, repeat order, profitable market expansion.
structures.source: all six files, header + 'Use this workflow when'

structures.name: Mandatory inherited standards (identical list, all six)
structures.detail: ../00_SHARED_STANDARDS/: 00_MASTER_OPERATING_SYSTEM.md, 01_TOOL_AND_REPORT_REGISTER.md, 02_REGIONAL_DOMAIN_LOCATION_FRAMEWORK.md, 03_URL_SITEMAP_MIGRATION_STANDARD.md, 04_MEASUREMENT_ATTRIBUTION_STANDARD.md, 05_QA_LAUNCH_MONITORING_LOOP.md, 06_2026_STANDARDS.md. Overlay additionally inherits: Master Agency OS, Competitive Intelligence Playbook, Metric Dictionary, Evidence/Agent Standard, Localization Manual, Monitoring Manual.
structures.source: all six files, 'Mandatory inherited standards' + overlay preamble

structures.name: Phase gate evidence chain (exact, identical wording all six)
structures.detail: Gate 0: approved Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, project risk classification. Gate 1: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet. Gate 2: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page or topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog. Gate 3: build/publishing complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps. Gate 4: completed test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1 issues, signed Launch Readiness certificate ('unresolved P0 issues stop launch'). Gate 5: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision. Stabilisation exit (Phase 6): critical paths stable, P0/P1 regressions closed or accepted, performance understood against the correct baseline.
structures.source: all six files, Gate N evidence lines

structures.name: Phase 1 URL classification (existing-asset files)
structures.detail: Classify every URL into exactly: protect | refresh | consolidate | redirect | archive/noindex | retire. Master URL inventory built from every discovery source (never navigation/sitemap alone). Freeze dated raw exports from GSC, GA4, GTM, CRM/backend, paid media, crawlers, backlinks, server logs, performance tools. Capture screenshots/copy/metadata/schema/internal links/conversion components for protected pages. Record defects separately from redesign preferences. Interview operators/sales/support for hidden dependencies and offline URL uses.

structures.name: Shopify-specific trust controls (5) and content controls (5), identical all six
structures.detail: Trust: merchant identity and policies; accurate product/variant/inventory data; shipping/duties/taxes/returns/delivery by market; reviews and product proof; payment security/support/order status. Content: products/collections/pages/blogs; search/filter/merchandising content; market-language localisation; product schema/feed content; post-purchase and retention. NOTE: these blocks also appear duplicated inline earlier in every Phase 1 checklist (template artifact).

structures.name: Shopify platform controls (recurring)
structures.detail: Export products/variants/collections/pages/blogs/menus/redirects/themes/apps/customers-orders-as-permitted/markets/domains/languages/policies/metafields/feeds; audit platform URL constraints, automatic canonicals/sitemaps, tag/filter/search URLs, collection-product paths, app proxy URLs; app register with business value, cost, scripts, data, schema, theme changes, uninstall residue (Phase 1). Phase 2: approve Shopify Markets architecture (primary domain, dedicated domains/subdomains/subfolders, languages, currencies, products, pricing, fulfilment); define theme/Liquid/component and metafield/metaobject architecture before page-builder proliferation; define native-vs-app responsibility for reviews, bundles, subscriptions, search, filters, localisation, feeds, pixels. Phase 3: build a duplicate theme and controlled market configuration - do not edit the live theme directly for a major release; synchronise catalogue/item IDs/inventory/price/currency/shipping/returns/feed/structured data; test Shopify customer events/pixels + GA4 + consent without duplication; import/test URL redirects and update links to final handles. Phase 4: validate Shopify-generated sitemap child files, canonicals, hreflang/Markets behaviour, robots controls; Shopify Web Performance regression by URL/template; test notification emails, inventory, fulfilment, taxes/duties, refunds, gift cards, discounts, customer accounts.

structures.name: Do-not-launch list (7 stop conditions, identical all six)
structures.detail: 1 primary conversion/CRM-order/payment path fails; 2 production indexability, canonicals, sitemap or priority redirects wrong; 3 analytics cannot measure primary outcome or duplicates material events; 4 target market receives wrong language/currency/availability/price/shipping/contact route; 5 critical security/privacy/accessibility/legal issue remains; 6 protected high-value content/links/URLs/proof removed without approved evidence; 7 rollback, owners or command-centre coverage unavailable for a material release.
structures.source: all six files, 'Do not launch or close the release if'

structures.name: AI-agent execution rules (9, identical all six)
structures.detail: 1 select correct workflow before acting; 2 never infer an existing URL/page has no value without checking all discovery and commercial sources; 3 label every finding as observed fact | calculated result | tool estimate | user-provided assumption | recommendation; 4 attach evidence and affected URLs to every issue; 5 no issue closed without retest evidence; 6 escalate conflicts between commercial truth and third-party SEO scores - do not optimise for the score; 7 preserve immutable pre-change exports and screenshots; 8 stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval - do not silently bypass; 9 add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow rather than keeping them only in chat.

structures.name: Overlay phase control and proof matrix (identical all six)
structures.detail: Rows 0-8 with columns Phase | Required work | Evidence | Do not proceed when. Notable stop conditions: P0 open or unaccepted P1 stops release; 'estimates presented as truth' stops phase 1; 'baseline overwritten' stops phase 1; 'production-only edits, untraceable app/plugin/config changes' stops implementation; guardrail breach stops release; 'unexplained material revenue, conversion, indexation or ranking loss' stops stabilization close; 'vanity reporting, no owner, repeated recommendations with no learning' stops phase 8. WARNING: overlay numbering is shifted one phase relative to the base checklist (overlay 3=specify architecture vs base Phase 2; overlay 4=implement vs base Phase 3; overlay 5=QA vs base Phase 4; overlay 6=release vs base Phase 5; overlay 7=stabilization vs base Phase 6; overlay 8 merges base 7+8).
structures.source: all six files, 'Phase control and proof matrix'

structures.name: Exact finding format (12 mandatory fields, identical all six)
structures.detail: 1 issue ID, phase, severity; 2 exact metric/formula and affected dimensions; 3 current value, period, source of truth; 4 comparable own baseline, competitor peer values/percentiles, applicable external benchmark; 5 absolute/relative gap and confidence; 6 affected URLs/products/locations/campaigns/cohorts; 7 likely mechanism supported by corroborating evidence; 8 exact recommendation, owner, dependency; 9 acceptance criteria and automated/manual test; 10 business guardrail, monitoring window, rollback condition; 11 what must not be done; 12 excluded alternatives and why.

structures.name: Competitor and market-share framework (identical all six)
structures.detail: 9 competitor set types built separately: direct, SERP, paid, marketplace, local, publisher, substitute, AI-answer, aspirational. Peer benchmark tiers: median / upper-quartile / leader, using identical market+device+language+period. 7 opportunity classifications: defend, mandatory parity, flank, attack, category-creation, partner, deliberate-ignore. Quantify: addressable demand, attainable share, qualified conversion, contribution, confidence. Archive competitor pages/ads/offers/reviews/SERPs with date+region+source; do not infer spend or performance from an ad library. Cadence: priority competitor panel monthly; complete market map quarterly. Shopify market-share attack patterns: catalog/feed/search/merchandising advantages; remove app/theme friction with measured impact; increase profitable CVR, AOV and repeat purchase by market.
structures.source: all six files, 'Competitor and market-share requirements' + 'Market-share attack patterns'

structures.name: Evidence and completion requirements (identical all six)
structures.detail: Archive raw PDF where useful plus CSV/JSON/crawl/log and configuration; generate SHA-256 manifest and NEVER overwrite baseline evidence; link each closed issue to implementation reference + staging proof + live proof + monitored result; record decisions as included | deferred | not applicable | rejected | unknown | accepted-risk; P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review.
structures.source: all six files, 'Evidence and completion requirements'

structures.name: Required metric panel (10 metrics, identical all six)
structures.detail: Columns: ID | Metric | Source | Target method | Red flag | Improvement path. Rows: COM-001 Revenue (OWN seasonal baseline + ECONOMIC plan); COM-002 Contribution margin (ECONOMIC target by business model); COM-003 Revenue per session (OWN baseline, peer/context only); COM-007 LTV (OWN cohorts, model assumptions documented; red flag LTV:CAC below approved threshold); SEO-006 Indexable URL count (equals approved inventory within explained variance); TEC-004 LCP P75 (Good <=2.5s / needs improvement 2.5-4s / poor >4s, cited [G12]); TEC-005 INP P75 (Good <=200ms / 200-500ms / poor >500ms, cited [G12]); CRO-005 Add-to-cart rate (OWN cohort + product-type peer context); CRO-006 Checkout completion (OWN baseline, peer research context); CRO-008 Return/refund rate (OWN product economics). Benchmark-class vocabulary used: OWN baseline, ECONOMIC target, peer/context, external benchmark [G12].

structures.name: Mandatory do-not-do register (6 prohibitions, identical all six)
structures.detail: 1 no redesign for visual novelty without a measurable user/brand/search/commercial purpose; 2 no delete/redirect of an existing page without master URL and preservation checks; 3 no benchmark whose definition or segment is not comparable; 4 no copying competitor content, claims, creative or dark patterns; 5 no closing work before live evidence and monitoring; 6 no ignored recommendation left unexplained - use the Decision/Exclusion Register.

structures.name: Monitoring cadence ladder (identical core, all six)
structures.detail: Daily during stabilisation: uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives. Weekly for 8-12 weeks: GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, qualified lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links. Monthly: executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing-page performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog; plus Shopify Analytics/Web Performance/search-terms-zero-results/app-theme-changes/market reports. Quarterly: full technical, content, UX/CRO, accessibility, security, competitor, architecture review. Standing alerts: content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change. Track extras: organic files add monthly content-decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor-change reports; landing files add daily spend/sessions/conversion/qualified-outcome/revenue-margin/page-speed/errors while campaigns run. Stabilization comparison windows (overlay): 24h/72h/7d/28d vs pre-release AND seasonal baselines. New-asset files: first stable operating baseline is 4-8 weeks post-launch before normalising targets.
structures.source: all six files, Phases 6-7 + overlay row 7

structures.name: Mandatory tools (16, identical all six)
structures.detail: GSC; GA4+GTM; CRM/backend commercial data; Screaming Frog HTML+JS crawls; Semrush Site Audit/visibility; DataForSEO APIs where automation/scale required; Ahrefs or equivalent backlinks; PageSpeed Insights/CrUX + GTmetrix or WebPageTest; Clarity/Hotjar; accessibility/browser-device/security/uptime tools; Shopify Analytics; Shopify Web Performance; Shopify Markets; Search & Discovery; Merchant Center; theme/app profiling. Rule: add tools only when they have a defined decision or operational use. Overlay: run/archive exact reports specified in TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv with tool/version/configuration, market/device/date, known gaps.
structures.source: all six files, 'Mandatory tools and reports' + 'Required tool/report runs'

structures.name: Per-file deliverable deltas (beyond common 10)
structures.detail: Common 10: Project Charter+classification, market/domain/location matrix, baseline/research pack, KPI baseline-target-guardrail sheet, page/query/audience map, issue register+backlog, analytics/event/attribution spec, QA evidence+signed gate records, launch/post-launch report, monitoring dashboard+CI backlog. 01 adds: proposed business sitemap, proposed XML sitemap specification, content/template inventory. 02 adds: master URL inventory, current sitemap/architecture audit, preservation register, redirect/change map, + the three 01 items. 03 adds: keyword/topic/intent map, technical/content/authority roadmap, editorial and link-earning standard. 04 adds: the four 02 preservation items + the three 03 items. 05 adds: traffic-source/message-match matrix, control/variant and experiment register. 06 adds: the four 02 preservation items + the two 05 items.

structures.name: KPI and guardrail scorecard (13 items, identical all six)
structures.detail: Shopify conversion funnel; net sales and margin; AOV; checkout completion; refund/return; repeat customer rate; market/product/collection profitability; app cost and performance impact; organic clicks/impressions and priority rankings where applicable; indexation and crawl health; CWV by important template; technical error and redirect rate; accessibility/security/privacy closure. Segmentation axes: market, domain/subfolder, language, location, device, source/campaign, page/product/service type.
structures.source: all six files, 'KPI and guardrail scorecard'

structures.name: Track-specific Phase 2/5/6/8 deltas
structures.detail: Store track (01/02) Phase 2 'Site strategy, architecture and specification': full page/template inventory, launch-critical vs phased, governed reusable components. Organic track (03/04) Phase 2 'Organic strategy, architecture and roadmap': 12-month technical/content/authority roadmap; one primary owning page per intent cluster, resolve cannibalisation before expansion; editorial standards (originality, experience, expertise, claims, sourcing, refresh cadence); digital PR/link-earning + local/partner/reputation + internal-link plans. Landing track (05/06) Phase 2 'Offer, message, page and experiment specification': message-match chain from ad/query/referrer to headline/proof/offer/CTA; one primary conversion + minimum qualification data; control/variant, experiment design, sample-size approach and guardrail metrics BEFORE traffic starts. Existing-asset files (02/04/06) add in Phase 2: preservation specification + change-impact register per protected asset; avoid simultaneous changes to URL/intent/content/layout/offer/tracking unless necessary and approved. Phase 5 deltas: 02/04/06 'release with redirect/change map, control metrics and rollback triggers active'; 03/04 'submit/monitor sitemaps and priority URLs, record publication and discovery dates'; 05/06 'launch with previous page/control preserved, confirm traffic allocation'. Phase 6 deltas: existing files compare vs recent AND seasonal baselines; organic files review query/page movement by cohort of changes; landing files review lead/order quality before declaring a conversion winner; all reconcile orders/revenue/discounts/tax/shipping/refunds between platform, analytics, finance. Phase 8 deltas: organic feeds winning queries back into pages; landing tests one hypothesis at a time + experiment learning register.

structures.name: Roles and sign-off table (9 roles, identical all six)
structures.detail: Accountable business owner (commercial outcome, scope, priority, budget, acceptance); Project/product owner (requirements, dependencies, backlog, gates, evidence); SEO/content; Design/UX/CRO; Development/DevOps (implementation, performance, security, deployment, rollback); Analytics/data; CRM/sales/ecommerce operations; Market/legal/privacy owner (localisation, claims, policy, consent, market approval); QA (independent test execution, evidence, retest).

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 0 - Classification, authority and readiness (identical all six)
steps: Assign project ID, accountable owner, workflow file, approvers, evidence folder
Classify business model, asset type, new/existing status, project risk
Record production/staging/legacy/campaign domains; target regions/languages/currencies/locations/legal entities/fulfilment/traffic routing
Define primary commercial outcome, qualified conversion, secondary conversions, guardrails
Record budget, release date, dependencies, blackout periods, rollback authority
Confirm first-party access; identify missing data BEFORE recommendations
GATE 0: Project Charter + access register + market/domain map + outcome definition + risk classification

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 1 - new files: Research and launch baseline / existing files: Discovery and protected baseline
steps: NEW: demand/opportunity baselines; journeys/intents/objections; domain+regional architecture BEFORE content/design; proposed business sitemap + URL policy + page inventory + XML sitemap spec; mark third-party estimates as estimates; document assumptions (no history exists); validate demand before producing the entire asset

EXISTING: freeze dated raw exports (GSC/GA4/GTM/CRM/paid/crawlers/backlinks/logs/perf); master URL inventory from every source; audit current XML sitemap index+children; classify every URL protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire; capture protected-page evidence; pre-change KPI baselines + guardrail thresholds; defects separate from redesign preferences; interview operators

ORGANIC files add: query-topic-page map by intent/funnel/market/language/location; benchmark direct/SERP/publisher/marketplace/local competitors; technical/content/authority/link/reputation/SERP-feature gaps

conflicts: AI-agent rule 9 (all six files): 'Add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow' authorizes agent edits to doctrine; v1 requires doctrine/gate changes via owner ruling (DECISIONS.md) and agent never self-merges. Must be rewritten as propose-only (DIRECTIVES.md/PR + owner approval).

URL disposition classes 'archive/noindex' and 'retire' (02/04/06 Phase 1) and Phase 4/5 robots/DNS/SSL/CDN steps collide with HARD GATES no-deletions and no-DNS/robots-changes: package assigns execution to Development/DevOps role with no owner-only carve-out. Merge must mark retire/noindex/robots/DNS actions as owner-approved, human-executed.

Roles-and-sign-off table (9 human roles) and overlay 'P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review' assume an agency staff v1 does not have; unmapped, this either blocks every launch or gets silently self-signed by the agent - both unacceptable. Requires owner role-mapping ruling.

Phase 5 'Deploy using the approved sequence' with DevOps-role deployment authority could be read as delegating production release; v1 doctrine is owner-only PR merge and human-only DNS flips. Deploy-sequence text must embed those constraints or it weakens HARD GATE i.

No golden_page gate, no design_source mode, no Beauty Gate, no GO-Science audit, no external dual-AI design review anywhere in the six files: adopting them as-is would silently drop five v1 merge-blocking gates (violates R8 and the gates-added-never-weakened rule). Not a package contradiction but a merge-plan obligation: these must be inserted into Phases 2-4 before the Launch Readiness certificate.

'Complete a real primary conversion' (Gates 4-5) on a live Shopify store means a real payment transaction; must be assigned to a human (agent executing purchases/payments is out of bounds), with a refund/cleanup procedure defined.
injection_flags: Every file contains a section explicitly addressed to AI agents ('AI-agent execution rules', 9 numbered rules). Rules 1-8 are procedural descriptions; rule 9 instructs the reading agent to modify shared standards/workflows - if executed literally by an agent ingesting this package it would alter OS doctrine without owner approval. Treated as data, flagged, not acted on.

Overlay preamble in all six files uses directive voice to the executor ('This workflow inherits... The original checklist remains valid') - benign framing but it asserts binding authority over whoever reads it; binding status is the owner's merge decision, not the document's claim.

References to external artifacts the workflows tell the operator to run/consume: TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv ('Run and archive the exact ... reports specified in TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv') and seven ../00_SHARED_STANDARDS/*.md paths. These are passive file references, not URLs or shell commands; nothing in the six files asks an agent to fetch a URL, execute a command, or exfiltrate data. No hidden/encoded text observed.
No claims of pre-authorization, no urgency framing, no credential requests. Overall injection risk of this section: low; only rule 9 needs neutering at merge time.
open_questions: Overlay 'Phase control and proof matrix' numbering is shifted one phase versus the base checklist in the same files (overlay phase 4 = implementation vs base Phase 3 build; overlay 8 covers base Phases 7+8). Which numbering governs the merged OS, and should the matrix be renumbered to match?

Role mapping: who fills the 9 sign-off roles in a solo-owner operation, and what counts as the required 'independent human review' for P0/P1 closure and launch gates - the owner, Dr. Deepu John, a hire, or (not human) the external AI auditors?
Real-conversion launch test on KAPPL: who places and refunds the real order, and is a designated test-payment procedure acceptable evidence?
Phase 1 in every file lists the Shopify trust/content control items twice (inline and again under subheadings) - generation artifact to deduplicate at merge, or intentional two-pass check?
What does the '[G12]' citation on TEC-004/TEC-005 target values resolve to (presumably 06_2026_STANDARDS.md) - confirm the benchmark source so R2 provenance is a real reference, not a dangling one.
TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv vs 01_TOOL_AND_REPORT_REGISTER.md: same artifact or two registers? Which is canonical for the R7 tool/skill map?

Applicability boundary: v1 factory is Next.js/Vercel; these six workflows assume Shopify-hosted stores (themes, Markets, checkout). Do they bind only the KAPPL Shopify track, and do front gates (design_source/golden_page) apply to Shopify theme work in the same form?

Owner ruling needed on approval granularity: package Phase 2 implies several discrete approvals (requirements, IA, Markets architecture, measurement plan); v1 doctrine is one fat strategy approval. Keep fat, or split with multiple signed rows in approvals.yaml?

readings.summary: Six D2C workflow files (01_NEW_WEBSITE, 02_EXISTING_WEBSITE_UPGRADE_MIGRATION, 03_NEW_ORGANIC_PROGRAMME, 04_EXISTING_ORGANIC_GROWTH_RECOVERY, 05_NEW_PRODUCT_OFFER_LANDING_PAGE, 06_EXISTING_PRODUCT_OFFER_LANDING_PAGE_OPTIMISATION; all Version 1.0, Issued 2026-07-19; Workflow IDs D2C-NEW_WEBSITE, D2C-EXISTING_WEBSITE, D2C-NEW_ORGANIC, D2C-EXISTING_ORGANIC, D2C-NEW_LANDING, D2C-EXISTING_LANDING). All six share one skeleton: identical commercial objective/audiences/conversions; 7 inherited shared standards; Phases 0-8 each with named "Gate N evidence" block; identical Phase 0, 4 (core), 5 (core), 6 (core), 7 (core), 8 (core); identical 16-item mandatory tool list; identical 13-item KPI/guardrail scorecard; identical 9-role sign-off table; identical 7-condition "Do not launch or close" list; identical 9-rule AI-agent execution rules; and an appended identical "Version 2 Agency-OS Overlay" (phase control/proof matrix, 12-field finding format, competitor/market-share requirements, evidence requirements incl. SHA-256 manifests, D2C competitive-edge controls, 10-row metric panel with OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC target classes, TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv runs, 6-item do-not-do register). Deltas: NEW variants use Phase 1 "Research and launch baseline" (assumption documentation, validate-demand-first); EXISTING variants use Phase 1 "Discovery and protected baseline" (freeze raw exports, master URL inventory, 6-class URL classification, preservation spec, old-vs-new comparison, regression vs protected baseline, redirect/change map, seasonal-baseline comparison). Website pair adds template inventory/state coverage/catalogue sync; organic pair renames Phases 2-3 to organic strategy/implementation (12-month roadmap, cannibalisation resolution, editorial+link-earning standards, monthly decay/cannibalisation/lost-link reports); landing pair renames Phases 2-3 to offer/message/experiment spec and landing build (message-match chain, control/variant + sample-size before traffic, paid-mobile speed test, one-hypothesis-at-a-time, experiment learning register). The package strongly reinforces v1 doctrine (staging-only, immutable baselines, ask-don't-assume, no self-approval) but four hard-gate frictions exist: agent-facing launch/deploy/Search-Console/robots steps, "retire/archive" URL actions vs no-deletions, a 9-role authority table that could dilute owner-only approval, and no clinical sign-off role. R8 requires the 63-gate registry, beauty, go-science and front gates to be merged INTO this phase skeleton, not replaced by its thinner 7-condition stop list.

Phase 1: NEW variants (01/03/05) 'Research and launch baseline'; EXISTING variants (02/04/06) 'Discovery and protected baseline' -> Gate 1. Phase 2: website pair 'Site strategy, architecture and specification'; organic pair 'Organic strategy, architecture and roadmap'; landing pair 'Offer, message, page and experiment specification' -> Gate 2. Phase 3: website pair 'Design, content, development and integration'; organic pair 'Technical, content, authority and conversion implementation'; landing pair 'Landing-page build and integration' -> Gate 3. Phase 4 'Pre-launch or pre-release QA' -> Gate 4 (signed Launch Readiness certificate; unresolved P0 stops launch). Phase 5 'Launch or controlled release' -> Gate 5. Phase 6 'Post-launch stabilisation' -> 'Stabilisation exit' (critical paths stable; P0/P1 closed or accepted; performance understood vs correct baseline). Phase 7 'Monitoring cadence'. Phase 8 'Continuous improvement loop'.

structures.name: Gate evidence definitions (identical wording)
structures.detail: Gate 0: approved Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, project risk classification. Gate 1: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet. Gate 2: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page or topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog. Gate 3: build/publishing complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps. Gate 4: completed test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1 issues, signed Launch Readiness certificate. Gate 5: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision.
structures.source: all six files, 'Gate N evidence' lines

structures.name: Overlay phase control and proof matrix (identical table, columns: Phase | Required work | Evidence | Do not proceed when)
structures.detail: Do-not-proceed conditions per phase: P0 no owner / unclear denominator / missing commercial source / unauthorized scope; P1 incomplete URL discovery / baseline overwritten / estimates presented as truth; P2 recommendation lacking metric, cause, economics, acceptance criteria or evidence; P3 design changes without purpose or protected-elements list; P4 production-only edits, untraceable app/plugin/config changes; P5 open P0, unaccepted P1, broken conversion/redirect/tracking/backup; P6 guardrail breach or inability to verify live commercial path; P7 unexplained material revenue/conversion/indexation/ranking loss; P8 vanity reporting, no owner, repeated recommendations with no learning. Note: overlay matrix phase numbering is shifted vs body (matrix P4=implement, P5=QA, P6=release, P7=stabilise, P8=monitor, while body has build=3, QA=4, launch=5).
structures.source: all six files, 'Phase control and proof matrix'

structures.name: Exact finding format (12 mandatory fields)
structures.detail: 1 issue ID, phase, severity; 2 exact metric/formula and affected dimensions; 3 current value, period, source of truth; 4 comparable own baseline, competitor peer values/percentiles, applicable external benchmark; 5 absolute/relative gap and confidence; 6 affected URLs/products/locations/campaigns/cohorts; 7 likely mechanism with corroborating evidence; 8 exact recommendation, owner, dependency; 9 acceptance criteria and automated/manual test; 10 business guardrail, monitoring window, rollback condition; 11 what must not be done; 12 excluded alternatives and why.

structures.name: Benchmark classes (metric Target method)
structures.detail: Three classes used in the metric panel Target-method column: OWN (own seasonal baseline / cohorts / product economics), PEER (competitor median then upper-quartile, identical market/device/language/period; also leader values), ECONOMIC (target derived from business-model economics, e.g. CAC linked to contribution/LTV). Peer statistics: median / upper quartile / leader.
structures.source: all six files, 'Required metric panel' + 'Competitor and market-share requirements'

structures.name: Required metric panel (identical 10 rows; columns ID | Metric | Source | Target method | Red flag | Improvement path)
structures.detail: COM-001 Revenue (Finance/backend; OWN seasonal + ECONOMIC plan); COM-002 Contribution margin (Finance; ECONOMIC); COM-003 Revenue per session (Backend+analytics joined; OWN, peer context only); COM-006 CAC (Finance+ad platforms; ECONOMIC linked to contribution/LTV); COM-007 LTV (Finance/CRM; OWN cohorts, assumptions documented); SEO-004 Weighted organic SOV (Semrush/STAT/AccuRanker; PEER median then upper quartile); CRO-005 Add-to-cart rate (Shopify/backend+analytics; OWN cohort + product-type peer context); CRO-006 Checkout completion (Shopify/backend; OWN, peer research context); CRO-008 Return/refund rate (ERP/Shopify/finance; OWN product economics); AI-002 Prompt mention share (Controlled prompt panel; PEER same prompt/model with confidence intervals). ID sequence is sparse (COM-004/005, SEO-001-003, CRO-001-004, AI-001 absent) - full dictionary presumably in shared Metric Dictionary.

structures.name: Competitor set taxonomy (9 types) and opportunity classification (7 types)
structures.detail: Competitor sets built separately: direct, SERP, paid, marketplace, local, publisher, substitute, AI-answer, aspirational. Opportunity classes: defend, mandatory parity, flank, attack, category-creation, partner, deliberate-ignore. Cadence: priority competitor panel monthly; complete market map quarterly. Archive competitor pages/ads/offers/reviews/SERPs with date, region, source; never infer spend/performance from an ad library.
structures.source: all six files, 'Competitor and market-share requirements'

structures.name: Decision/exclusion classification (6 states)
structures.detail: Every decision recorded as one of: included, deferred, not applicable, rejected, unknown, accepted-risk. Companion rule in do-not-do register: 'Do not leave ignored recommendations unexplained; use the Decision/Exclusion Register.'
structures.source: all six files, 'Evidence and completion requirements' + 'Mandatory do-not-do register'

structures.name: URL classification (EXISTING variants, 6 classes)
structures.detail: Classify every URL: protect, refresh, consolidate, redirect, archive/noindex, retire. Built from master URL inventory drawn from every discovery source (never navigation/sitemap alone). Protection triggers: rankings, conversions, backlinks, paid traffic, referral traffic, offline references. For protected pages capture screenshots, copy, metadata, schema, internal links, conversion components.

structures.name: Evidence and completion requirements (overlay)
structures.detail: Archive raw PDF plus CSV/JSON/crawl/log and configuration; generate SHA-256 manifest; never overwrite baseline evidence; link each closed issue to implementation reference + staging proof + live proof + monitored result; P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review. Stabilisation comparison windows: 24h / 72h / 7d / 28d vs pre-release and seasonal baselines.
structures.source: all six files, 'Evidence and completion requirements' + proof matrix row 7

structures.name: Stop-launch conditions (identical 7)
structures.detail: Do not launch or close if: (1) primary conversion, CRM/order or payment path fails; (2) production indexability, canonicals, sitemap or priority redirects wrong; (3) analytics cannot measure primary outcome or duplicates material events; (4) a target market receives wrong language/currency/product availability/price/shipping/contact route; (5) critical security, privacy, accessibility or legal issue remains; (6) protected high-value content/links/URLs/proof removed without approved evidence; (7) rollback, owners or command-centre coverage unavailable for a material release.
structures.source: all six files, 'Do not launch or close the release if'

structures.name: AI-agent execution rules (identical 9)
structures.detail: 1 select correct workflow before acting; 2 never infer an existing URL/page has no value without checking all discovery and commercial sources; 3 label every finding as observed fact / calculated result / tool estimate / user-provided assumption / recommendation (5-class evidence labeling); 4 attach evidence and affected URLs to every issue; 5 no issue closure without retest evidence; 6 escalate conflicts between commercial truth and third-party SEO scores, never optimise for the score; 7 preserve immutable pre-change exports and screenshots; 8 stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval, never silently bypass; 9 add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow, not only chat.

structures.name: Mandatory do-not-do register (identical 6 prohibited shortcuts)
structures.detail: No redesign for visual novelty without measurable user/brand/search/commercial purpose; no delete/redirect of an existing page without master URL and preservation checks; no benchmark whose definition or segment is not comparable; no copying competitor content/claims/creative/dark patterns; no closing work before live evidence and monitoring; no unexplained ignored recommendations (Decision/Exclusion Register).

structures.name: Roles and sign-off table (identical 9 roles; columns Role | Minimum responsibility)
structures.detail: Accountable business owner (commercial outcome, scope, priority, budget, acceptance); Project/product owner (requirements, dependencies, backlog, gates, evidence); SEO/content; Design/UX/CRO; Development/DevOps (implementation, performance, security, deployment, rollback); Analytics/data; CRM/sales/ecommerce operations (revenue truth); Market/legal/privacy owner (localisation, claims, policy, consent, market approval); QA (independent test execution, evidence, retest). No clinical/medical sign-off role exists.

structures.name: Mandatory tools (identical 16) and KPI scorecard (identical 13)
structures.detail: Tools: GSC; GA4+GTM; CRM/backend commercial data; Screaming Frog HTML+JS crawls; Semrush Site Audit/visibility; DataForSEO APIs where automation/scale required; Ahrefs or equivalent backlinks; PSI/CrUX plus GTmetrix or WebPageTest; Clarity/Hotjar; accessibility/browser-device/security/uptime tools; Merchant Center; product-feed tool; reviews/UGC; search and merchandising; email/SMS lifecycle; profit and attribution tools. Rule: add tools only with a defined decision or operational use. KPI scorecard: gross/net revenue, conversion rate, revenue per session, AOV, gross margin, CAC, refund/return rate, repeat purchase + LTV, organic clicks/impressions + priority rankings, indexation and crawl health, CWV by important template, technical error and redirect rate, accessibility/security/privacy closure. Segmentation axes: market, domain/subfolder, language, location, device, source/campaign, page/product/service type.
structures.source: all six files, 'Mandatory tools and reports' + 'KPI and guardrail scorecard'

structures.name: D2C trust controls (5) and content controls (5) - identical across all 6, duplicated inside Phase 1
structures.detail: Trust: clear merchant identity and support; accurate product/ingredient-material/use/safety/suitability information; authentic reviews/UGC and product proof; price/tax/shipping/delivery/return transparency; secure payment and order-support process. Content: product and variant pages; collection/category and use-case pages; comparison/routine-bundle/compatibility content; guides/ingredients-materials/usage/care/safety; shipping/returns/subscription/loyalty/post-purchase content. NOTE: these items appear verbatim two-to-three times per file (inline in Phase 1 checklist AND again as dedicated subsections) - a generation artifact.
structures.source: all six files, Phase 1 + 'D2C-specific trust controls' + 'D2C-specific content controls'

structures.name: D2C competitive edge controls (5) and market-share attack patterns (3) - identical
structures.detail: Capture and test: product/variant and margin; price, offer and delivery; product proof and claims; returns/refunds and repeat purchase; merchant/marketplace visibility. Attack patterns: win profitable product/problem clusters; differentiate offer, proof, merchandising and service; outgrow via retention and contribution, not discount volume.

structures.name: Monitoring cadence (common core + per-type deltas)
structures.detail: Daily during stabilisation: uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives. Weekly for 8-12 weeks: GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, qualified lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links. Monthly: executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing-page performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog. Quarterly: full technical/content/UX-CRO/accessibility/security/competitor/architecture review. Standing alerts: content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change. Organic delta (03/04): monthly content-decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor-change reports. Landing delta (05/06): daily spend/sessions/conversion/qualified-outcome/revenue-margin/page-speed/errors while campaigns run.

structures.name: Continuous improvement loop (7 common steps + deltas)
structures.detail: Collect evidence (users, sales/support, commercial systems, search, crawls, competitors); diagnose constraint and segment (no metric-to-cosmetic jumps); prioritise by business impact/reach/confidence/risk/effort; write hypothesis + acceptance criteria + primary metric + guardrails + owner + rollback; implement ONE controlled change or a clearly documented batch; QA implementation and data before evaluating; adopt/iterate/revert/retire on evidence, record the learning. Organic delta: feed winning queries/objections/sales questions back into pages. Landing delta: one clear hypothesis at a time; maintain experiment learning register.

structures.name: Deltas: 01_NEW_WEBSITE
structures.detail: Phase 1 (Research and launch baseline): demand/opportunity baselines; journeys/intents/objections/proof/conversion paths; domain+regional architecture BEFORE content/design; proposed business sitemap + URL policy + page inventory + XML sitemap spec; baseline targets with third-party estimates marked as estimates; requirements before development; ecommerce integration checklist (catalogue/inventory, cart/checkout/payment/tax/shipping/returns, feed/structured data, reviews/bundles/subscriptions/search-filter/recommendations, lifecycle email/SMS + customer service); validate demand before producing entire asset; document assumptions (no history). Phase 2 extras: full page/template inventory with launch-critical vs phased; nav/internal links mapped to journeys+demand+commercial priority; search/filter/location/utility requirements; reusable governed templates not one-off pages; product/variant/collection/bundle/subscription/upsell/lifecycle journeys with margin guardrails. Phase 3 extras: priority templates with real content early; consistent global header/footer/nav; custom 404/search-zero/loading/error/success/unavailable states; synchronise catalogue/item IDs/inventory/price/currency/shipping/returns/feed/structured data. Phase 4 extras: sample/test every template not only homepage; verify all nav/breadcrumb/footer/contextual destinations; test cart/discounts/tax/shipping/payment-failure/confirmation/refund/market-specific checkout. Phase 6 extras: establish first stable 4-8 week operating baseline before normalising targets; reconcile orders/revenue/discounts/tax/shipping/refunds across platform/analytics/finance. Deliverable deltas: proposed business sitemap; proposed XML sitemap specification; content/template inventory.

structures.name: Deltas: 02_EXISTING_WEBSITE_UPGRADE_MIGRATION
structures.detail: Phase 1 (Discovery and protected baseline): freeze dated raw exports (GSC, GA4, GTM, CRM/backend, paid media, crawlers, backlinks, server logs, performance tools); master URL inventory from every discovery source; audit current XML sitemap index/children + current visual architecture; 6-class URL classification; identify protected pages; capture protected-page components; record current analytics/tag/CRM/forms/payments/feeds/response times; pre-change KPI baselines + launch guardrail thresholds from comparable periods; mark what already works as protected; record defects separately from redesign preferences; interview operators/sales/support for hidden dependencies and offline URL uses. Phase 2 extras: preservation specification + change-impact register per protected asset; avoid simultaneous changes to URL+intent+content+layout+offer+tracking unless necessary and approved. Phase 3 extra: maintain old-vs-new comparison and preserve existing production asset until the new version passes. Phase 4 extra: regression checks against protected baseline; resolve every unexplained loss. Phase 5 extra: release with redirect/change map, control metrics and rollback triggers active. Phase 6 extra: compare with recent AND seasonal baselines, investigate losses by page/segment. Deliverable deltas: master URL inventory; current sitemap/architecture audit; preservation register; redirect/change map where URLs change; proposed business sitemap; proposed XML sitemap spec; content/template inventory.

structures.name: Deltas: 03_NEW_ORGANIC_PROGRAMME
structures.detail: Phase 1 organic additions: product/collection query mapping; Merchant Center and shopping surfaces; product/merchant structured data + feed consistency; editorial-to-commercial internal linking; Image/Lens and review visibility; query-topic-page map segmented by intent/funnel/market/language/location; benchmark direct commercial + SERP competitors + publishers + marketplaces + local results; identify technical/content/authority/internal-link/reputation/SERP-feature gaps. Phase 2 (Organic strategy, architecture and roadmap): 12-month technical/content/authority roadmap with expected business role and dependency; one primary owning page per important intent cluster, resolve cannibalisation before expansion; editorial standards (originality, experience, expertise, claims, sourcing, refresh cadence); digital PR/link-earning + local/partner/reputation + internal-link plans. Phase 3 (Technical, content, authority and conversion implementation): fix technical/indexation/architecture constraints BEFORE scaling content; upgrade priority commercial pages and connect supporting content; publish only after editorial+SEO+factual-claims+link+conversion QA; dashboards branded/non-branded, page type, topic, market, commercial outcome. Phase 4 extras: validate indexability/rendered content/canonicals/schema/internal links per published template; check content differentiation vs actual competing results; reject thin/repetitive production. Phase 5 extra: submit/monitor sitemaps and priority URLs, record publication and discovery dates. Phase 6 extra: review query/page movement, indexation, leads/orders, assisted revenue by cohort of changes; plus 4-8 week baseline (NEW). Deliverable deltas: keyword/topic/intent map; technical/content/authority roadmap; editorial and link-earning standard.

structures.name: Deltas: 04_EXISTING_ORGANIC_GROWTH_RECOVERY
structures.detail: Exact union of 02's protected-baseline machinery and 03's organic machinery: Phase 1 = freeze exports + master URL inventory + 6-class classification + protected capture + organic query mapping + gap benchmarks + operator interviews. Phase 2 = 03's roadmap items + 02's preservation spec + avoid-simultaneous-changes. Phase 3 = 03's + old-vs-new/preserve-production-until-pass. Phase 4 = 03's + regression vs protected baseline. Phase 5 = 03's sitemap monitoring + 02's redirect/change map + rollback triggers. Phase 6 = cohort review + recent AND seasonal baseline comparison (no 4-8 week new-baseline item). Phase 7 adds monthly decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor reports. Deliverable deltas (union): master URL inventory; current sitemap/architecture audit; preservation register; redirect/change map; keyword/topic/intent map; technical/content/authority roadmap; editorial and link-earning standard.

structures.name: Deltas: 05_NEW_PRODUCT_OFFER_LANDING_PAGE
structures.detail: Phase 1 landing additions: match product/variant/price/promotion/audience to campaign; show product evidence/use/delivery/returns BEFORE friction points; sticky purchase CTA where appropriate; measure product view -> variant -> add-to-cart -> checkout -> payment -> purchase; protect margin and qualified purchase, not only conversion rate; traffic-source and audience map (campaign, keyword/ad, creative, email/referrer, region, device, expected intent); page indexability class: SEO indexable / paid-only noindex / evergreen / temporary / controlled test variant; record offer economics, availability, qualification, fulfilment, sales-response capacity. Phase 2 (Offer, message, page and experiment specification): message-match chain from ad/query/referrer to headline/proof/offer/CTA; ONE primary conversion + minimum qualification data; proof/objections/pricing/delivery-response promise/policies/mobile sticky actions; define control/variant, experiment design, sample-size approach, guardrail metrics BEFORE traffic starts. Phase 3 (Landing-page build and integration): fast focused page with limited navigational leakage appropriate to traffic source; form/checkout states, validation, confirmation, CRM routing, remarketing/consent controls; campaign-safe URL, canonical/indexability, Open Graph and sharing metadata. Phase 4 extras: click every ad/email/referral destination and verify message/product/region/language/device/tracking; run real submissions/purchases and confirm source/campaign/value/lead-order status downstream; validate page speed under paid-social mobile network conditions. Phase 5 extra: launch with previous page/control preserved where applicable; confirm traffic allocation. Phase 6 extra: review lead/order quality + sales/fulfilment feedback before declaring a conversion winner; 4-8 week baseline. Deliverable deltas: traffic-source/message-match matrix; control/variant and experiment register.

structures.name: Deltas: 06_EXISTING_PRODUCT_OFFER_LANDING_PAGE_OPTIMISATION
structures.detail: Union of 05's landing machinery and 02's protected-baseline machinery: Phase 1 = freeze exports + master URL inventory + 6-class classification + protected capture + 05's campaign-matching/traffic-source items + operator interviews. Phase 2 = 05's experiment spec + preservation spec + avoid-simultaneous-changes. Phase 3 = 05's + old-vs-new/preserve-production-until-pass. Phase 4 = 05's + regression vs protected baseline. Phase 5 = 05's control-preserved launch + redirect/change map + rollback triggers. Phase 6 = 05's winner-declaration guard + recent AND seasonal comparison (no 4-8 week item). Deliverable deltas (union): master URL inventory; current sitemap/architecture audit; preservation register; redirect/change map; traffic-source/message-match matrix; control/variant and experiment register.

structures.name: Common required deliverables (10, all files)
structures.detail: Project Charter and classification record; market/domain/location matrix; baseline or research pack; KPI baseline/target/guardrail sheet; page/query/audience map appropriate to workflow; issue register and prioritised backlog; analytics/event/attribution specification; QA evidence and signed gate records; launch/post-launch report; monitoring dashboard and continuous-improvement backlog. Per-file deltas listed in each delta structure above.

registers.name: Decision/Exclusion Register
registers.columns: decision state (included | deferred | not applicable | rejected | unknown | accepted-risk) + reason; referenced for every ignored recommendation
registers.purpose: Record disposition of every recommendation/decision; feeds v1 R2 decision provenance and R3 what-to-implement/what-to-reject chains

registers.name: Preservation register / preservation specification
registers.columns: protected asset (URL/copy/layout/CTA/proof/form/link/tracking), captured evidence (screenshots, metadata, schema, internal links, conversion components), change-impact entry
registers.purpose: Guarantee protected high-value assets survive migration; required deliverable in 02/04/06; pairs with change-impact register

registers.name: Master URL inventory
registers.columns: URL, discovery sources, classification (protect | refresh | consolidate | redirect | archive/noindex | retire), commercial signals (rankings, conversions, backlinks, paid, referral, offline references)
registers.purpose: Complete URL universe before any change; prerequisite for any delete/redirect per do-not-do register

registers.name: Redirect/change map
registers.columns: old URL, new URL/action, control metrics, rollback trigger
registers.purpose: Released ACTIVE at Phase 5 with control metrics and rollback triggers in existing-asset workflows

registers.name: Issue register / implementation backlog
registers.columns: issue ID, priority, owner, dependencies, acceptance criteria; findings carry the 12-field exact finding format
registers.purpose: Every change maps to a requirement or issue ID; no closure without retest evidence

registers.name: Control/variant and experiment register + experiment learning register
registers.columns: control/variant definition, experiment design, sample-size approach, guardrail metrics, outcome (adopt/iterate/revert/retire), learning
registers.purpose: Landing-page pair (05/06): experiment governance defined before traffic starts; one hypothesis at a time

registers.name: Access register / access-risk register
registers.columns: first-party system, access status, missing data
registers.purpose: Gate 0 evidence: confirm access to all first-party systems and identify missing data before recommendations

registers.name: TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv (referenced, lives in shared standards)
registers.columns: tool/version/configuration, market/device/date, exact exports, cadence, known gaps
registers.purpose: Exact report runs archived per workflow; overlaps R7 tool/skill map

registers.name: Traffic-source/message-match matrix
registers.columns: campaign, keyword/ad, creative, email/referrer, region, device, expected intent -> headline/proof/offer/CTA
registers.purpose: Landing pair deliverable: message-match chain from source to page

registers.name: Required metric panel
registers.columns: ID | Metric | Source | Target method (OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC) | Red flag | Improvement path
registers.purpose: 10 D2C metrics with defined red flags and improvement paths; IDs from shared Metric Dictionary

registers.name: Mandatory do-not-do register
registers.columns: 6 fixed prohibitions (see structures)
registers.purpose: Prohibited-shortcut list, identical in all six files

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 0 - Classification, authority and readiness (identical in all 6)
steps: Assign project ID, accountable owner, workflow file, approvers, evidence folder
Classify business model, asset type, new/existing status, project risk
Record production/staging/legacy/campaign domains, subdomains, subfolders
Record target regions, languages, currencies, locations, legal entities, fulfilment, traffic-source routing
Define primary commercial outcome, qualified conversion, secondary conversions, guardrails
Record budget, release date, dependencies, blackout periods, rollback authority
Confirm access to all first-party systems; identify missing data before recommendations
GATE 0: Project Charter + access register + market/domain map + outcome definition + risk classification

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 1 - NEW: Research and launch baseline / EXISTING: Discovery and protected baseline
steps: NEW: demand/opportunity baselines; journeys; domain+regional architecture before content/design; proposed sitemap/URL policy/XML spec; estimates marked as estimates; validate demand first; document assumptions

EXISTING: freeze dated raw exports; master URL inventory from every source; sitemap audit; classify URLs protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire; capture protected components; pre-change KPI baselines + guardrail thresholds; defects separate from preferences; operator interviews
All: D2C trust controls (5) + content controls (5); per-type additions (ecommerce integration / organic query mapping / campaign matching)
GATE 1: baseline/research pack + risks + protected assets or assumptions + current-state findings + KPI/guardrail sheet

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 2 - Strategy/specification (title varies: site strategy | organic strategy+roadmap | offer/message/experiment spec)
steps: Common: approve business requirements; approve IA/sitemap/URL rules/navigation/linking model; one primary intent + one primary conversion per important page; page briefs; design system + states; performance budgets + third-party governance; privacy/consent/security/backup/incident requirements; backlog with issue IDs/priority/owner/dependencies/acceptance criteria
Website: template inventory, launch-critical vs phased, governed reusable templates
Organic: 12-month roadmap, one owning page per cluster + cannibalisation resolution, editorial standards, link-earning plans
Landing: message-match chain, one primary conversion + qualification data, control/variant + sample size + guardrails before traffic
EXISTING variants add: preservation specification + change-impact register; avoid simultaneous URL/intent/content/layout/offer/tracking changes
All D2C: map product/variant/collection/bundle/subscription/upsell/lifecycle journeys with margin guardrails
GATE 2: approved blueprint + ownership + domain/region decisions + measurement plan + backlog

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 3 - Build (title varies: design/content/dev/integration | technical/content/authority/conversion | landing-page build)
steps: Common: build ONLY on controlled staging, production indexing blocked, access restricted; semantic HTML/status codes/canonicals/directives/schema; navigation/breadcrumbs/internal links; analytics events/consent/CRM integrations/QA logging; performance budgets/caching/CDN; accessibility behaviours; release notes mapping every change to requirement or issue ID
All D2C: synchronise catalogue, item IDs, inventory, price, currency, shipping, returns, feed, structured data
EXISTING variants add: old-vs-new comparison; preserve existing production asset until new version passes
GATE 3: build complete on controlled environment + release notes + owner checks + no unexplained scope gaps

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 4 - Pre-launch or pre-release QA (core identical)
steps: Four crawls: HTML, JavaScript, XML-sitemap, all-known-URL list
Compare staging vs approved inventory and (existing) vs production baseline
Validate robots.txt, meta robots, X-Robots-Tag, canonicals, status codes, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data
Test primary user tasks across devices/browsers/languages/currencies/networks; forms/calls/WhatsApp/booking/CRM/cart/checkout/payments/email/error recovery
Validate GA4/GTM/pixels, consent, attribution, ecommerce values, backend reconciliation
Field/lab performance, accessibility, security, privacy, visual regression
Migration rehearsal, redirect tests, DNS/SSL/CDN plan, backup and rollback rehearsal
D2C: test cart/discounts/tax/shipping/payment-failure/confirmation/refund/market-specific checkout
EXISTING variants: regression vs protected baseline, resolve every unexplained loss
GATE 4 STOP CONDITION: signed Launch Readiness certificate; unresolved P0 issues stop launch

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 5 - Launch or controlled release (core identical)
steps: Open launch command centre; record exact release time/version and participants
Deploy via approved sequence; preserve rollback path
Immediately validate availability, SSL, robots/noindex, canonicals, priority URLs, redirects, sitemap, analytics
Complete a REAL primary conversion; verify in frontend, backend/CRM, analytics, notifications
Check markets/languages/currencies/locations/availability/traffic-source destinations
Submit/update Search Console sitemaps + feeds (submission is not guaranteed indexing)
Record incidents, owner, resolution, retest evidence
EXISTING: redirect/change map + control metrics + rollback triggers active; Landing: previous control page preserved, traffic allocation confirmed
GATE 5: live validation record + real conversion + incident log + sitemap/feed/ads checks + acceptance or rollback decision
Within 24 hours: full production crawl vs final staging/production baseline
Inspect priority URLs, redirects, sitemap processing, 404/5xx, canonicals, schema, rendering
Monitor commercial + organic signals; compare by template/device/region/language/source/location
Fix P0/P1 regressions immediately; record root cause + preventive control
Stabilisation review + approval before closing launch project
NEW variants: establish first stable 4-8 week operating baseline before normalising targets; EXISTING variants: compare vs recent AND seasonal baselines, investigate losses by page/segment
D2C: reconcile orders/revenue/discounts/tax/shipping/refunds across platform/analytics/finance
EXIT: critical paths stable; P0/P1 closed or accepted; performance understood vs correct baseline
Daily during stabilisation; weekly for 8-12 weeks; monthly scorecard+recrawl; quarterly full review; standing decay/link/redirect/script/privacy/platform alerts
Organic pair: monthly content-decay, cannibalisation, lost-link, competitor-change reports
Landing pair: daily spend/sessions/conversion/qualified-outcome/revenue-margin/speed/errors while campaigns run

Collect evidence -> diagnose constraint (no metric-to-cosmetic jumps) -> prioritise by impact/reach/confidence/risk/effort -> hypothesis with acceptance criteria/guardrails/owner/rollback -> ONE controlled change -> QA implementation and data -> adopt/iterate/revert/retire and record learning
Organic pair: feed winning queries/objections back into pages; Landing pair: one hypothesis at a time + experiment learning register

overlaps.package_item: Phase 0-8 skeleton with Gate 0-5 evidence blocks + stabilisation exit
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 FRONT GATES (brief -> strategy -> design_source -> golden_page -> full build) in launches/<domain>/approvals.yaml + generated per-site checklists

SHA-256 manifests over archived evidence; four-link issue closure (implementation ref + staging proof + live proof + monitored result)

Living competitive intelligence system: 9 competitor set types, 7-class opportunity taxonomy (defend/parity/flank/attack/category-creation/partner/deliberate-ignore), monthly priority panel + quarterly full market map, archived competitor evidence with date/region/source
AI-answer visibility metric AI-002 'Prompt mention share' via controlled prompt panel with confidence intervals
OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC benchmark-class system with per-metric red flags and improvement paths
6-class URL disposition taxonomy (protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire) extending v1 KEEP/MERGE/301

Avoid-simultaneous-changes rule (URL+intent+content+layout+offer+tracking never changed together without approval)
Stabilisation windows 24h/72h/7d/28d and 4-8 week post-launch operating baseline before target normalisation
