conflicts: Phase 5 steps 'Deploy using the approved sequence', 'Submit/update Search Console sitemaps', and robots/noindex validation-and-change work are written as unqualified workflow steps; under v1 HARD GATES the agent makes no production writes, no DNS/robots changes, and production DNS flips are always human. Merge must annotate every Phase 5 execution step as HUMAN-EXECUTES (agent prepares/verifies only). Source: all six files, Phase 5.

URL classification 'retire' and 'archive/noindex' (Phase 1, files 02/04/06) authorizes page removal/deindexing; v1 HARD GATE prohibits deletions by the agent and robots changes. Classification is planning-only; execution requires owner ruling logged in DECISIONS.md. Source: 02/04/06 Phase 1.

Roles and sign-off table grants Development/DevOps deployment+rollback authority, QA independent sign-off, and market/legal approval to roles that do not exist in the v1 operating model (owner is sole approver/merger; agent never self-merges). Adopting the table verbatim would dilute owner-only approval - a gate weakening. Roles must be mapped to actual people with owner retaining all merge/launch authority. Source: all six files, 'Roles and sign-off'.

No clinical sign-off role exists in any D2C workflow; v1 requires Dr. Deepu John sign-off for clinical content, and the package's own trust controls demand 'accurate product, ingredient/material, use, safety and suitability information' (directly clinical for KAPPL Ayurvedic products). The 'Market/legal/privacy owner' role is not equivalent. Clinical sign-off gate must be ADDED to the D2C role/gate set (gates added, never weakened; R8). Source: all six files, trust controls + roles table.

The 7-condition 'Do not launch' list and Launch Readiness certificate are far thinner than the v1 63-gate registry + beauty + go-science + design external review; if the package checklists replace generated per-site checklists, dozens of blocking gates silently disappear. Certificate must be defined as aggregating the v1 blocking gates (R8). Source: all six files, Phase 4/'Do not launch' vs context brief items 2/4/5/6.

'Do not redesign for visual novelty without a measurable purpose' could be invoked against beauty-gate-driven iteration; needs an explicit reconciliation note that BEAUTY_DOCTRINE conformance is a measurable brand/commercial purpose so the beauty gate survives undiluted (R8). Source: all six files, do-not-do register.

Package requires access to systems the factory does not hold for all entities (finance/ERP data, ad platforms, server logs, email/SMS lifecycle tools); running the workflows as written would force either assumption-filling (violating never-invent-facts) or blocked phases. Access gaps must be surfaced at Gate 0 and ASKED per R4, never estimated. Source: all six files, Phase 0/1 + metric panel sources.

Overlay proof-matrix phase numbering is internally shifted versus the body checklist (matrix: 4=implement, 5=QA, 6=release, 7=stabilise, 8=monitor; body: 3=build, 4=QA, 5=launch, 6=stabilise, 7=monitor, 8=improve). Any automation keyed to phase numbers will mis-gate unless one numbering is canonicalised. Source: all six files, 'Phase control and proof matrix' vs body headings.
injection_flags: Every file contains a section titled 'AI-agent execution rules' (9 numbered imperatives) written as direct instructions to an AI agent, plus imperative agent-addressed lines in the overlay ('Stop at phase gates...', 'do not silently bypass', 'Add new learnings to the shared standard'). Content is benign and aligned with v1 doctrine, but per merge discipline these are DATA describing intended agent behaviour, to be re-issued only through the owner's own OS after review - not followed from the package. Present in all six files, identical text.

AI-agent rule 9 instructs the agent to WRITE to shared standards and workflow files ('Add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow'); if executed blindly this is a self-modifying-doctrine channel. Must be gated through v1 DIRECTIVES.md capture + owner ack, consistent with R1's 'never dilute the process while evolving it'.

Files reference relative paths (../00_SHARED_STANDARDS/*.md) and an external file TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv and instruct running 'the exact reports specified' in it; the CSV's contents were not in scope for this reader and should be verified before any agent executes tool runs from it. No URLs, shell commands, credentials or exfiltration vectors found in any of the six files; no hidden/encoded text observed.
open_questions: Role mapping: who fills the 9 sign-off roles for Kairali (solo owner + AI agent + external auditors)? Does 'independent human review' for P0/P1 closure mean the owner, or must a second human be introduced?

Should the clinical sign-off (Dr. Deepu John) be formally added to the D2C role table/gate set for KAPPL ingredient/use/safety/suitability claims, and does it extend to Ayurvedic product efficacy wording on commerce pages?

Metric Dictionary authority: the panel's ID sequence is sparse (COM-004/005, SEO-001-003, CRO-001-004, AI-001 missing) - confirm the shared Metric Dictionary is the master list and the D2C panel is a deliberate subset, so registry rows reference dictionary IDs not file copies.
Deduplication: D2C trust/content control items are repeated verbatim 2-3x inside Phase 1 of every file (inline + dedicated subsections) - dedupe on merge or preserve package text verbatim?
Canonical phase numbering: body (build=3, QA=4, launch=5) vs overlay proof matrix (implement=4, QA=5, release=6) - which numbering becomes canonical for gate IDs and automation?
AI-002 controlled prompt panel: which models, which prompts, what cadence, who owns it - owner decision needed before this metric is operable (also an R1/R7 tool-selection question).

Workflow-to-entity mapping: which of the 6 D2C workflows governs KAPPL's Shopify track (checkout outside the monorepo) vs factory-built commerce sites, and do KTAHV/Villa Raag lead-gen sites use the (unseen) lead-gen/local business-model folders instead of D2C?
Proportionality for landing pages: all 9 phases apply even to a single campaign landing page - is a reduced fast-path permitted for the v1 'landing' class, or is full ceremony mandatory?

R6 specifics: the package orders baseline-before-sitemap but never names the DataForSEO PDF report of the OLD site - confirm it becomes a named Gate 1 deliverable in the EXISTING variants and its old-vs-new values feed the owner's external monitoring tool.

Access reality: finance/ERP, ad-platform, server-log and email/SMS lifecycle data are assumed by the metric panel - which sources actually exist per entity, and which metric rows go 'not applicable' at Gate 0 rather than being estimated?

Launch Readiness certificate form: is it a new signed artifact in launches/<domain>/, and does it formally list the v1 blocking gates (beauty, go-science, design dual-PASS, registry class checklist) as prerequisites?

readings.summary: B2C_OPERATING_MANUAL_2026.md (2,292 lines) contains a short manual header (commercial purpose, competitive-advantage focus, mandatory B2C report pack, workflow-selection rule) plus SIX near-identical workflows: B2C-NEW_WEBSITE, B2C-EXISTING_WEBSITE, B2C-NEW_ORGANIC, B2C-EXISTING_ORGANIC, B2C-NEW_LANDING, B2C-EXISTING_LANDING (all Version 1.0, Issued 2026-07-19). Every workflow shares one skeleton: Phases 0-8 with Gate 0-5 evidence packs, a stabilisation-exit condition, monitoring cadence, continuous-improvement loop, 14 mandatory tools, deliverables, a 12-item KPI/guardrail scorecard, a 9-role sign-off table, 7 stop-launch conditions, 9 AI-agent execution rules, and an identical 'Version 2 Agency-OS Overlay' (phase control/proof matrix with per-phase do-not-proceed stops, 12-field finding format, 9 competitor-set types, 7 opportunity classes, OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC benchmark classes, SHA-256 evidence manifests, 6-value decision classification, 10-metric panel COM/SEO/AI/UX/CRO/LOC, 6-item do-not-do register). Deltas per workflow are limited to Phase 1 (Research-and-launch-baseline for NEW vs Discovery-and-protected-baseline for EXISTING), Phase 2/3 titles+items per asset type (website/organic/landing), a few extra QA/launch/stabilisation/monitoring lines, and deliverable additions (Master URL inventory, Preservation register, Redirect/change map for EXISTING; keyword map+roadmap+editorial standard for ORGANIC; message-match matrix+experiment register for LANDING). The package never mentions v1's beauty gate, go-science, 63-gate registry, front gates (design_source/golden_page), or external AI design review — R8 requires these be relocated into Phases 2-4, not replaced. Several package items (archive/noindex/retire URL class, GSC sitemap submission, launch command centre deploy/DNS/SSL, agent editing shared standards, real test conversions in live CRM) brush against HARD GATES and need owner-only execution rules in the merge.

structures.name: Six B2C workflow IDs and file positions
structures.detail: B2C-NEW_WEBSITE (lines 29-392); B2C-EXISTING_WEBSITE (396-770); B2C-NEW_ORGANIC (775-1145); B2C-EXISTING_ORGANIC (1150-1532); B2C-NEW_LANDING (1537-1906); B2C-EXISTING_LANDING (1911-2292). All: Version 1.0, Issued 2026-07-19. Two axes: asset type (website / organic programme / landing page) x lifecycle (new / existing). Identical across all six: Commercial objective text, primary audiences (individual consumers, family decision-makers, local visitors, patients/guests, influencers/referrers), primary conversions (qualified enquiry, consultation/appointment, booking, call/WhatsApp connection, store/location visit, direct purchase).

structures.name: Manual header: workflow selection rule
structures.detail: "For mixed projects, one workflow is primary and the others are declared overlays; do not silently merge scopes." Mandatory B2C report pack: GSC/GA4/CRM/call/booking baselines; URL+sitemap inventory; competitor SERP/local/offer/UX/reputation analysis; organic and AI SOV; technical crawl/rendering; page and form funnel; response-time and lead-quality; performance/accessibility/security; localization and location health. Measures 'connected calls, consultations, bookings, qualified enquiries, attendance, sale, revisit, referral and review... not button clicks alone'.

structures.name: Mandatory inherited standards (identical in all six workflows)
structures.detail: ../00_SHARED_STANDARDS/00_MASTER_OPERATING_SYSTEM.md, 01_TOOL_AND_REPORT_REGISTER.md, 02_REGIONAL_DOMAIN_LOCATION_FRAMEWORK.md, 03_URL_SITEMAP_MIGRATION_STANDARD.md, 04_MEASUREMENT_ATTRIBUTION_STANDARD.md, 05_QA_LAUNCH_MONITORING_LOOP.md, 06_2026_STANDARDS.md. Overlay additionally 'inherits the Master Agency OS, Competitive Intelligence Playbook, Metric Dictionary, Evidence/Agent Standard, Localization Manual and Monitoring Manual' and states 'The original checklist remains valid; this overlay adds the controls'.

structures.name: Gate evidence definitions (identical wording all six workflows)
structures.detail: Gate 0: approved Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, project risk classification. Gate 1: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet. Gate 2: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page or topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog. Gate 3: build/publishing complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps. Gate 4: completed test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1 issues, signed Launch Readiness certificate ('unresolved P0 issues stop launch'). Gate 5: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision. Stabilisation exit (Phase 6): 'critical paths are stable, P0/P1 regressions are closed or accepted, and performance is understood against the correct baseline.'

structures.name: Overlay: Phase control and proof matrix — do-not-proceed stop conditions
structures.detail: Columns: Phase | Required work | Evidence | Do not proceed when. Stops verbatim: P0 'No owner, unclear denominator, missing commercial source or unauthorized scope'; P1 'Incomplete URL discovery; baseline overwritten; estimates presented as truth'; P2 'Recommendation has no metric, cause, economics, acceptance criteria or evidence'; P3 'Design changes without a purpose or protected-elements list'; P4 'Production-only edits, untraceable app/plugin/config changes'; P5 'Open P0; unaccepted P1; broken conversion/redirect/tracking/backup'; P6 'Guardrail breach or inability to verify live commercial path'; P7 'Unexplained material revenue, conversion, indexation or ranking loss'; P8 'Vanity reporting, no owner, repeated recommendations with no learning'. Note the overlay matrix shifts numbering: matrix P5=launch QA, P6=release via command centre, P7=24h/72h/7d/28d stabilisation compare, P8=monitor/next constraint (vs body phases where 4=QA, 5=launch, 6=stabilisation, 7=monitoring, 8=improvement).

structures.name: Exact finding format (12 mandatory fields)
structures.detail: 1 issue ID, phase, severity; 2 exact metric/formula + affected dimensions; 3 current value, period, source of truth; 4 comparable own baseline, competitor peer values/percentiles, applicable external benchmark; 5 absolute/relative gap and confidence; 6 affected URLs/products/locations/campaigns/cohorts; 7 likely mechanism supported by corroborating evidence; 8 exact recommendation, owner, dependency; 9 acceptance criteria + automated/manual test; 10 business guardrail, monitoring window, rollback condition; 11 what must not be done; 12 excluded alternatives and why.

structures.name: Benchmark classes (target methods) in metric panel
structures.detail: Three classes in caps: OWN (seasonal baseline / cohort / trend), PEER (median then upper quartile; peer-by-location for local), ECONOMIC (economic plan / sales capacity+economics / sales target). Qualifiers used: 'peer/context only', 'industry context + experiment', 'availability caveat' (AI-001). Peer statistics required: median / upper-quartile / leader values recorded 'using identical market, device, language and period'.
structures.source: B2C_OPERATING_MANUAL_2026.md metric panel lines 361-375 and competitor requirements lines 330-338

structures.name: Required metric panel — 10 metrics with IDs (identical 6x)
structures.detail: Columns: ID | Metric | Source | Target method | Red flag | Improvement path. Rows: COM-001 Revenue (Finance/backend); COM-003 Revenue per session (Backend+analytics joined); COM-004 Qualified lead rate (CRM); COM-005 Lead-to-win rate (CRM); SEO-001 GSC clicks (GSC); SEO-004 Weighted organic SOV (Semrush/STAT/AccuRanker); AI-001 Google generative impressions (GSC Generative AI report); UX-001 Task success rate (usability test); CRO-001 Primary conversion rate (Backend/CRM+analytics); LOC-001 Local pack visibility share (Local rank tracker/DataForSEO). Numbering gaps (COM-002, SEO-002/003 absent) imply a master Metric Dictionary elsewhere in the package.

structures.name: Classification chains and label taxonomies
structures.detail: URL classification (existing workflows Phase 1): protect / refresh / consolidate / redirect / archive-noindex / retire. Decision classification (overlay evidence requirements): included / deferred / not applicable / rejected / unknown / accepted-risk. Finding labels (AI rule 3): observed fact / calculated result / tool estimate / user-provided assumption / recommendation. Landing-page indexability status (landing workflows Phase 1): SEO indexable / paid-only noindex / evergreen / temporary / controlled test variant. Severity: P0 (stops launch) / P1 (fix or formally accept); 'P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review'.

structures.name: Competitor and market-share requirements (identical 6x)
structures.detail: 9 competitor set types built SEPARATELY: direct, SERP, paid, marketplace, local, publisher, substitute, AI-answer, aspirational. 7 opportunity classes: defend, mandatory parity, flank, attack, category-creation, partner, deliberate-ignore. Quantify: addressable demand, attainable share, qualified conversion, contribution, confidence. Archive competitor pages/ads/offers/reviews/SERPs with date+region+source; 'do not infer spend or performance from an ad library'. Cadence: priority competitor panel monthly; complete market map quarterly. B2C market-share attack patterns (3): win problem+location demand competitors under-serve; use proof and service design to improve qualified conversion; build referral/revisit/review loops.

structures.name: Evidence and completion requirements (overlay, identical 6x)
structures.detail: Archive raw PDF plus CSV/JSON/crawl/log and configuration; generate SHA-256 manifest and NEVER overwrite baseline evidence; link each closed issue to implementation reference + staging proof + live proof + monitored result; record the 6-value decision classification; P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review. Body AI rule 7 adds: preserve immutable pre-change exports and screenshots.

structures.name: Stop-launch conditions — 'Do not launch or close the release if' (7 items, identical 6x)
structures.detail: 1 Primary conversion, CRM/order or payment path fails. 2 Production indexability, canonicals, sitemap or priority redirects are wrong. 3 Analytics cannot measure the primary outcome or duplicates material events. 4 A target market receives wrong language, currency, product/service availability, price, shipping or contact route. 5 A critical security, privacy, accessibility or legal issue remains. 6 Protected high-value content, links, URLs or proof were removed without approved evidence. 7 Rollback, owners or command-centre coverage unavailable for a material release.

structures.name: Mandatory do-not-do register (6 items, identical 6x)
structures.detail: 1 Do not redesign for visual novelty without a measurable user, brand, search or commercial purpose. 2 Do not delete or redirect an existing page without the master URL and preservation checks. 3 Do not apply a benchmark whose definition or segment is not comparable. 4 Do not copy competitor content, claims, creative or dark patterns. 5 Do not close work before live evidence and monitoring. 6 Do not leave ignored recommendations unexplained; use the Decision/Exclusion Register.

structures.name: AI-agent execution rules (9 rules, identical 6x)
structures.detail: 1 Select the correct workflow before taking action. 2 Never infer an existing URL/page has no value without checking all discovery and commercial sources. 3 Label every finding (5-value taxonomy). 4 Attach evidence and affected URLs to every issue. 5 Do not close an issue without retest evidence. 6 Escalate conflicts between commercial truth and third-party SEO scores; do not optimise for the score. 7 Preserve immutable pre-change exports and screenshots. 8 Stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval; do not silently bypass them. 9 Add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow rather than keeping them only in chat.

structures.name: Roles and sign-off table (9 roles, identical 6x)
structures.detail: Accountable business owner (commercial outcome, scope, priority, budget, acceptance); Project/product owner (requirements, dependencies, backlog, gates, evidence); SEO/content; Design/UX/CRO; Development/DevOps (implementation, performance, security, deployment, rollback); Analytics/data; CRM/sales/ecommerce operations (routing, fulfilment, lead/order quality, revenue truth); Market/legal/privacy owner (localisation, claims, policy, consent, market approval); QA (independent test execution, evidence, retest).

structures.name: KPI and guardrail scorecard (12 items) + segmentation dimensions (identical 6x)
structures.detail: qualified leads; booking/appointment rate; lead-to-sale rate; revenue per session; call connection and qualification; cost per qualified lead; repeat/revisit/referral; organic clicks/impressions and priority rankings; indexation and crawl health; Core Web Vitals by important template; technical error and redirect rate; accessibility/security/privacy closure. Segment by: market, domain/subfolder, language, location, device, source/campaign, page/product/service type.

structures.name: Mandatory tools and reports (14 items, identical 6x)
structures.detail: Google Search Console; GA4 + GTM; CRM/backend commercial data; Screaming Frog HTML and JavaScript crawls; Semrush Site Audit and visibility; DataForSEO APIs where automation/scale required; Ahrefs or equivalent backlink verification; PageSpeed Insights/CrUX plus GTmetrix or WebPageTest; Clarity/Hotjar behavioural evidence; accessibility/browser-device/security/uptime tools; Google Business Profile; call tracking; booking platform; local rank/citation tools. Rule: 'Add tools only when they have a defined decision or operational use.' Overlay adds: run and archive exact reports specified in TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv; record tool/version/configuration, market/device/date, known gaps.

structures.name: Required deliverables — common core (10) + per-workflow deltas
structures.detail: Common: Project Charter and classification record; market/domain/location matrix; baseline or research pack; KPI baseline/target/guardrail sheet; page/query/audience map; issue register + prioritised backlog; analytics/event/attribution specification; QA evidence and signed gate records; launch/post-launch report; monitoring dashboard + continuous-improvement backlog. NEW_WEBSITE adds: proposed business sitemap; proposed XML sitemap specification; content/template inventory. EXISTING_WEBSITE adds those PLUS: Master URL inventory; current sitemap/architecture audit; Preservation register; redirect/change map where URLs change. NEW_ORGANIC adds: keyword/topic/intent map; technical/content/authority roadmap; editorial and link-earning standard. EXISTING_ORGANIC = organic set + Master URL inventory + sitemap audit + Preservation register + redirect/change map. NEW_LANDING adds: traffic-source/message-match matrix; control/variant and experiment register. EXISTING_LANDING = landing set + the four existing-asset artifacts.

structures.name: B2C-specific control blocks (repeated per workflow)
structures.detail: Trust controls (5): clear identity/address/contact/team/credentials; service scope/process/price-range/eligibility/limitations; authentic testimonials/reviews + independently verifiable proof; privacy/cancellation/refund/safety/support info; local credibility, directions, response-time promise. Content controls (5): problem/need pages mapped to service solutions; service/programme/location/practitioner/proof pages; decision content (process, comparison, suitability, FAQs, pricing, next steps); post-service support and retention content; YMYL/health content reviewed and claims controlled. Competitive edge controls (5, overlay): capture+test urgent vs considered journey; call/WhatsApp/booking routing; location/service eligibility; trust/credentials/reviews; lead response and no-show/cancellation. NOTE: trust+content control items are DUPLICATED inside every Phase 1 checklist (inline once, then again under headed subsections) — a generation artifact to dedupe on merge.

structures.name: Asset-type conversion-infrastructure deltas (Phase 1)
structures.detail: WEBSITE workflows: mobile-first contact and booking; accessible forms and confirmation states; CRM routing by service/location/language; call and WhatsApp tracking; location/map/travel/availability integrations. ORGANIC workflows: local and non-local query segmentation; service-location architecture without doorway duplication; Business Profile and review integration; branded/non-branded and symptom/problem-to-service mapping; referral and authority content; query-topic-page map segmented by intent/funnel/market/language/location; benchmark direct commercial/SERP/publisher/marketplace/local competitors; identify technical/content/authority/internal-link/reputation/SERP-feature gaps. LANDING workflows: match campaign/search promise exactly; place phone/WhatsApp/form/booking CTA per urgency; proof near claims and forms; minimise fields while qualifying sufficiently; track response time and sales outcome not only submissions; traffic-source and audience map (campaign, keyword/ad, creative, email/referrer, region, device, expected intent); indexability status decision; offer economics/availability/qualification/fulfilment/sales-response capacity.

structures.name: NEW vs EXISTING Phase 1 delta
structures.detail: NEW ('Research and launch baseline'): demand/opportunity baselines from market research, competitor SERPs, paid data, sales/customer research, business economics; select domain and regional architecture BEFORE content or design production; build proposed business sitemap + URL policy + page inventory + XML sitemap spec; baseline targets marked as estimates; validate demand/proposition before producing entire asset (research/prototypes/limited campaign tests where risk is high); document assumptions since no historical performance exists. EXISTING ('Discovery and protected baseline'): freeze dated raw exports (GSC, GA4, GTM, CRM/backend, paid media, crawlers, backlinks, server logs, performance tools); master URL inventory from EVERY discovery source ('do not rely on current navigation or sitemap alone'); audit current XML sitemap index + child sitemaps + current visual architecture; classify every URL (6-class chain); identify protected pages (rankings, conversions, backlinks, paid/referral traffic, offline references); capture screenshots/copy/metadata/schema/internal links/conversion components of protected pages; record current analytics/tag/CRM/forms/payments/feeds/response times; pre-change KPI baselines + launch guardrail thresholds from comparable periods; mark what already works as protected; record defects separately from redesign preferences; interview operators/sales/support for hidden dependencies and offline URL uses.

structures.name: EXISTING-only additions in Phases 2-6
structures.detail: Phase 2: prepare preservation specification + change-impact register for every protected asset; avoid simultaneous changes to URL, intent, content, layout, offer and tracking unless necessary and approved. Phase 3: maintain old-versus-new comparison and preserve the existing production asset until the new version passes. Phase 4: run regression checks against the protected baseline and resolve every unexplained loss. Phase 5: release with redirect/change map, control metrics and rollback triggers active. Phase 6: compare with both recent AND seasonal baselines; investigate losses by page/segment.

structures.name: Asset-type Phase 2/3 titles and key deltas
structures.detail: WEBSITE P2 'Site strategy, architecture and specification' / P3 'Design, content, development and integration' (build all priority templates with real content early; custom 404/search-zero/loading/error/success/unavailable states). ORGANIC P2 'Organic strategy, architecture and roadmap' (12-month technical/content/authority roadmap; one primary owning page per intent cluster, resolve cannibalisation before expansion; editorial standards for originality/experience/expertise/claims/sourcing/refresh; digital PR/link-earning, local/partner/reputation, internal-link plans) / P3 'Technical, content, authority and conversion implementation' (fix technical/indexation constraints BEFORE scaling content; publish only after editorial+SEO+factual/claims+link+conversion QA; dashboards by branded/non-branded, page type, topic, market, commercial outcome). LANDING P2 'Offer, message, page and experiment specification' (message-match chain ad/query/referrer → headline/proof/offer/CTA; ONE primary conversion + minimum qualification data; control/variant, experiment design, sample-size approach, guardrail metrics defined BEFORE traffic starts) / P3 'Landing-page build and integration' (fast focused page, limited navigational leakage; campaign-safe URL/canonical/OG decisions). All asset types share: 'Map urgent versus considered journeys and select call, WhatsApp, form, booking or purchase CTA accordingly' and 'Route enquiries by location/service/language and record response-time ownership'.

structures.name: Asset-type QA/launch/stabilisation/monitoring deltas (Phases 4-8)
structures.detail: WEBSITE P4: sample and test EVERY template not only homepage; verify all navigation/breadcrumb/footer/contextual-link destinations. ORGANIC P4: validate indexability/rendered content/canonicals/schema/internal links per published template; check content differentiation against actual competing results — reject thin or repetitive production. LANDING P4: click every ad/email/referral destination and verify message/product/region/language/device/tracking; run real submissions/purchases and confirm source/campaign/value/lead-order status downstream; validate page speed under paid-social mobile network conditions. ORGANIC P5: record publication and discovery dates. LANDING P5: previous page/control preserved, confirm traffic allocation. P6 deltas: website — 4-8 week operating baseline before normalising targets; organic — query/page movement by change cohort; landing — review lead/order quality before declaring a conversion winner. P7 deltas: organic — monthly content-decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor-change reports; landing — daily spend/sessions/conversion/revenue-margin/speed/errors while campaigns run. P8 deltas: organic — feed winning queries/objections/sales questions back; landing — one hypothesis at a time + experiment learning register.

structures.name: Monitoring cadence + windows (identical core, all six)
structures.detail: Daily during stabilisation: uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives. Weekly for 8-12 weeks: GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, qualified lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links. Monthly: executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog. Quarterly: full technical/content/UX-CRO/accessibility/security/competitor/architecture review. Standing alerts: content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change. Overlay stabilisation windows: compare 24h/72h/7d/28d results with pre-release and seasonal baselines. Post-launch: full production crawl within 24 hours vs final staging/production baseline. First stable operating baseline: 4-8 weeks post-launch.

structures.name: Continuous improvement loop (7 steps, identical core)
structures.detail: 1 Collect evidence (users, sales/support, commercial systems, search, crawls, competitors). 2 Diagnose constraint and affected segment; do not jump from a metric to a cosmetic solution. 3 Prioritise by business impact, reach, confidence, risk, effort. 4 Write hypothesis, acceptance criteria, primary metric, guardrails, owner, rollback. 5 Implement one controlled change or a clearly documented batch. 6 QA the implementation and data before evaluating performance. 7 Adopt, iterate, revert or retire based on evidence; record the learning.

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 0 - Classification, authority and readiness (identical all six)
steps: Assign project ID, accountable owner, workflow file, approvers, evidence folder
Classify business model, asset type, new/existing status, project risk
Record production/staging/legacy/campaign domains, subdomains, subfolders
Record target regions, languages, currencies, locations, legal entities, fulfilment, traffic-source routing
Define primary commercial outcome, qualified conversion, secondary conversions, guardrails
Record budget, release date, dependencies, blackout periods, rollback authority
Confirm access to all first-party systems; identify missing data BEFORE recommendations
GATE 0 evidence: Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, risk classification

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 1 - Research and launch baseline (NEW) / Discovery and protected baseline (EXISTING)
steps: NEW: demand/opportunity baselines; journeys/intents/objections/proof/conversion paths; domain+regional architecture before content/design; proposed sitemap+URL policy+page inventory+XML spec; targets from realistic benchmarks with estimates marked; tracking/CRM/feed/local/security/accessibility requirements; validate demand before full production; document assumptions

EXISTING: freeze dated raw exports; master URL inventory from every discovery source; sitemap audit + visual architecture; classify every URL protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire; identify+capture protected pages; record current analytics/CRM/forms/payments/response times; pre-change KPI baselines + guardrail thresholds; mark working assets protected; defects separate from redesign preferences; interview operators
Plus per-asset-type control blocks (website/organic/landing) + B2C trust controls (5) + B2C content controls (5, incl. YMYL/health claims control)
GATE 1 evidence: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 2 - Strategy/specification (title varies: Site strategy | Organic strategy+roadmap | Offer/message/page/experiment spec)
steps: Approve business requirements, audience, message, offer, differentiation, success measures
Approve IA, proposed sitemap, URL naming rules, navigation, search/filter, internal-linking model
Map ONE primary search intent + ONE primary conversion objective per important page
Page briefs: protected content, proof, CTA, schema, media, localisation, analytics, owner
Design system, accessibility, content components, all loading/error/empty/success states
Performance budgets by template + third-party script/app governance
Privacy, consent, security, backup, access, incident-response requirements
Implementation backlog with issue IDs, priority, owner, dependencies, acceptance criteria

Asset-type extras (12-month roadmap / cannibalisation / message-match chain / experiment design before traffic); EXISTING extras (preservation spec + change-impact register; avoid simultaneous URL+intent+content+layout+offer+tracking changes)
GATE 2 evidence: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page/topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 3 - Build/implementation (title varies by asset type)
steps: Build ONLY on controlled staging with production indexing blocked and access restricted
Semantic HTML, crawlable links, status codes, canonicals, directives, schema, responsive media
Navigation, breadcrumbs, contextual internal links, cross-market selectors
Analytics events, consent, CRM/backend integrations, QA logging
Performance budgets, image/font strategy, caching, CDN, third-party controls
Accessible keyboard/focus/form/modal/error behaviour
Release notes; every change mapped to a requirement or issue ID
Asset-type extras; EXISTING extra: old-vs-new comparison, preserve production asset until new version passes
GATE 3 evidence: build complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 4 - Pre-launch or pre-release QA (identical core)
steps: HTML crawl + JavaScript crawl + XML sitemap crawl + all-known-URL list crawl
Compare staging vs approved page inventory (and vs production baseline for existing)
Validate robots.txt, meta robots, X-Robots-Tag, canonicals, status codes, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data
Test every primary user task on target devices/browsers/languages/currencies/network conditions
Test forms, calls, WhatsApp, booking, CRM, search, account, cart, checkout, payments, email, error recovery
Validate GA4/GTM/pixels, consent, attribution, ecommerce values, backend reconciliation
Field/lab performance, accessibility, security, privacy, visual regression tests
Migration rehearsal, redirect tests, DNS/SSL/CDN plan, backup and rollback rehearsal
Signed Launch Readiness certificate; UNRESOLVED P0 ISSUES STOP LAUNCH
Asset-type extras; EXISTING extra: regression vs protected baseline, resolve every unexplained loss
GATE 4 evidence: test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1, signed certificate

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 5 - Launch or controlled release (identical core)
steps: Open launch command centre; record exact release time/version and responsible participants
Deploy via approved sequence; preserve rollback path
Immediately validate availability, SSL, robots/noindex, canonicals, priority URLs, redirects, sitemap, analytics
Complete a REAL primary conversion; verify in frontend, backend/CRM, analytics, notifications
Check markets, languages, currencies, locations, availability, traffic-source destinations
Submit/update GSC sitemaps and platform/feed destinations; submission is not guaranteed indexing
Record incidents, owner, resolution, retest evidence
EXISTING extra: redirect/change map + control metrics + rollback triggers active; LANDING extra: control preserved + traffic allocation
GATE 5 evidence: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision
Full production crawl within 24 hours vs final baseline
Inspect priority URLs, redirect sources, sitemap processing, 404/5xx, canonicals, schema, rendering
Monitor transactions/forms, qualified conversions, revenue, paid destinations, feeds, support incidents
Monitor organic clicks/impressions, rankings, indexed priority pages, crawl activity, backlink destinations
Compare performance/conversion by template, device, region, language, source, location
Fix P0/P1 regressions immediately; record root cause + preventive control
Stabilisation review + approval before closing the launch project; 4-8 week operating baseline (new assets); review connected calls/enquiries/bookings/no-show, not button clicks
STABILISATION EXIT: critical paths stable, P0/P1 closed or accepted, performance understood vs correct baseline
Daily during stabilisation: uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives
Weekly for 8-12 weeks: GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links
Monthly: executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog
Quarterly: full technical/content/UX-CRO/accessibility/security/competitor/architecture review
Standing alerts: content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change
Asset-type extras: organic monthly decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor reports; landing daily spend-to-margin while campaigns run

Collect evidence → diagnose constraint (no metric-to-cosmetic jumps) → prioritise by impact/reach/confidence/risk/effort → hypothesis with acceptance criteria/primary metric/guardrails/owner/rollback → ONE controlled change or documented batch → QA implementation and data first → adopt/iterate/revert/retire and record the learning
Asset-type extras: organic feeds winning queries back into pages; landing keeps experiment learning register, one hypothesis at a time

workflow_skeleton.phase: Version 2 Agency-OS Overlay (appended verbatim to each of the six workflows)
steps: Phase control and proof matrix (phases 0-8, each with required work / evidence / do-not-proceed stop)
Exact finding format (12 fields)
Competitor and market-share requirements (9 set types, 7 opportunity classes, monthly panel / quarterly map)
Evidence and completion requirements (SHA-256 manifests, never overwrite baseline, 6-value decision classification, independent human review for P0/P1 + launch gates)
B2C-specific competitive edge controls (5) + market-share attack patterns (3)
Required metric panel (10 metrics, OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC target methods)
Required tool/report runs (TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv, record tool/version/config/market/device/date/gaps)
Mandatory do-not-do register (6)

registers.name: Required metric panel
registers.columns: ID | Metric | Source | Target method | Red flag | Improvement path
registers.purpose: Per-workflow mandatory metric set (COM-001/003/004/005, SEO-001/004, AI-001, UX-001, CRO-001, LOC-001) with OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC benchmark classes

registers.name: Phase control and proof matrix
registers.columns: Phase | Required work | Evidence | Do not proceed when
registers.purpose: Overlay gate table for phases 0-8 with explicit stop conditions per phase

registers.name: Roles and sign-off
registers.columns: Role | Minimum responsibility
registers.purpose: 9-role RACI-lite for gate sign-off; QA independent; P0/P1 closure needs independent human review

registers.name: Decision/Exclusion Register
registers.columns: not defined in this file (referenced; likely defined in a shared standard)
registers.purpose: Records ignored/rejected recommendations with reasons; backs finding-format field 12 (excluded alternatives and why) — direct R2 provenance vehicle

registers.name: Preservation register (+ preservation specification, change-impact register)
registers.columns: implied: protected URLs, copy, layouts, CTAs, proof, forms, links, tracking + screenshots/metadata/schema captures
registers.purpose: EXISTING-asset deliverable protecting live value; feeds stop-launch condition 6 and do-not-do rule 2 — package cousin of v1 PROTECTION MAP

registers.name: Master URL inventory + redirect/change map
registers.columns: URL + 6-class disposition (protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire) + discovery sources

registers.name: Issue register and prioritised backlog
registers.columns: 12-field finding format; backlog rows carry issue ID, priority, owner, dependencies, acceptance criteria
registers.purpose: Single structured store for findings and implementation work; every change maps to a requirement or issue ID

registers.name: Control/variant and experiment register (+ experiment learning register)

registers.name: Access register
registers.columns: not detailed

registers.name: TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv (referenced external file)
registers.columns: not shown in this file

registers.name: Traffic-source/message-match matrix
registers.columns: campaign, keyword/ad, creative, email/referrer, region, device, expected intent → page/message
registers.purpose: Landing-page deliverable ensuring ad-to-page message match

overlaps.package_item: Phase 0-8 lifecycle with Gate 0-5 evidence packs (all six B2C workflows)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 FRONT GATES (brief → strategy → design_source → golden_page → full build) + launches/<domain>/ checklists generated from gates/registry.yaml
overlaps.note: Package phases are the macro project spine; v1 front gates map inside it (brief≈Gate 0, strategy≈Gates 1-2, design_source+golden_page must be INSERTED into Phases 2-3 — package has no design-approval or golden-page step at all).

overlaps.package_item: Gate evidence folders, 'evidence folder' assignment at Phase 0, signed gate records deliverable
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 EVIDENCE LAW — launches/<domain>/ committed to git, 'if it isn't in the repo, it didn't happen', append-only, IST timestamps
overlaps.note: Adopt package evidence lists as the content spec; keep v1 storage law (git, append-only, timestamps) as the physical implementation.

overlaps.package_item: Overlay evidence requirements: SHA-256 manifests, never overwrite baseline, raw PDF+CSV/JSON/crawl/log archives
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 content-mined/ immutability + append-only audit passes
overlaps.note: Strict superset of v1; SHA-256 manifest generation is new and strengthens immutability.

overlaps.package_item: 'Build only on controlled staging with production indexing blocked'; overlay P4 stop 'Production-only edits, untraceable app/plugin/config changes'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE 1 (no production writes) + staging-only doctrine
overlaps.note: Fully consistent; adds an explicit merge-blocking phrasing for untraceable config changes.

overlaps.package_item: AI rule 3: label every finding observed fact / calculated result / tool estimate / user-provided assumption / recommendation; P1 stop 'estimates presented as truth'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE: never invent facts/IDs/prices (gaps ASKED not filled) + R4 ask-when-in-doubt
overlaps.note: Operationalizes the v1 rule into a 5-value label taxonomy; adopt as the standard finding vocabulary.

overlaps.package_item: AI rule 8: stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval, never silently bypass; 'P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE: agent never self-merges/self-approves; owner-only bypass, logged
overlaps.note: Compatible, but v1 wording is stricter and names the owner; keep v1 as governing text, cite package rule as reinforcement.

overlaps.package_item: 'Do not launch or close the release if' 7 stop-launch conditions
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 63-gate registry merge-blocking rows + PROOF-OF-WORK (no 'done' without working URL/real output)
overlaps.note: Convert the 7 conditions into registry gates with required|adapted|n_a per site class; gates added never weakened (R8-safe direction).

overlaps.package_item: Mandatory do-not-do register (6 rules incl. no visual-novelty redesign, no page delete/redirect without preservation checks, no dark patterns)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 HARD GATE no deletions + BUILD DECISION MATRIX PROTECTION MAP + BEAUTY doctrine's purpose-driven design
overlaps.note: Adopt all 6; but v1 is stricter on deletion (agent NEVER deletes — preservation checks do not license agent deletion) — record that hierarchy explicitly.

overlaps.package_item: EXISTING Phase 1: master URL inventory from every discovery source + 6-class URL classification (protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire) + protected-page capture
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 BUILD DECISION MATRIX: MINE FIRST full inventory + PROTECTION MAP (KEEP/MERGE/301)
overlaps.note: Package chain is richer; map KEEP→protect, MERGE→consolidate, 301→redirect, and ADD refresh/archive-noindex/retire — but archive-noindex/retire decisions are owner-ruled and human-executed (HARD GATES: no deletions, no robots changes).

overlaps.package_item: EXISTING Phase 1 freeze of dated raw exports (GSC, GA4, GTM, CRM, paid, crawls, backlinks, logs, performance) BEFORE Phase 2 sitemap approval; DataForSEO in mandatory tools
overlaps.existing_mechanism: R6 BASELINE-BEFORE-SITEMAP (DataForSEO PDF of old site before new sitemap) — currently a requirement, not yet a mechanism
overlaps.note: Package sequencing satisfies R6 structurally; add the specific DataForSEO PDF report as a named Gate 1 artifact and feed old-vs-new values to the owner's monitoring tool.

overlaps.package_item: Exact finding format field 12 (excluded alternatives and why) + Decision/Exclusion Register + 6-value decision classification (included/deferred/n-a/rejected/unknown/accepted-risk)

Per-phase 'do not proceed when' stop conditions (proof matrix) covering all 9 phases — more granular than v1's front gates.
12-field exact finding format including 'what must not be done' and 'excluded alternatives and why' — a ready-made R2 decision-provenance record.
OWN / PEER / ECONOMIC benchmark-class system with peer median → upper-quartile → leader percentiles under identical market/device/language/period.

9-type competitor set taxonomy (direct, SERP, paid, marketplace, local, publisher, substitute, AI-answer, aspirational) + 7 opportunity classes (defend, mandatory parity, flank, attack, category-creation, partner, deliberate-ignore) + monthly panel / quarterly map cadence.
SHA-256 evidence manifests with never-overwrite baseline rule.
6-value decision classification (included/deferred/not applicable/rejected/unknown/accepted-risk) and Decision/Exclusion Register.
5-value finding-label taxonomy (observed fact / calculated result / tool estimate / user-provided assumption / recommendation).
6-class URL disposition chain (protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire) extending v1's KEEP/MERGE/301.

Controlled experiment framework for landing pages: control/variant, sample-size approach, guardrail metrics defined before traffic; experiment learning register; declare-winner only after lead/order-quality review.
Formal stabilisation windows (24h/72h/7d/28d) and 4-8-week post-launch operating baseline before targets are normalised.
AI-visibility metric AI-001 (Google generative impressions from the GSC Generative AI report) as a standing panel metric.
B2C-specific control blocks: 5 trust controls, 5 content controls (incl. YMYL claims control hook), 5 competitive-edge capture-and-test controls, 3 market-share attack patterns.
Message-match chain specification (ad/query/referrer → headline/proof/offer/CTA) and traffic-source/message-match matrix deliverable.
Urgent-vs-considered journey mapping with CTA selection (call/WhatsApp/form/booking/purchase) and response-time ownership recording.
Launch Readiness certificate + launch command centre + real-conversion live verification as named launch artifacts.
Preservation specification + change-impact register + 'avoid simultaneous changes to URL, intent, content, layout, offer and tracking' rule for existing assets.
conflicts: R8 dilution risk: the package's six B2C workflows contain NO beauty gate, NO go-science audit, NO design external AI review (ChatGPT+Perplexity dual-PASS), NO front-gate approvals.yaml (design_source MODE A/B, golden_page), and no reference to the 63-gate registry. Adopting the package workflow layer as-is would silently drop these — they must be relocated into Phases 2-4 with merge-blocking force preserved.

URL classes 'archive/noindex or retire' and landing class 'paid-only noindex' authorize indexing-directive changes and page retirement; HARD GATES forbid agent robots changes and any deletions. Merge must mark these dispositions owner-ruled and human-executed (DECISIONS.md), never agent-executable.

Phase 5 launch command centre includes deploy, DNS/SSL/CDN plan and GSC sitemap submission; v1: production DNS flips are always human, no DNS changes by agent, plus the known GSC two-account trap. Each command-centre step needs an explicit executor column (human vs agent-verify-only).

Phase 5 'complete a REAL primary conversion' and landing Phase 4 'run real submissions/purchases' write real records into production CRM/booking/payment systems — brushes HARD GATE no-production-writes; requires an owner-defined flagged-test-record protocol with humans executing payment/booking steps.

Roles table lets 'Development/DevOps' own deployment and 'QA' independently certify; in a solo-owner + agent operation the agent could end up as author+deployer+QA, violating v1's separation (agent never self-merges/self-approves; independent review). Role-to-person binding required before adoption.

AI-agent rule 9 instructs the agent to modify shared standards and workflow files directly; v1 requires gate changes via owner-approved PRs, registry rules owner-ruled, gates added never weakened. Must be rewritten as 'propose via PR; owner merges'.

Package generic 'Market/legal/privacy owner' replaces v1's NAMED clinical authority (Dr. Deepu John) for YMYL/health content; keeping only the generic role would weaken the clinical HARD GATE for KTAHV.

Package severity model (P0 stop / P1 fix-or-accept, with 'unaccepted P1' blocking launch but P1 acceptance allowed) is looser than v1's binary merge-blocking gates; mapping P1-acceptance authority must rest with the owner or it weakens gate force.

Landing experiment framework presumes design variants can be produced; v1 current state has designs FROZEN — experiments require an explicit owner unfreeze ruling, otherwise workflow steps are unexecutable.
injection_flags: Six identical 'AI-agent execution rules' blocks (lines 282-292, 661-671, 1036-1046, 1423-1433, 1797-1807, 2183-2193) are imperative second-person-style instructions addressed to an AI agent ('Select the correct workflow before taking action', 'Stop at phase gates...'). Content is benign and largely v1-aligned, but they are direct agent directives inside DATA and must be re-issued through the merged OS, not obeyed from the package. Rule 9 in particular instructs the agent to edit shared standards/workflow files — acting on it verbatim would bypass v1's owner-merge control.

Repeated 'This workflow must be used with: ../00_SHARED_STANDARDS/...' blocks instruct the reader/agent to load seven other package files; treat as cross-references to analyze, not load-and-obey chains.

References to executing/archiving 'the exact... reports specified in TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv' delegate tool-run authority to an external CSV not yet reviewed — do not run anything it lists until the CSV is ingested and owner-approved (R7 audit).

No URLs, shell commands, credentials, or fetch-and-execute payloads found anywhere in the file; no hidden/encoded text observed. Overall injection risk: low, but the direct-address agent-rule blocks and the external CSV delegation should be neutralized (rewritten as merged-OS doctrine) before any agent operates from this package.

readings.summary: B2B_OPERATING_MANUAL_2026.md (2298 lines) = manual header (commercial purpose, competitive-advantage focus, mandatory B2B report pack, workflow-selection rule) + SIX workflows, each Version 1.0 / Issued 2026-07-19: B2B-NEW_WEBSITE, B2B-EXISTING_WEBSITE, B2B-NEW_ORGANIC, B2B-EXISTING_ORGANIC, B2B-NEW_LANDING, B2B-EXISTING_LANDING. All six share one Phase 0-8 skeleton (Gate 0-5 evidence blocks, stabilisation exit, monitoring cadence, improvement loop), an identical 15-item mandatory tool list, 13-item B2B KPI scorecard, 9-role sign-off table, 7 stop-launch conditions, 9 AI-agent execution rules, and an identical appended V2 Agency-OS Overlay (phase control/proof matrix, 12-field finding format, competitor/market-share requirements, SHA-256 evidence rules, B2B edge controls, 9-metric panel, do-not-do register). Differences between the six are small, systematic deltas: NEW vs EXISTING changes Phase 1 (research baseline vs protected baseline + preservation), and website/organic/landing changes Phase 2/3 focus plus a few extra deliverables. The package is workflow doctrine compatible with v1 in spirit (staging-only, evidence, human gates, never-invent) but contains no design/beauty/go-science/golden-page gates of its own — v1 gates must be relocated in, not replaced (R8). Main conflicts: Phase 5 deploy/DNS/robots/GSC tasks and the "real primary conversion" live test must be re-assigned to human-only under HARD GATES; the 9-role table and AI-agent rule 9 (agent edits shared standards) must be constrained to owner-approval reality. Notable defect: Phase 1 trust/content control items are duplicated verbatim inside each workflow (mechanical template assembly) — dedupe on merge.

structures.name: Phase/gate naming and order (common skeleton)
structures.detail: Phase 0 'Classification, authority and readiness' -> Gate 0. Phase 1 'Research and launch baseline' (NEW variants) / 'Discovery and protected baseline' (EXISTING variants) -> Gate 1. Phase 2 'Site strategy, architecture and specification' (website) / 'Organic strategy, architecture and roadmap' (organic) / 'Offer, message, page and experiment specification' (landing) -> Gate 2. Phase 3 'Design, content, development and integration' (website) / 'Technical, content, authority and conversion implementation' (organic) / 'Landing-page build and integration' (landing) -> Gate 3. Phase 4 'Pre-launch or pre-release QA' -> Gate 4. Phase 5 'Launch or controlled release' -> Gate 5. Phase 6 'Post-launch stabilisation' -> Stabilisation exit. Phase 7 'Monitoring cadence'. Phase 8 'Continuous improvement loop'.

structures.name: Gate evidence definitions (identical wording in all 6)
structures.detail: Gate 0: approved Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, project risk classification. Gate 1: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet. Gate 2: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page or topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog. Gate 3: build/publishing complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps. Gate 4: completed test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1 issues, signed Launch Readiness certificate. Gate 5: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision. Stabilisation exit: critical paths stable, P0/P1 regressions closed or accepted, performance understood against the correct baseline.

structures.name: Stop condition inside Phase 4
structures.detail: "Obtain signed Launch Readiness certificate; unresolved P0 issues stop launch." P0 = absolute stop; P1 may only be explicitly accepted (overlay Phase 5 row: 'Open P0; unaccepted P1' blocks).
structures.source: B2B_OPERATING_MANUAL_2026.md line 156 et al.; overlay row 5

structures.name: Do-not-launch list (7 stop-launch conditions, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: 1 Primary conversion, CRM/order or payment path fails. 2 Production indexability, canonicals, sitemap or priority redirects wrong. 3 Analytics cannot measure primary outcome or duplicates material events. 4 A target market receives wrong language/currency/product availability/price/shipping/contact route. 5 Critical security, privacy, accessibility or legal issue remains. 6 Protected high-value content, links, URLs or proof removed without approved evidence. 7 Rollback, owners or command-centre coverage unavailable for a material release.

structures.name: AI-agent execution rules (9, identical in all 6)
structures.detail: 1 Select the correct workflow before acting. 2 Never infer an existing URL/page has no value without checking all discovery and commercial sources. 3 Label every finding as observed fact | calculated result | tool estimate | user-provided assumption | recommendation. 4 Attach evidence and affected URLs to every issue. 5 No issue closed without retest evidence. 6 Escalate conflicts between commercial truth and third-party SEO scores; do not optimise for the score. 7 Preserve immutable pre-change exports and screenshots. 8 Stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval; do not silently bypass. 9 Add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow rather than keeping them only in chat.

structures.name: V2 overlay - Phase control and proof matrix (identical 6x)
structures.detail: 9 rows (phases 0-8), columns: Phase | Required work | Evidence | Do not proceed when. Key do-not-proceed conditions verbatim: P0 'No owner, unclear denominator, missing commercial source or unauthorized scope'; P1 'Incomplete URL discovery; baseline overwritten; estimates presented as truth'; P2 'Recommendation has no metric, cause, economics, acceptance criteria or evidence'; P3 'Design changes without a purpose or protected-elements list'; P4 'Production-only edits, untraceable app/plugin/config changes'; P5 'Open P0; unaccepted P1; broken conversion/redirect/tracking/backup'; P6 'Guardrail breach or inability to verify live commercial path'; P7 'Unexplained material revenue, conversion, indexation or ranking loss'; P8 'Vanity reporting, no owner, repeated recommendations with no learning'. Note overlay phase numbering shifts execution to phase 4 and release to phase 6 vs the base checklist (build=3, launch=5) — an internal inconsistency of the package.

structures.name: Exact finding format (12 mandatory fields)
structures.detail: 1 issue ID, phase, severity; 2 exact metric/formula + affected dimensions; 3 current value, period, source of truth; 4 comparable own baseline, competitor peer values/percentiles, applicable external benchmark; 5 absolute/relative gap + confidence; 6 affected URLs/products/locations/campaigns/cohorts; 7 likely mechanism supported by corroborating evidence; 8 exact recommendation, owner, dependency; 9 acceptance criteria + automated/manual test; 10 business guardrail, monitoring window, rollback condition; 11 what must not be done; 12 excluded alternatives and why.

structures.name: Benchmark classes and competitor taxonomy
structures.detail: Target-method benchmark classes: OWN (own baseline/cohort/seasonal/plan) vs PEER (peer median -> upper quartile -> leader percentiles, identical market/device/language/period). 9 competitor set types built separately: direct, SERP, paid, marketplace, local, publisher, substitute, AI-answer, aspirational. 7 opportunity classifications: defend, mandatory parity, flank, attack, category-creation, partner, deliberate-ignore. Cadence: priority competitor panel monthly; complete market map quarterly. Prohibition: do not infer spend or performance from an ad library; archive competitor pages/ads/offers/reviews/SERPs with date, region, source.

structures.name: Evidence and completion requirements (overlay)
structures.detail: Archive raw PDF plus CSV/JSON/crawl/log and configuration. Generate SHA-256 manifest; never overwrite baseline evidence. Link each closed issue to implementation reference, staging proof, live proof and monitored result. Decision classification (6 states): included | deferred | not applicable | rejected | unknown | accepted-risk. P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review.

structures.name: Required metric panel (9 metrics, columns: ID | Metric | Source | Target method | Red flag | Improvement path)
structures.detail: COM-004 Qualified lead rate (CRM, OWN baseline + sales capacity/economics). COM-005 Lead-to-win rate (CRM, OWN cohort + sales target). B2B-001 MQL-to-SQL rate (CRM, OWN cohort and capacity; red flag: MQL up, SQL rate down). B2B-002 Pipeline sourced/influenced (CRM, OWN plan, model clearly labelled). B2B-003 Lead response time (CRM/call system, SLA by lead value/urgency). SEO-004 Weighted organic SOV (Semrush/STAT/AccuRanker, PEER median then upper quartile in priority clusters). AI-002 Prompt mention share (Controlled prompt panel, PEER same prompt/model with confidence intervals). CRO-001 Primary conversion rate (Backend/CRM + analytics, OWN seasonal + industry context + experiment). UX-001 Task success rate (usability test, per critical task vs baseline/peer test).

structures.name: Mandatory do-not-do register (6 prohibitions, identical 6x)
structures.detail: 1 No redesign for visual novelty without measurable user/brand/search/commercial purpose. 2 No delete/redirect of an existing page without master URL and preservation checks. 3 No benchmark whose definition or segment is not comparable. 4 No copying competitor content, claims, creative or dark patterns. 5 No closing work before live evidence and monitoring. 6 No ignored recommendations left unexplained — use the Decision/Exclusion Register.

structures.name: URL classification chain (EXISTING variants, Phase 1)
structures.detail: Classify every URL: protect | refresh | consolidate | redirect | archive/noindex | retire. Built from master URL inventory drawn from every discovery source ('do not rely on the current navigation or sitemap alone'). Protected pages get screenshots, copy, metadata, schema, internal links and conversion components captured; defects recorded separately from redesign preferences; operators/sales/support interviewed for hidden dependencies and offline URL uses.

structures.name: B2B-specific trust controls (5) and content controls (5)
structures.detail: Trust: legal entity/leadership/team/market experience; case studies with context, method, outcomes; client/partner proof and references WITH PERMISSION; security/compliance/service levels/procurement information; clear contact ownership and response process. Content: industry/vertical pages; role/persona pages; solution/use-case pages; capabilities and implementation/process pages; case studies, research, technical resources, comparison and procurement content. NOTE: these items also appear duplicated inline in each Phase 1 checklist before their own headed sections — mechanical template duplication.

structures.name: B2B-specific competitive edge controls (5) + market-share attack patterns (3)
structures.detail: Capture and test: ICP and account segmentation; buying committee roles; long sales cycle and assisted content; CRM attribution and response SLA; case-study/proof governance. Attack patterns: own high-value problem/industry/use-case clusters; build comparison, alternative and integration pages with factual proof; improve MQL-to-SQL, account engagement and sales enablement.

structures.name: KPI and guardrail scorecard (13 items, identical 6x)
structures.detail: marketing-qualified accounts/leads; sales acceptance; meeting rate; pipeline value; opportunity velocity; win rate; revenue influenced; cost per opportunity/account; organic clicks/impressions and priority rankings where applicable; indexation and crawl health; Core Web Vitals by important template; technical error and redirect rate; accessibility/security/privacy closure. Segment by market, domain/subfolder, language, location, device, source/campaign, page/product/service type.

structures.name: Roles and sign-off table (9 roles, identical 6x)
structures.detail: Accountable business owner (commercial outcome, scope, priority, budget, acceptance) | Project/product owner (requirements, dependencies, backlog, gates, evidence) | SEO/content | Design/UX/CRO | Development/DevOps | Analytics/data | CRM/sales/ecommerce operations (revenue truth) | Market/legal/privacy owner (claims, consent, market approval) | QA (independent test execution, evidence, retest).

structures.name: Mandatory tools list (15 items, identical 6x)
structures.detail: GSC; GA4 + GTM; CRM/backend commercial data; Screaming Frog HTML and JavaScript crawls; Semrush Site Audit + visibility; DataForSEO APIs where automation/scale is required; Ahrefs or equivalent backlink verification; PageSpeed Insights/CrUX plus GTmetrix or WebPageTest; Clarity/Hotjar behavioural evidence; accessibility/browser/device/security/uptime tools; CRM/marketing automation; ABM/ad platforms; company enrichment; webinar/event tools; sales engagement and call intelligence. Rule: 'Add tools only when they have a defined decision or operational use.' Exact exports/config/cadence live in the shared Tool and Report Register / TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv.

structures.name: Monitoring cadence (Phase 7)
structures.detail: Daily during stabilisation: uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives. Weekly for 8-12 weeks: GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, qualified lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links. Monthly: executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing-page performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog. Quarterly: full technical, content, UX/CRO, accessibility, security, competitor, architecture review. Standing alerts: content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change. Deltas: organic adds monthly content-decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor-change reports; landing adds daily spend/sessions/conversion/qualified outcome/revenue-margin/page speed/errors while campaigns run. Stabilisation windows: 24h/72h/7d/28d comparisons (overlay P7); first stable operating baseline = 4-8 weeks post-launch before normalising targets.

structures.name: Per-workflow deltas vs common skeleton
structures.detail: NEW_WEBSITE P1 adds: CRM/marketing-automation integration, lead scoring/routing/SLA, lawful account enrichment, gated/ungated resource strategy, calendar/webinar/event/sales-enablement integration; validate demand before producing entire asset; document assumptions (no history). EXISTING_WEBSITE P1 = protected-baseline set (freeze dated raw exports GSC/GA4/GTM/CRM/paid/crawlers/backlinks/server logs/perf; master URL inventory; sitemap audit; URL classification; protected-page capture; pre-change KPI baselines/guardrails); P2 adds preservation specification + change-impact register + 'avoid simultaneous changes to URL, intent, content, layout, offer and tracking unless necessary and approved'; P3 adds old-vs-new comparison, preserve production until new passes; P4 adds regression checks vs protected baseline resolving every unexplained loss; P5 adds release with redirect/change map, control metrics, rollback triggers. ORGANIC variants P1 add: ICP/account-intent keyword mapping, industry/problem/solution architecture, thought leadership/expert entity building, digital PR/partner/association links, content-to-pipeline attribution, query-topic-page map by intent/funnel/market/language/location, competitor benchmark incl. publishers/marketplaces/local, gap identification; P2 adds 12-month technical/content/authority roadmap, one primary owning page per intent cluster + cannibalisation resolution before expansion, editorial standards, PR/link-earning plans; P3 adds fix technical/indexation before scaling content, publish only after editorial/SEO/factual-claims/link/conversion QA, branded/non-branded dashboards; P4 adds per-template indexability validation + reject thin/repetitive production; P5 adds record publication/discovery dates; P8 adds feed winning queries back. LANDING variants P1 add: one audience/problem/offer/next-step per page, message match to campaign/segment/sales stage, capture company/role/need/market without excessive friction, traffic-source and audience map, indexable vs paid-only-noindex vs evergreen vs temporary vs controlled-test-variant classification, offer economics/capacity; P2 adds message-match chain ad/query/referrer -> headline/proof/offer/CTA, ONE primary conversion + minimum qualification data, control/variant + experiment design + sample-size + guardrails BEFORE traffic; P3 adds fast focused page with limited navigational leakage, campaign-safe URL/canonical/OG decisions; P4 adds click every ad/email/referral destination, real submissions confirmed downstream, page speed under paid-social mobile network conditions; P5 adds previous page/control preserved + traffic allocation confirmed; P6 adds review lead/order quality before declaring a conversion winner; P8 adds one hypothesis at a time + experiment learning register. ALL B2B workflows: P2 ends 'Map content and CTA by buying role and stage; include sales handoff and account ownership'; P3 ends 'Integrate CRM campaign/member status, lead scoring, routing, SLA and opportunity-source preservation'; P6 ends 'Review sales acceptance, meeting quality, pipeline and opportunity velocity, not only form conversion'.

structures.name: Required deliverables (common 10 + deltas)
structures.detail: Common: Project Charter + classification record; market/domain/location matrix; baseline or research pack; KPI baseline/target/guardrail sheet; page/query/audience map; issue register + prioritised backlog; analytics/event/attribution specification; QA evidence + signed gate records; launch/post-launch report; monitoring dashboard + continuous-improvement backlog. Website adds: proposed business sitemap, proposed XML sitemap specification, content/template inventory. EXISTING adds: master URL inventory, current sitemap/architecture audit, preservation register, redirect/change map where URLs change. Organic adds: keyword/topic/intent map, technical/content/authority roadmap, editorial and link-earning standard. Landing adds: traffic-source/message-match matrix, control/variant and experiment register.

overlaps.package_item: Evidence and completion requirements (raw archives, SHA-256 manifests, never overwrite baseline, closed-issue linkage to staging+live proof)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: EVIDENCE LAW (launches/<domain>/ committed to git, append-only audit passes, immutable content-mined/, IST timestamps)

overlaps.existing_mechanism: BUILD DECISION MATRIX: MINE FIRST full inventory + PROTECTION MAP (KEEP/MERGE/301)

overlaps.package_item: Build only on controlled staging with production indexing blocked; overlay P4 blocks 'production-only edits'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE no production writes; staging tracks; production DNS flips always human
overlaps.note: Identical doctrine; v1 wording already enforced by scripts/CI — adopt package phrasing into workflow text only.

overlaps.existing_mechanism: HARD GATE: no DNS/robots changes by agent; human-only DNS flips; GSC two-account trap known

overlaps.package_item: Roles and sign-off 9-role table with 'independent human review' for P0/P1 closure and launch gates
overlaps.existing_mechanism: Owner-only approval (Abilash), agent builds, Dr. Deepu John clinical sign-off, external AI reviewers (ChatGPT/Perplexity) as independent QA
overlaps.note: Collapse the 9 roles to the real cast via an owner-approved role map; must not dilute owner-only approval or drop clinical sign-off (absent from the package). QA independence partially satisfiable by dual external AI audit, but 'independent human review' at launch gates = owner.

overlaps.package_item: Mandatory tools list (15) + 'add tools only with defined decision use' + TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv
overlaps.existing_mechanism: R7 tool/skill map requirement; v1 stack (Tavily/Perplexity/GPT audits, DataForSEO planned, Clarity MCP already connected)
