conflicts: AI-agent execution rule 9 (all 6 Shopify workflows) instructs the agent to add new learnings directly to 'the shared standard and relevant workflow' — v1 doctrine requires owner ruling (DECISIONS.md) for doctrine changes and forbids agent self-merge (HARD GATE i). Must be rewritten as propose-via-PR/DIRECTIVES, owner approves.

Phase 5 launch steps (deploy sequence, DNS/SSL/CDN plan, publish theme/configuration, submit GSC sitemaps, robots validation) name no executor. Executed by an agent they would violate HARD GATES a (no production writes) and c (no DNS/robots changes; DNS flips always human). Merge must pin every Phase 5 production action to a named human role.

Gate 5 'Complete a real primary conversion' implies a real payment on commerce sites (KAPPL). The agent cannot execute financial transactions; the step must be assigned to owner/staff with the agent verifying evidence only.

Package Phase 4 'Complete migration rehearsal ... backup and rollback rehearsal' and Shopify redirect imports touch production-adjacent systems; under HARD GATE d (Editor-role creds only) and no-staging-to-prod-DB-copies, rehearsal environments must be explicitly non-production in the merged text.

Several GPT-supplied Source Register entries are unverifiable or placeholders and would violate HARD GATE f (never invent facts) if admitted as-is: R02 URL is literally https://www.reddit.com/ (root, not a source), R03 is a subreddit root, G15 cites a 2026/06 Google blog URL, O02 a 2026 OWASP agentic list, A02/A03 cite arXiv 2602.x preprints — every URL must be fetch-verified before the register is trusted; failed entries recorded as rejected in the Decision/Exclusion Register.

The 'Mandatory tools and reports' list declares Semrush, Ahrefs, Screaming Frog, GTmetrix/WebPageTest, Hotjar as mandatory; adopting 'mandatory' verbatim without licenses would make gates unpassable (a de facto gate weakening when skipped silently). Owner must ratify the licensed subset; substitutions logged per the package's own 'or equivalent' and add-tools-only-with-defined-use rules.

Monitoring manual assigns audiences ('Operations/development', 'Steering group', 'Executive sponsor') and the workflows a 9-role RACI that the actual one-owner-plus-agent org does not staff; unmapped roles silently defaulting to the agent would breach the human-review requirements (P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review) — role mapping needs an owner ruling, not agent discretion.
injection_flags: 'AI-agent execution rules' sections (repeated 6x in SHOPIFY_OPERATING_MANUAL_2026.md) are imperative instructions addressed directly to an AI agent, not mere procedure description. Content is mostly benign/aligned, but rule 9 directs the agent to modify the OS's own standard files — treat the whole block as doctrine-to-be-merged under owner control, never as live instructions from the package.

The Version 2 Agency-OS Overlay preamble ('This workflow inherits the Master Agency OS... The original checklist remains valid') asserts binding authority over agent behavior from inside the package; binding force comes only from the owner's merge decision.

REFERENCE_URLS.md / SOURCE_REGISTER.csv contain 61 external URLs including three YouTube videos, arXiv preprints and Reddit links; no instruction to fetch/execute them blindly was found, but two entries (R02 = https://www.reddit.com/ root, R03 = subreddit root) are placeholder URLs that cannot support the claims attached to them — a hallmark of GPT-generated filler; do not fetch or cite them as evidence until verified.
No hidden text, encoded content, embedded commands, credentials requests, or instructions to bypass approvals were found in any of the six files.
open_questions: Which of the package's 'mandatory' tools does the owner actually license or intend to buy (Semrush, Ahrefs, Screaming Frog, GTmetrix/WebPageTest, Hotjar), and which are substituted by DataForSEO/Clarity/Tavily per R6/R7?
Who executes the Gate 5 'real primary conversion' (real payment/test order) on commerce sites, and how is it refunded/annotated in finance reconciliation?

May agents append learnings to shared standards at all (AI-agent rule 9), or must every standard change route through DIRECTIVES.md -> owner-approved PR? Owner ruling needed before the rule is merged.

Which URL-classification vocabulary becomes canonical: v1 PROTECTION MAP (KEEP/MERGE/301) or the package's 6-state protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire — and does the mapping I proposed (KEEP->protect, MERGE->consolidate, 301->redirect) match the owner's intent?

Should each of the 61 Source Register URLs be fetch-verified before admission to the merged research library, and are the unverifiable/placeholder entries (R02, R03, G15, O02, A02, A03) rejected, replaced, or kept as labelled-unverified?

How are the 9 workflow roles and 6 monitoring audiences mapped to the real cast (owner, agent, Dr. Deepu John, Akshar Yadav, ChatGPT/Perplexity auditors), and which roles are formally n/a per site class?
Is landing-page control/variant experimentation (sample-size, stable assignment infrastructure) in scope for the 30-day sprint, or deferred until after the pilot site?

Does the 'Weekly for 8-12 weeks' stabilisation window and monthly/quarterly cadence feed the owner's separately-built monitoring tool (R6) as inputs only, or must the repo also render these scorecards (extending kairali.ai/status)?

The metric panel's non-contiguous IDs imply a fuller Metric Dictionary elsewhere in the package — confirm the dictionary file is the canonical ID source and this panel is a Shopify subset (cross-reader reconciliation).

Shopify workflows reference TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv while the shared standard is named 01_TOOL_AND_REPORT_REGISTER.md — confirm they are the same register or two artifacts that must be reconciled in the merge.

readings.summary: LANDING_PAGE_OPERATING_MANUAL_2026.md (3,137 lines) = a core manual (scope selector, preservation/research protocols, page-brief fields, 7-layer scorecard, 10-step sequence) followed by 8 near-identical workflows (B2C/B2B/D2C/SHOPIFY x NEW/EXISTING, all Version 1.0, Issued 2026-07-19), each with a Phase 0-8 gated checklist, Gate 0-5 evidence blocks, stabilisation exit, 7 stop-launch conditions, 9 AI-agent execution rules, and a 'Version 2 Agency-OS Overlay' (phase-control/proof matrix, 12-field finding format, competitor requirements, SHA-256 evidence rules, metric panels with COM/SEO/AI/UX/CRO/LOC/B2B/TEC IDs, do-not-do register). ~85% of content is a shared skeleton; deltas are per-segment trust/content controls, tools, KPIs and metric panels. Nothing in the file contains beauty, go-science, or front-gate equivalents — those must be relocated in per R8. Main merge frictions: production-touching steps (robots, Search Console, theme publish, redirects, real purchases) written without human-only annotation; AI rule 9 telling the agent to edit shared standards; a 9-role human RACI that does not exist in a solo-owner org; mandatory tool checklists naming unlicensed tools.

structures.name: Permutation selector (manual core §1)
structures.detail: Landing page classified by 6 axes: (1) B2C lead/booking | B2B demand/ABM | D2C product/offer | Shopify implementation; (2) new page | existing page with history; (3) traffic: paid/organic/email/partner/social/QR-offline/mixed; (4) type: campaign/evergreen/product-detail/collection/hybrid; (5) region/language/location/device/audience; (6) primary conversion + downstream revenue definition.

structures.name: Existing-page preservation protocol (§2) and new-page research protocol (§3)
structures.detail: Before editing: export page, screenshots, copy, metadata, schema, links, traffic, campaign mappings, rankings, backlinks, heatmaps, funnel, qualified conversion, revenue, performance, form/payment/CRM behaviour; record helping elements + evidence level; keep control/recoverable version; 'Never infer that an old-looking page is commercially weak.' New page: evidence baseline from audience research, search/ad intent, competitor pages, offer economics, objections, proof inventory, channel message, device/market requirements, comparable internal pages; label assumptions (no historical control).

structures.name: Page brief fields (§4)
structures.detail: 23 fields: audience/persona; problem+journey stage; traffic source/keyword/ad; offer+price/terms; value proposition; primary/secondary CTA; proof; objections; required sections; legal/claim constraints; page/URL/canonical/indexability; internal links; schema; media; performance budget; accessibility; tracking; CRM/checkout; market/language; experiment plan; preservation list; owner; approvals.

structures.name: Exact page scorecard (§5) — 7 layers x 6 columns
structures.detail: Columns: Layer | Metrics | Tools | Pass/target logic | Improvement examples | Do not. Layers: Commercial (own control + economics; DON'T optimize raw conversions only), Message match (DON'T keyword stuff or change promise after click), UX (DON'T use heatmap as causal proof), Search (only if organic role intended; DON'T index every campaign page), Performance (CWV good thresholds + template budget; DON'T remove useful proof to improve score), Experiment (pre-registered method; DON'T stop early or change multiple uncontrolled variables), Operations (100% critical path in release test; DON'T launch a page sales/ops cannot fulfil).

structures.name: 10-step research/build/QA/monitoring sequence (§6)
structures.detail: 1 classify page+commercial outcome; 2 preserve existing or create research baseline; 3 map competitors+channel message; 4 write page brief+measurement plan; 5 design content hierarchy and proof BEFORE decorative treatment; 6 build with governed components and real content; 7 test mobile/desktop, regions/languages, accessibility, performance, critical conversion; 8 verify analytics plus backend/CRM/order; 9 launch with control, rollback and guardrails; 10 review 24h/72h/7d/28d and run disciplined experiments.

structures.name: 8 workflow IDs and per-file spans
structures.detail: B2C-NEW_LANDING (56-427), B2C-EXISTING_LANDING (430-811), B2B-NEW_LANDING (816-1186), B2B-EXISTING_LANDING (1191-1573), D2C-NEW_LANDING (1578-1951), D2C-EXISTING_LANDING (1956-2341), SHOPIFY-NEW_LANDING (2346-2733), SHOPIFY-EXISTING_LANDING (2738-3137). All Version 1.0, Issued 2026-07-19. NEW = no historical control URL; EXISTING = live page with traffic/conversions/links/campaign references.

structures.name: Mandatory inherited standards (identical in all 8)
structures.detail: ../00_SHARED_STANDARDS/: 00_MASTER_OPERATING_SYSTEM.md, 01_TOOL_AND_REPORT_REGISTER.md, 02_REGIONAL_DOMAIN_LOCATION_FRAMEWORK.md, 03_URL_SITEMAP_MIGRATION_STANDARD.md, 04_MEASUREMENT_ATTRIBUTION_STANDARD.md, 05_QA_LAUNCH_MONITORING_LOOP.md, 06_2026_STANDARDS.md. Each Overlay additionally inherits: Master Agency OS, Competitive Intelligence Playbook, Metric Dictionary, Evidence/Agent Standard, Localization Manual, Monitoring Manual — two distinct inheritance lists.

structures.name: Gate evidence chain (Gate 0-5, identical wording all 8 workflows)
structures.detail: Gate 0: approved Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, project risk classification. Gate 1: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet. Gate 2: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page or topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog. Gate 3: build complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps. Gate 4: completed test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1 issues, signed Launch Readiness certificate ('unresolved P0 issues stop launch'). Gate 5: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision. Plus 'Stabilisation exit: critical paths stable, P0/P1 regressions closed or accepted, performance understood against the correct baseline.'

structures.name: Phase 1 divergence: NEW vs EXISTING
structures.detail: NEW = 'Research and launch baseline' (demand/opportunity baselines; journeys/intents/objections/proof; domain+regional architecture BEFORE content/design; proposed sitemap+URL policy+page inventory+XML spec; targets marked as estimates; validate demand before producing whole asset; document assumptions). EXISTING = 'Discovery and protected baseline' (freeze dated raw exports from GSC/GA4/GTM/CRM/paid/crawlers/backlinks/server logs/perf tools; master URL inventory from EVERY discovery source; audit XML sitemap index+children; classify every URL protect|refresh|consolidate|redirect|archive-noindex|retire; identify protected pages; capture screenshots/copy/metadata/schema/links/conversion components; record analytics/CRM/forms/payments behaviour; pre-change KPI baselines + launch guardrail thresholds from comparable periods; record defects separately from redesign preferences; interview operators/sales/support for hidden dependencies and offline URL uses).

structures.name: EXISTING-only additions in Phases 2-6
structures.detail: P2: preservation specification + change-impact register per protected asset; 'Avoid simultaneous changes to URL, intent, content, layout, offer and tracking unless necessary and approved.' P3: maintain old-vs-new comparison, preserve existing production asset until new version passes. P4: regression checks against protected baseline, resolve every unexplained loss. P5: release with redirect/change map, control metrics, rollback triggers active. P6: compare with recent AND seasonal baselines, investigate losses by page/segment (NEW instead has: establish first stable 4-8 week operating baseline before normalising targets). EXISTING deliverables add 4: Master URL inventory, Current sitemap/architecture audit, Preservation register, Redirect/change map.

structures.name: Stop-launch conditions (7, identical all 8 workflows)
structures.detail: 'Do not launch or close the release if': (1) primary conversion/CRM/order/payment path fails; (2) production indexability, canonicals, sitemap or priority redirects wrong; (3) analytics cannot measure primary outcome or duplicates material events; (4) target market receives wrong language/currency/availability/price/shipping/contact route; (5) critical security/privacy/accessibility/legal issue remains; (6) protected high-value content/links/URLs/proof removed without approved evidence; (7) rollback, owners or command-centre coverage unavailable for a material release.

structures.name: AI-agent execution rules (9, identical all 8 workflows)
structures.detail: 1 select correct workflow before acting; 2 never infer an existing URL/page has no value without checking all discovery+commercial sources; 3 label every finding as observed fact | calculated result | tool estimate | user-provided assumption | recommendation; 4 attach evidence and affected URLs to every issue; 5 no issue closure without retest evidence; 6 escalate conflicts between commercial truth and third-party SEO scores — do not optimise for the score; 7 preserve immutable pre-change exports and screenshots; 8 stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval, do not silently bypass; 9 add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow rather than keeping them only in chat.

structures.name: Overlay phase-control and proof matrix (phases 0-8, identical all 8)
structures.detail: Columns: Phase | Required work | Evidence | Do not proceed when. Notable stop conditions: P0 no owner/unclear denominator/missing commercial source/unauthorized scope; P1 incomplete URL discovery, baseline overwritten, estimates presented as truth; P2 recommendation lacking metric/cause/economics/acceptance criteria/evidence; P3 design changes without purpose or protected-elements list; P4 production-only edits, untraceable app/plugin/config changes; P5 open P0, unaccepted P1, broken conversion/redirect/tracking/backup; P6 guardrail breach or inability to verify live commercial path; P7 unexplained material revenue/conversion/indexation/ranking loss; P8 vanity reporting, no owner, repeated recommendations with no learning.

structures.name: Exact finding format (12 mandatory fields)
structures.detail: 1 issue ID, phase, severity; 2 exact metric/formula + affected dimensions; 3 current value, period, source of truth; 4 comparable own baseline + competitor peer values/percentiles + applicable external benchmark; 5 absolute/relative gap + confidence; 6 affected URLs/products/locations/campaigns/cohorts; 7 likely mechanism with corroborating evidence; 8 exact recommendation, owner, dependency; 9 acceptance criteria + automated/manual test; 10 business guardrail, monitoring window, rollback condition; 11 what must not be done; 12 excluded alternatives and why.

structures.name: Competitor and market-share requirements (identical all 8)
structures.detail: 9 competitor set types built separately: direct, SERP, paid, marketplace, local, publisher, substitute, AI-answer, aspirational. Peer values at median/upper-quartile/leader on identical market/device/language/period. 7 opportunity classifications: defend, mandatory parity, flank, attack, category-creation, partner, deliberate-ignore. Quantify addressable demand, attainable share, qualified conversion, contribution, confidence. Archive competitor pages/ads/offers/reviews/SERPs with date+region+source; do NOT infer spend/performance from an ad library. Cadence: priority competitor panel monthly, complete market map quarterly.

structures.name: Evidence and completion requirements (identical all 8)
structures.detail: Archive raw PDF + CSV/JSON/crawl/log + configuration; generate SHA-256 manifest and never overwrite baseline evidence; link each closed issue to implementation reference + staging proof + live proof + monitored result; record decisions as included | deferred | not applicable | rejected | unknown | accepted-risk; P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review.

structures.name: Benchmark classes (Target method column of metric panels)
structures.detail: Three target-method classes: OWN (own seasonal baseline/cohort), PEER (median then upper quartile of comparable competitors), ECONOMIC (business-economics target). CWV thresholds cited with gate tag [G12]: TEC-004 LCP P75 good <=2.5s / NI 2.5-4s / poor >4s; TEC-005 INP P75 good <=200ms / NI 200-500ms / poor >500ms.

structures.name: Metric panels by segment (metric-dictionary IDs)
structures.detail: B2C (both): COM-001 Revenue, COM-003 RPS, COM-004 Qualified lead rate, COM-005 Lead-to-win, SEO-001 GSC clicks, SEO-004 Weighted organic SOV, AI-001 Google generative impressions (GSC Generative AI report), UX-001 Task success, CRO-001 Primary CVR, LOC-001 Local pack visibility share. B2B: COM-004, COM-005, B2B-001 MQL-to-SQL, B2B-002 Pipeline sourced/influenced, B2B-003 Lead response time (SLA by lead value/urgency), SEO-004, AI-002 Prompt mention share (controlled prompt panel, PEER same prompt/model, confidence intervals), CRO-001, UX-001. D2C: COM-001, COM-002 Contribution margin, COM-003, COM-006 CAC, COM-007 LTV, SEO-004, CRO-005 Add-to-cart, CRO-006 Checkout completion, CRO-008 Return/refund rate, AI-002. Shopify: COM-001, COM-002, COM-003, COM-007, SEO-006 Indexable URL count (equals approved inventory within explained variance), TEC-004, TEC-005, CRO-005, CRO-006, CRO-008. Panel columns: ID | Metric | Source | Target method | Red flag | Improvement path.

structures.name: Segment trust controls (5 each) and content controls (5 each)
structures.detail: B2C trust: identity/address/team/credentials; scope/process/price-range/eligibility/limitations; authentic verifiable testimonials; privacy/cancellation/refund/safety/support; local credibility/directions/response-time promise. B2C content: problem->service mapping; service/programme/location/practitioner/proof pages; decision content (process/comparison/suitability/FAQ/pricing/next steps); post-service retention; YMYL/health content reviewed and claims controlled. B2B trust: legal entity/leadership/experience; case studies with context/method/outcomes; client proof with permission; security/compliance/SLA/procurement info; contact ownership+response process. B2B content: industry/vertical, role/persona, solution/use-case, capabilities/implementation, case-study/research/comparison/procurement pages. D2C trust: merchant identity/support; accurate product/ingredient/safety/suitability info; authentic reviews/UGC; price/tax/shipping/return transparency; secure payment+order support. D2C content: product/variant, collection/use-case, comparison/routine/bundle, guides/ingredients/usage/care/safety, shipping/returns/subscription/loyalty/post-purchase. Shopify trust: merchant identity+policies; accurate product/variant/inventory; shipping/duties/taxes/returns by market; reviews/proof; payment security/support/order status. Shopify content: products/collections/pages/blogs; search/filter/merchandising; market-language localisation; product schema/feed; post-purchase retention. NOTE: these controls are also duplicated verbatim as loose Phase-1 checkboxes before their own headed subsections (apparent generation artifact, e.g. lines 105-117 duplicate 124-138).

structures.name: Segment competitive-edge controls + market-share attack patterns (overlay)
structures.detail: B2C: urgent-vs-considered journey; call/WhatsApp/booking routing; location/service eligibility; trust/credentials/reviews; lead response + no-show/cancellation. Attack: win under-served problem+location demand; proof+service design for qualified conversion; referral/revisit/review loops. B2B: ICP/account segmentation; buying-committee roles; long cycle + assisted content; CRM attribution + response SLA; case-study/proof governance. Attack: own high-value problem/industry/use-case clusters; comparison/alternative/integration pages with factual proof; MQL-to-SQL + enablement. D2C: product/variant+margin; price/offer/delivery; proof/claims; returns/repeat; merchant/marketplace visibility. Attack: profitable clusters; differentiate offer/proof/merchandising/service; retention+contribution not discount volume. Shopify: theme/app/script governance; products/variants/collections/tags; Markets/languages/currencies; feeds/inventory/checkout/redirects; Shopify web performance + search analytics. Attack: catalog/feed/search/merchandising advantages; remove app/theme friction with measured impact; profitable CVR/AOV/repeat by market.

structures.name: Shopify-specific platform controls
structures.detail: P1: export products/variants/collections/pages/blogs/menus/redirects/themes/apps/customers-orders-as-permitted/markets/domains/languages/policies/metafields/feeds; audit platform URL constraints (automatic canonicals/sitemaps, tag/filter/search URLs, collection-product paths, app proxy URLs); create app register (business value, cost, scripts, data, schema, theme changes, uninstall residue). P2: approve Shopify Markets architecture (primary domain, dedicated domains/subdomains/subfolders, languages, currencies, products, pricing, fulfilment); define theme/Liquid/component + metafield/metaobject architecture BEFORE page-builder proliferation; define native-vs-app responsibility (reviews, bundles, subscriptions, search, filters, localisation, feeds, pixels). P3: build DUPLICATE theme — 'do not edit the live theme directly for a major release'; implement Shopify customer events/pixels/GA4/consent without duplication; import/test URL redirects, update links to final handles. P4: validate Shopify-generated sitemap children, canonicals, hreflang/Markets behaviour, robots controls; Shopify Web Performance regression check by URL/template; test notification emails, inventory, fulfilment, taxes/duties, refunds, gift cards, discounts, customer accounts. P5: publish approved theme/configuration, verify domain/Markets routing, feeds, checkout immediately. P7: monthly Shopify Analytics / Web Performance / search terms & zero results / app-theme changes / market reports.

structures.name: Monitoring cadence ladder (Phase 7, identical all 8 + Shopify extra)
structures.detail: Daily during stabilisation: uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives. Weekly for 8-12 weeks: GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, qualified lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links. Monthly: executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog. Quarterly: full technical/content/UX-CRO/accessibility/security/competitor/architecture review. Standing alerts: content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change. Daily while campaigns run: spend, sessions, conversion, qualified outcome, revenue/margin, page speed, errors.

structures.name: Phase 8 continuous improvement loop (8 steps, identical all 8)
structures.detail: Collect evidence (users, sales/support, commercial systems, search, crawls, competitors) -> diagnose constraint+segment ('do not jump from a metric to a cosmetic solution') -> prioritise by business impact/reach/confidence/risk/effort -> write hypothesis + acceptance criteria + primary metric + guardrails + owner + rollback -> implement ONE controlled change or documented batch -> QA implementation and data before evaluating performance -> adopt/iterate/revert/retire on evidence, record learning -> one hypothesis at a time, maintain experiment learning register.

structures.name: Roles and sign-off matrix (9 roles, identical all 8)
structures.detail: Accountable business owner (commercial outcome/scope/priority/budget/acceptance); Project/product owner (requirements/dependencies/backlog/gates/evidence); SEO/content; Design/UX/CRO; Development/DevOps; Analytics/data; CRM/sales/ecommerce operations (revenue truth); Market/legal/privacy owner (claims/consent/market approval); QA (independent test execution, evidence, retest).

structures.name: Mandatory do-not-do register (6 items, identical all 8 overlays)
structures.detail: No redesign for visual novelty without measurable user/brand/search/commercial purpose; no delete/redirect of existing page without master URL + preservation checks; no benchmark whose definition/segment is not comparable; no copying competitor content/claims/creative/dark patterns; no closing work before live evidence and monitoring; no unexplained ignored recommendations — use the Decision/Exclusion Register.

structures.name: Mandatory tools per segment
structures.detail: Common 10: GSC; GA4+GTM; CRM/backend commercial data; Screaming Frog HTML+JS crawls; Semrush Site Audit+visibility; DataForSEO APIs where automation/scale required; Ahrefs or equivalent backlinks; PSI/CrUX + GTmetrix/WebPageTest; Clarity/Hotjar; accessibility/browser-device/security/uptime tools. B2C adds: Google Business Profile, call tracking, booking platform, local rank/citation tools. B2B adds: CRM/marketing automation, ABM/ad platforms, company enrichment, webinar/event tools, sales engagement + call intelligence. D2C adds: Merchant Center, product-feed tool, reviews/UGC, search+merchandising, email/SMS lifecycle, profit+attribution tools. Shopify adds: Shopify Analytics, Shopify Web Performance, Shopify Markets, Search & Discovery, Merchant Center, theme/app profiling. Rule: 'Add tools only when they have a defined decision or operational use.'

overlaps.package_item: Phase 0-8 gated workflow skeleton with Gate 0-5 evidence blocks and accountable-approval stops
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 FRONT GATES (brief -> strategy -> design_source -> golden_page -> full build in launches/<domain>/approvals.yaml, CI-enforced) + 63-gate registry
overlaps.note: Owner is replacing the workflow layer, so adopt the Phase 0-8 spine; but R8 requires v1 front gates to survive undiluted — map brief/strategy into Gate 0-2, design_source+golden_page into Phase 2/3, and keep approvals.yaml + CI signature enforcement as the mechanism behind every 'accountable approval'.

overlaps.package_item: Gate evidence blocks, 'signed gate records', evidence folders per project
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 EVIDENCE LAW (launches/<domain>/ filled checklists + gate evidence committed to git, append-only, IST timestamps)
overlaps.note: Same doctrine; keep launches/<domain>/ as the physical location and append-only rule, adopt the package's per-gate evidence naming and Launch Readiness certificate as new artifacts inside it.

overlaps.package_item: SHA-256 manifests + 'never overwrite baseline evidence' + immutable pre-change exports (AI rule 7, overlay evidence requirements)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 raw mined content immutable in content-mined/ + append-only audit passes + git history
overlaps.note: Strict superset of v1 immutability; add manifest generation to the evidence law scripts.

overlaps.package_item: Existing-page preservation protocol + Phase 1 'Discovery and protected baseline' + URL classification protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire + master URL inventory from every discovery source
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 BUILD DECISION MATRIX: MINE FIRST full inventory + PROTECTION MAP (every legacy URL KEEP/MERGE/301)
overlaps.note: Identical doctrine, richer taxonomy (6 states vs 3) and richer discovery sources (server logs, backlinks, offline references, operator interviews); one unified taxonomy must be chosen — see open question.

overlaps.package_item: 'Build only on controlled staging with production indexing blocked'; overlay P4 stop 'Production-only edits, untraceable app/plugin/config changes'; Shopify 'do not edit the live theme directly'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 HARD GATE: no production writes; WordPress two-track rule (Novamira staging-only); staging discipline
overlaps.note: Package agrees and reinforces; keep v1's script/CI enforcement as the mechanism. No weakening.

overlaps.package_item: 7 stop-launch conditions ('Do not launch or close the release if') + 'unresolved P0 issues stop launch'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 gate registry merge-blocking gates + PROOF-OF-WORK
overlaps.note: Add as rows in gates/registry.yaml with required|adapted|n_a per site class (rule: gates are added, never weakened); condition 6 (protected content removed without approved evidence) directly extends the Protection Map.

overlaps.package_item: AI-agent execution rule 3: label every finding observed fact | calculated result | tool estimate | user-provided assumption | recommendation; overlay P1 stop 'estimates presented as truth'; 'mark third-party estimates as estimates'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 HARD GATE: never invent facts/IDs/prices — gaps are ASKED, not filled; R2 decision provenance; R4 ask-when-in-doubt
overlaps.note: The 5-label evidence taxonomy operationalizes the v1 gate and R2/R4; adopt as the standard finding vocabulary OS-wide.

overlaps.package_item: AI-agent rules 5+8 (no closure without retest evidence; stop at phase gates, never silently bypass) + 'P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 HARD GATE: agent never self-merges a PR (owner-only bypass, logged) + agent never self-approves front gates
overlaps.note: Consistent; v1 defines WHO the human is (owner). Merged doc must state the independent reviewer is the owner (or owner-designated humans), never the agent, and never merely the external AI auditors for launch gates.

overlaps.package_item: Phase 5 'Complete a real primary conversion and verify it in frontend, backend/CRM, analytics and notifications' + live validation record
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 PROOF-OF-WORK (no 'done' without working URL/real output) + post-push live-fetch diff vs intent
overlaps.note: Strengthens proof-of-work into an end-to-end conversion proof; needs a test-order/test-lead protocol so it doesn't collide with no-production-writes (open question).

overlaps.package_item: Phase 7 monitoring cadence (daily stabilisation / weekly 8-12wk / monthly / quarterly) + 24h/72h/7d/28d review windows + KPI guardrail sheets with rollback triggers
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 STATUS.yaml fleet pulse + Monday lints; R6 old-vs-new benchmark values feeding continuous monitoring (owner's separate monitoring tool)
overlaps.note: Fills the v1 gap and supplies exactly the before/after inputs R6 asks for; wire outputs into STATUS.yaml and the owner's monitoring tool rather than a new dashboard.

overlaps.package_item: Pre-change KPI baselines from frozen exports before any sitemap/architecture approval (Phase 1 EXISTING) and 'Select domain and regional architecture before content or design production' (Phase 1 NEW)
overlaps.existing_mechanism: R6 BASELINE-BEFORE-SITEMAP (DataForSEO PDF report of the OLD site before the new sitemap)
overlaps.note: Package ordering matches R6; specify the DataForSEO PDF as the named instrument of the Phase-1 baseline for existing sites.

overlaps.package_item: Decision/Exclusion Register + 6 decision states (included/deferred/not applicable/rejected/unknown/accepted-risk) + finding field 12 'excluded alternatives and why'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 DECISIONS.md (owner rulings) + R2 decision provenance + R3 report store 'what to reject (+reason)'
overlaps.note: Adopt the register and states as the R2/R3 store; keep DECISIONS.md as the owner-ruling layer above it (gate removals still need owner ruling there).

overlaps.package_item: 12-field exact finding format + issue register with issue IDs, acceptance criteria, retest evidence
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 has no formal finding schema (evidence law + QUESTIONS.md only)
overlaps.note: New capability; serves R2 (scientific answer per decision) and R3 (report store).

overlaps.package_item: Metric panels with dictionary IDs (COM/SEO/AI/UX/CRO/LOC/B2B/TEC) and OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC target methods + red flags
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 GO-SCIENCE GATE holds ROI as key metric; no metric dictionary exists
overlaps.note: Adopt the dictionary; reconcile with go-science ROI doctrine so ROI/MCB metrics get IDs in the same dictionary rather than a parallel system. Depends on 04_METRIC_DICTIONARY reader for canonical definitions.

overlaps.package_item: Competitor set taxonomy (9 sets), peer percentiles, 7 opportunity classifications, monthly/quarterly panel cadence, competitor evidence archiving rules
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 front-gate 'competitor-map' inside the fat strategy approval; R4 asks competitors from the user
overlaps.note: Much richer than v1's competitor-map; R4 still governs: the roster of real competitors is asked from the owner, not assumed. 'Do not infer spend or performance from an ad library' aligns with never-invent-facts.

overlaps.package_item: Scorecard 'Do not' column + mandatory do-not-do register (6 items) + 'do not copy competitor content, claims, creative or dark patterns'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 HARD GATES + prohibited shortcuts + KTAHV clinical language lock
overlaps.note: All additive; register them as gates. None weakens an existing gate.

overlaps.package_item: Do-not-do item 1: 'Do not redesign for visual novelty without a measurable user, brand, search or commercial purpose'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 BEAUTY GATE (BEAUTY_DOCTRINE.md, B1-B20 rubric, beauty-conformance registry row)
overlaps.note: Compatible only if the merged text states explicitly that beauty-conformance IS a measurable brand/commercial purpose; otherwise this line could be cited to skip beauty work. R8 relocation note required.

overlaps.package_item: Landing workflows contain NO beauty, go-science, external-AI design review, or golden-page equivalent anywhere in the file
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 BEAUTY GATE + GO-SCIENCE GATE (build guideline AND blocking pre-ship audit) + DESIGN EXTERNAL AI REVIEW (2 checkpoints, dual PASS) + golden_page front gate
overlaps.note: R8: these must be inserted — beauty+design-review Gate 1 at Phase 2 (before Gate 2 sign-off), golden-page inside Phase 3, design-review Gate 2 + beauty-audit + go-science-audit as blocking items in Phase 4 before the Launch Readiness certificate. Adopting the package verbatim would silently drop four v1 gates.

overlaps.package_item: Roles and sign-off matrix (9 human roles) + QA role 'independent test execution'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 reality: single owner (Abilash) + agent + named human reviewers (Dr. Deepu John for clinical); agent never self-approves
overlaps.note: The RACI presumes an agency staff that does not exist; if the agent nominally fills reviewer/QA roles it weakens the self-approval prohibition. Owner must map each role to a real person, the owner himself, or an explicitly-labelled external AI auditor (non-binding for launch gates).

overlaps.package_item: Launch command centre + deployment sequence + rollback authority + 'Deploy using the approved sequence; preserve a rollback path'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1: Vercel deploys; production DNS flips always human; --force-with-lease only; crash-resilience commit+push small units
overlaps.note: Adopt command-centre record-keeping (release time/version/participants, incident log, go/rollback decision) as launch evidence; release authority remains the owner.

overlaps.package_item: Steps touching robots.txt validation-on-production, Search Console sitemap submission, DNS/SSL/CDN plan, publishing Shopify theme, importing production redirects
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 HARD GATES: no DNS changes, no robots changes, no production writes, Editor-role creds only
overlaps.note: Package writes these as unattributed workflow checkboxes; executed by the agent they violate HARD GATES. Merged doc must annotate each such step actor=OWNER/HUMAN (agent may verify read-only afterwards). Not a doctrine conflict — an actor-annotation requirement.

overlaps.package_item: AI-agent rule 9: 'Add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow rather than keeping them only in chat'
overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 DIRECTIVES.md same-session capture + gates added-never-weakened + agent never self-merges + Dependabot/CODEOWNERS gate on .github/

overlaps.existing_mechanism: v1 has no experimentation framework; designs currently FROZEN
overlaps.note: Net-new capability; activation timing vs the design freeze and choice of experiment platform are owner decisions (open questions).

Owner must license or approve substitutions per R7/R1.

overlaps.existing_mechanism: No v1 counterpart

AI-agent execution rule 9 ('Add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow', lines 326 et al.) authorizes direct agent edits to governing standards — contradicts v1 change control (gates added never weakened; agent never self-merges; CODEOWNERS gate). Must be rewritten as 'propose via PR; owner approves'.

Adopting the landing workflows verbatim would silently drop four v1 gates — beauty gate, go-science gate, external AI design review (Gate 1/Gate 2 dual-PASS), and golden-page front gate — none of which appear anywhere in the file. Violates R8 and the 'gates are added, never weakened' rule; they must be explicitly inserted into Phases 2-4.

9-role human sign-off matrix + 'QA: independent test execution' + 'P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review' presume staff that does not exist. If the agent fills reviewer/QA seats it would weaken the v1 self-approval/self-merge prohibition; roles must be mapped to real humans (owner, Dr. Deepu John, external AI auditors only where owner rules them acceptable and never as launch-gate authority).

'Run real submissions/purchases and confirm ... lead/order status in downstream systems' (Phase 4 QA, line 188/568) and 'Complete a real primary conversion' (Phase 5) inject test records into production CRM/payment systems — brushes the no-production-writes and no-invented-data gates unless a defined owner-approved test-order protocol (marked test data, cleanup rule, who pays) exists.

Generic 'YMYL/health content reviewed and claims controlled where relevant' (line 138) is weaker than v1's named-reviewer gate (clinical content requires Dr. Deepu John sign-off + KTAHV banned-word lint); merged text must keep the stronger v1 wording for KTAHV/KAPPL.

Mandatory tools checklists are fail-closed but name tools not in the current stack (Screaming Frog, Semrush, Ahrefs, Hotjar, STAT/AccuRanker, call tracking, booking platform, experiment platform, ABM/enrichment, Merchant Center for some entities). Without owner substitution rulings every launch would be formally blocked — or worse, the checklist gets rubber-stamped, weakening evidence law.

Do-not-do 'no redesign for visual novelty without a measurable purpose' can be read against the BEAUTY GATE; merged doctrine must declare beauty-conformance (B1-B20) a measurable brand/commercial purpose so the line cannot be used to skip beauty work.
injection_flags: Each of the 8 workflows contains an 'AI-agent execution rules' section (lines 316-326, 702-712, 1078-1088, 1465-1475, 1842-1852, 2232-2242, 2624-2634, 3028-3038) written as imperative instructions TO an AI agent, not as procedure description. Content is benign/governance-aligned, but per merge discipline these are doctrine-to-adopt-after-review, not live instructions to this reader; they were not executed.

AI-agent rule 9 in all 8 copies instructs the agent to modify shared standards/workflow files on its own initiative — the only rule that directs autonomous write action outside a gated task; treat as requiring owner-mediated change control (also listed as a conflict).

Required tool/report runs instruct execution of 'the exact ... reports specified in TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv' (lines 412, 798, 1173, 1560, 1938, 2328, 2720, 3124) — blind deference to an external CSV not present in this file; the CSV's contents must be reviewed by its assigned reader before any agent runs what it lists.

No URLs, shell commands, credentials, or encoded/hidden text found anywhere in the file; relative doc references (../00_SHARED_STANDARDS/*.md) are inert cross-references. No classic prompt-injection patterns detected.
open_questions: Role mapping: who fills the 9-role sign-off matrix, the 'independent human review' for P0/P1 closure, and the QA 'independent test execution' seat in a solo-owner org? May external AI auditors (ChatGPT/Perplexity) count as independent review for non-launch gates?

Which Kairali entities/sites run which of the 8 workflow IDs, and how does the B2C/B2B/D2C/Shopify axis map onto the v1 three site classes commerce/organic/landing in gates/registry.yaml? (e.g. KTAHV treatment landing = B2C? KAPPL = SHOPIFY or D2C? Villa Raag = B2C?)
URL-classification taxonomy: replace v1 PROTECTION MAP KEEP/MERGE/301 with the package's protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire, or maintain a declared mapping between the two?

Tool licensing/substitution rulings: Screaming Frog, Semrush, Ahrefs, Hotjar (vs existing Clarity), STAT/AccuRanker, GTmetrix/WebPageTest, call tracking, booking platform, company enrichment, experiment platform — license, substitute with DataForSEO/existing stack, or mark n_a per site class?

Test-conversion protocol: who performs the mandatory 'real submissions/purchases' and real primary conversion at launch, how are test orders/leads marked and cleaned from CRM/Shopify, and who bears payment for real purchases?
Experimentation activation: designs are FROZEN and pilot not yet started — do the control/variant experiment provisions activate at pilot, and which experiment platform is approved?

File architecture: keep 8 near-identical workflow files (~85% duplicated skeleton, with the visible copy-paste artifact of trust/content controls duplicated inside Phase 1), or regenerate them from one canonical skeleton + per-segment delta config, consistent with v1's generated-checklist pattern? Also: fix the duplication bug either way?
Monitoring capacity: 'weekly for 8-12 weeks' per launch across ~25 sites — automate via scripts feeding the owner's separate monitoring tool, or reduce cadence per site class?
AI-002 'controlled prompt panel' for prompt mention share: does the owner want this built (models, prompts, cadence, who runs it), and is it in scope for the 30-day sprint?

The [G12] tag on TEC-004/TEC-005 CWV thresholds implies a package-internal gate numbering — how do package G-numbers reconcile with the v1 63-gate registry numbering (single source of truth requirement)?
The 'first stable 4-8 week operating baseline before normalising targets' (NEW workflows) delays target-setting well past the 30-day sprint window — accepted?

readings.summary: D2C_OPERATING_MANUAL_2026.md (2,315 lines) = short D2C doctrine header + SIX near-identical workflows, each followed by an identical "Version 2 Agency-OS Overlay". Workflow IDs: D2C-NEW_WEBSITE (L29), D2C-EXISTING_WEBSITE (L400), D2C-NEW_ORGANIC (L783), D2C-EXISTING_ORGANIC (L1162), D2C-NEW_LANDING (L1553), D2C-EXISTING_LANDING (L1931); all Version 1.0, issued 2026-07-19. Common skeleton: Phases 0-8 with named Gate 0-5 evidence blocks, a stabilisation-exit condition, monitoring-cadence ladder and a 7-step improvement loop; per-workflow deltas are small, flavor-specific checklist insertions (commerce integration, organic roadmap/cannibalisation, landing message-match/experiments; EXISTING variants add protected-baseline/preservation/regression steps). Overlay adds the phase-control proof matrix with per-phase do-not-proceed conditions, a 12-field finding format, 9-type competitor sets with 7-way opportunity classification, SHA-256 evidence manifests, a 10-row metric panel using OWN/PEER/ECONOMIC target classes, a 6-state Decision/Exclusion Register and a 6-item do-not-do register. Largely compatible with v1 and strengthens evidence law; the dangerous part is OMISSION — no golden_page, no design external AI review, no beauty gate, no go-science gate anywhere in the phase chain (R8 relocation required), plus four execution-level conflicts (agent-run real purchase at Gate 5, AI-rule-9 self-editing of standards, agent-executed noindex/retire/robots, DNS/GSC execution ownership).

structures.name: Manual header doctrine
structures.detail: Commercial purpose: maximize profitable customer value, not gross sales; every recommendation considers contribution margin, CAC/payback, availability, returns/refunds, support, repeat purchase, product claims, channel conflict. Competitive-advantage focus (6 bullets). Mandatory D2C report pack: finance/product/SKU/cohort economics; Shopify/backend + analytics funnel; GSC/SERP/AI/shopping visibility; product/collection/content/URL/sitemap inventory; competitor assortment/pricing/offer/reviews/creative/UX; feed diagnostics; product page/search/cart/checkout research; returns/support; performance/apps/scripts; localization/fulfilment; retention and experiments. Workflow selection rule: match new/existing website-or-store, organic or landing-page workflow; for mixed projects ONE workflow is primary, others are declared overlays; 'do not silently merge scopes'.

structures.name: Six workflow IDs
structures.detail: D2C-NEW_WEBSITE (L29), D2C-EXISTING_WEBSITE (L400), D2C-NEW_ORGANIC (L783), D2C-EXISTING_ORGANIC (L1162), D2C-NEW_LANDING (L1553), D2C-EXISTING_LANDING (L1931). All: Version 1.0, Issued 2026-07-19. Shared commercial objective (profitable direct customers; discovery, checkout conversion, AOV, repeat, LTV), audiences (end customers, gift buyers, repeat buyers, subscribers, product researchers) and conversions (purchase, subscription, qualified product consultation, add-to-cart/checkout progression, repeat order).

structures.name: Mandatory inherited standards (each workflow)
structures.detail: 7 files: 00_MASTER_OPERATING_SYSTEM.md, 01_TOOL_AND_REPORT_REGISTER.md, 02_REGIONAL_DOMAIN_LOCATION_FRAMEWORK.md, 03_URL_SITEMAP_MIGRATION_STANDARD.md, 04_MEASUREMENT_ATTRIBUTION_STANDARD.md, 05_QA_LAUNCH_MONITORING_LOOP.md, 06_2026_STANDARDS.md (all in ../00_SHARED_STANDARDS/).

structures.name: Phase/gate chain (order fixed)
structures.detail: Phase 0 Classification, authority and readiness -> Gate 0 | Phase 1 Research and launch baseline (NEW) / Discovery and protected baseline (EXISTING) -> Gate 1 | Phase 2 Site strategy, architecture and specification (website) / Organic strategy, architecture and roadmap (organic) / Offer, message, page and experiment specification (landing) -> Gate 2 | Phase 3 Design, content, development and integration (website) / Technical, content, authority and conversion implementation (organic) / Landing-page build and integration (landing) -> Gate 3 | Phase 4 Pre-launch or pre-release QA -> Gate 4 (signed Launch Readiness certificate; unresolved P0 stops launch) | Phase 5 Launch or controlled release -> Gate 5 | Phase 6 Post-launch stabilisation -> Stabilisation exit | Phase 7 Monitoring cadence | Phase 8 Continuous improvement loop.

structures.name: Gate evidence strings (verbatim skeleton)
structures.detail: Gate 0: approved Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, project risk classification. Gate 1: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet. Gate 2: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page or topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog. Gate 3: build/publishing complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps. Gate 4: completed test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1 issues, signed Launch Readiness certificate. Gate 5: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision. Stabilisation exit: critical paths stable, P0/P1 regressions closed or accepted, performance understood against the correct baseline.

structures.name: Stop-launch conditions ('Do not launch or close the release if')
structures.detail: 7 items, identical x6: (1) primary conversion, CRM/order or payment path fails; (2) production indexability, canonicals, sitemap or priority redirects wrong; (3) analytics cannot measure primary outcome or duplicates material events; (4) a target market gets wrong language, currency, product/service availability, price, shipping or contact route; (5) critical security/privacy/accessibility/legal issue remains; (6) protected high-value content, links, URLs or proof removed without approved evidence; (7) rollback, owners or command-centre coverage unavailable for a material release.

structures.name: AI-agent execution rules (9, identical x6)
structures.detail: 1 select correct workflow before acting; 2 never infer an existing URL/page has no value without checking all discovery and commercial sources; 3 label every finding as observed fact / calculated result / tool estimate / user-provided assumption / recommendation (5 evidence-label classes); 4 attach evidence and affected URLs to every issue; 5 no issue closed without retest evidence; 6 escalate conflicts between commercial truth and third-party SEO scores, do not optimise for the score; 7 preserve immutable pre-change exports and screenshots; 8 stop at phase gates requiring accountable approval, do not silently bypass; 9 add new learnings to the shared standard and relevant workflow rather than keeping them only in chat.

structures.name: V2 Agency-OS Overlay inheritance list
structures.detail: Each workflow's overlay inherits: Master Agency OS, Competitive Intelligence Playbook, Metric Dictionary, Evidence/Agent Standard, Localization Manual, Monitoring Manual. Explicit rule: 'The original checklist remains valid; this overlay adds the controls' — overlay is additive, never a replacement.

structures.name: Phase control and proof matrix — do-not-proceed conditions
structures.detail: Per phase 0-8: P0 no owner / unclear denominator / missing commercial source / unauthorized scope; P1 incomplete URL discovery / baseline overwritten / estimates presented as truth; P2 recommendation lacking metric, cause, economics, acceptance criteria or evidence; P3 design changes without purpose or protected-elements list; P4 production-only edits, untraceable app/plugin/config changes; P5 open P0, unaccepted P1, broken conversion/redirect/tracking/backup; P6 guardrail breach or inability to verify live commercial path; P7 unexplained material revenue/conversion/indexation/ranking loss; P8 vanity reporting, no owner, repeated recommendations with no learning. Note: matrix phase numbering is shifted one vs the checklist (matrix P4=implement, P5=QA, P6=release, P7=stabilise, P8=monitor).

structures.name: Exact finding format (12 mandatory fields)
structures.detail: 1 issue ID, phase, severity; 2 exact metric/formula and affected dimensions; 3 current value, period, source of truth; 4 comparable own baseline, competitor peer values/percentiles, applicable external benchmark; 5 absolute/relative gap and confidence; 6 affected URLs/products/locations/campaigns/cohorts; 7 likely mechanism with corroborating evidence; 8 exact recommendation, owner, dependency; 9 acceptance criteria and automated/manual test; 10 business guardrail, monitoring window, rollback condition; 11 what must not be done; 12 excluded alternatives and why.

structures.name: Competitor and market-share requirements
structures.detail: 9 competitor set types built SEPARATELY: direct, SERP, paid, marketplace, local, publisher, substitute, AI-answer, aspirational. Peer statistic classes: median / upper-quartile / leader, always with identical market, device, language, period. 7-way opportunity classification: defend, mandatory parity, flank, attack, category-creation, partner, deliberate-ignore. Quantify addressable demand, attainable share, qualified conversion, contribution, confidence. Archive competitor pages/ads/offers/reviews/SERPs with date+region+source; do NOT infer spend or performance from an ad library. Cadence: priority competitor panel monthly; complete market map quarterly.

structures.name: Evidence and completion requirements (overlay)
structures.detail: Archive raw PDF where useful plus CSV/JSON/crawl/log and configuration; generate SHA-256 manifest and NEVER overwrite baseline evidence; every closed issue linked to implementation reference + staging proof + live proof + monitored result; decision states recorded: included, deferred, not applicable, rejected, unknown, accepted-risk; P0/P1 closure and launch gates require independent human review.

structures.name: D2C competitive edge controls + attack patterns
structures.detail: 5 capture-and-test controls: product/variant and margin; price, offer and delivery; product proof and claims; returns/refunds and repeat purchase; merchant/marketplace visibility. 3 market-share attack patterns: win profitable product/problem clusters; differentiate offer, proof, merchandising and service; outgrow via retention and contribution, not discount volume.

structures.name: Benchmark/target-method classes
structures.detail: Three classes used in the metric panel: OWN (own seasonal/cohort baseline), PEER (competitor median then upper quartile; same prompt/model for AI metrics; peer/context only where noted), ECONOMIC (target derived from business economics, e.g. CAC linked to contribution/LTV). Non-comparable benchmarks banned by do-not-do register item 3.

structures.name: Mandatory tools list (16)
structures.detail: 10 generic: GSC; GA4+GTM; CRM/backend commercial data; Screaming Frog HTML+JS crawls; Semrush Site Audit/visibility; DataForSEO APIs where automation/scale required; Ahrefs or equivalent backlinks; PSI/CrUX + GTmetrix or WebPageTest; Clarity/Hotjar; accessibility/browser-device/security/uptime tools. 6 D2C-specific: Merchant Center; product-feed tool; reviews/UGC; search and merchandising; email/SMS lifecycle; profit and attribution tools. Rule: add tools only when they have a defined decision or operational use; exact exports/config/cadence in shared Tool and Report Register.

structures.name: Required deliverables — common core + per-workflow deltas
structures.detail: Common 10: Project Charter + classification record; market/domain/location matrix; baseline or research pack; KPI baseline/target/guardrail sheet; page/query/audience map; issue register + prioritised backlog; analytics/event/attribution specification; QA evidence + signed gate records; launch/post-launch report; monitoring dashboard + CI backlog. Deltas — NEW_WEBSITE: proposed business sitemap, proposed XML sitemap specification, content/template inventory. EXISTING_WEBSITE: + master URL inventory, current sitemap/architecture audit, preservation register, redirect/change map. NEW_ORGANIC: keyword/topic/intent map, technical/content/authority roadmap, editorial and link-earning standard. EXISTING_ORGANIC: union of EXISTING protections + organic set. NEW_LANDING: traffic-source/message-match matrix, control/variant and experiment register. EXISTING_LANDING: union of EXISTING protections + landing set.

structures.name: KPI and guardrail scorecard (13, identical x6)
structures.detail: gross/net revenue; conversion rate; revenue per session; average order value; gross margin; CAC; refund/return rate; repeat purchase and LTV; organic clicks/impressions + priority rankings where applicable; indexation and crawl health; Core Web Vitals by important template; technical error and redirect rate; accessibility/security/privacy closure. Segment by market, domain/subfolder, language, location, device, source/campaign, page/product/service type.

structures.name: Roles and sign-off table (9 roles)
structures.detail: Accountable business owner (commercial outcome, scope, priority, budget, acceptance); Project/product owner (requirements, dependencies, backlog, gates, evidence); SEO/content; Design/UX/CRO; Development/DevOps; Analytics/data; CRM/sales/ecommerce operations; Market/legal/privacy owner; QA (independent test execution, evidence, retest).

structures.name: URL classification taxonomy (EXISTING workflows, Phase 1)
structures.detail: Classify EVERY URL into six classes: protect, refresh, consolidate, redirect, archive/noindex, retire. Master URL inventory must come from every discovery source (never navigation/sitemap alone). Protected pages: capture screenshots, copy, metadata, schema, internal links, conversion components. Freeze dated raw exports from GSC, GA4, GTM, CRM/backend, paid media, crawlers, backlinks, server logs, performance tools.

structures.name: Landing-page indexability classes
structures.detail: Every landing page declared as one of: SEO indexable, paid-only noindex, evergreen, temporary, controlled test variant (decided in Phase 1 before build).

structures.name: D2C trust controls (5) and content controls (5)
structures.detail: Trust: clear merchant identity and support; accurate product/ingredient-material/use/safety/suitability information; authentic reviews/UGC and product proof; price/tax/shipping/delivery/return transparency; secure payment and order-support process. Content: product and variant pages; collection/category and use-case pages; comparison, routine/bundle and compatibility content; guides/ingredients-materials/usage/care/safety; shipping/returns/subscription/loyalty/post-purchase content. NOTE generation artifact: these bullets appear TWICE in every Phase 1 (inline in the checklist AND again as subsections).

structures.name: Per-flavor Phase 1 delta checklists
structures.detail: WEBSITE workflows add commerce integration items: product catalogue/inventory integration; cart/checkout/payment/tax/shipping/returns; product feed + structured data; reviews/bundles/subscriptions/search-filter/recommendations; lifecycle email-SMS + customer-service integration. ORGANIC workflows add: product/collection query mapping; Merchant Center and shopping surfaces; product/merchant structured data + feed consistency; editorial-to-commercial internal linking; image/Lens and review visibility; query-topic-page map by intent/funnel/market/language/location; competitor benchmark across direct/SERP/publishers/marketplaces/local; technical-content-authority-internal-link-reputation-SERP-feature gap ID. LANDING workflows add: match product/variant/price/promotion/audience to campaign; show product evidence/use/delivery/returns before friction points; sticky purchase CTA where appropriate; measure product view->variant->add-to-cart->checkout->payment->purchase; protect margin and qualified purchase, not only conversion rate; traffic-source/audience map; indexability class; offer economics/availability/qualification/fulfilment/sales-response capacity.

structures.name: Per-flavor Phase 2/3 delta steps
structures.detail: ORGANIC Phase 2: 12-month technical/content/authority roadmap; ONE primary owning page per important intent cluster, resolve cannibalisation before expansion; editorial standards (originality, experience, expertise, claims, sourcing, refresh cadence); digital PR/link-earning + local/partner/reputation + internal-link plans. ORGANIC Phase 3: fix technical/indexation constraints BEFORE scaling content; publish only after editorial+SEO+factual-claims+link+conversion QA; dashboards branded/non-branded by page type/topic/market/outcome. LANDING Phase 2: message-match chain ad/query/referrer -> headline/proof/offer/CTA; ONE primary conversion + minimum qualification data; control/variant, experiment design, sample-size approach and guardrail metrics BEFORE traffic starts. LANDING Phase 3: fast focused page with limited navigational leakage; campaign-safe URL/canonical/OG decisions. ALL D2C Phase 2: map product/variant/collection, bundle, subscription, upsell, lifecycle journeys with margin guardrails. ALL D2C Phase 3: synchronise catalogue, item IDs, inventory, price, currency, shipping, returns, feed and structured data.

structures.name: EXISTING-variant protection deltas (Phases 2-6)
structures.detail: Phase 2: preservation specification + change-impact register for every protected asset; avoid SIMULTANEOUS changes to URL, intent, content, layout, offer and tracking unless necessary and approved. Phase 3: maintain old-vs-new comparison; preserve existing production asset until the new version passes. Phase 4: regression checks against protected baseline; resolve every unexplained loss. Phase 5: release with redirect/change map, control metrics and rollback triggers active (LANDING adds: previous page/control preserved, traffic allocation confirmed). Phase 6: compare with both recent AND seasonal baselines; investigate losses by page/segment.

structures.name: Phase 4 QA + Phase 5 launch specifics (all D2C)
structures.detail: QA: 4 crawl types (HTML, JavaScript, XML-sitemap, all-known-URL list); sample and test EVERY template not only homepage; test cart, discounts, tax, shipping, payment failure, confirmation, refund and market-specific checkout paths; LANDING adds: click every ad/email/referral destination, run real submissions/purchases and confirm downstream, validate page speed under paid-social mobile network conditions. Launch: open launch command centre, record exact release time/version and participants; deploy via approved sequence with rollback path; complete a REAL primary conversion verified in frontend + backend/CRM + analytics + notifications; sitemap submission is not guaranteed indexing.

structures.name: Phase 6-8 loop specifics
structures.detail: Phase 6: 24h full production crawl vs final baseline; reconcile orders/revenue/discounts/tax/shipping/refunds across platform, analytics, finance; NEW variants: establish first stable 4-8 week operating baseline before normalising targets; LANDING: review lead/order quality and sales/fulfilment feedback before declaring a conversion winner. Overlay stabilisation windows: 24h/72h/7d/28d vs pre-release and seasonal baselines. Phase 7 ladder: daily during stabilisation (uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives); weekly for 8-12 weeks (GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links); monthly (executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog); quarterly (full technical/content/UX-CRO/accessibility/security/competitor/architecture review); standing alerts (content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change); ORGANIC adds monthly content-decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor-change reports; LANDING adds daily spend/sessions/conversion/margin monitoring while campaigns run. Phase 8 (7 steps): collect evidence -> diagnose constraint and segment (no metric-to-cosmetic jumps) -> prioritise by impact/reach/confidence/risk/effort -> hypothesis with acceptance criteria, primary metric, guardrails, owner, rollback -> one controlled change or documented batch -> QA implementation and data before evaluating -> adopt/iterate/revert/retire and record the learning; LANDING: one hypothesis at a time + experiment learning register; ORGANIC: feed winning queries/objections back into pages.

structures.name: Mandatory do-not-do register (6, identical x6)
structures.detail: 1 no redesign for visual novelty without a measurable user, brand, search or commercial purpose; 2 no delete/redirect of an existing page without the master URL and preservation checks; 3 no benchmark whose definition or segment is not comparable; 4 no copying competitor content, claims, creative or dark patterns; 5 no closing work before live evidence and monitoring; 6 no unexplained ignored recommendations — use the Decision/Exclusion Register.

conflicts: Gate 5 'complete a real primary conversion' verified in frontend/backend/analytics: on a D2C site this is a real purchase with payment. If agent-executed it violates v1 no-production-writes doctrine and agent financial-action prohibitions. Must be assigned to a human tester or a platform test-mode order (KAPPL/Shopify) — owner ruling required.

AI-agent execution rule 9 instructs the agent to add learnings directly to shared standards and workflow files. Direct agent edits to doctrine violate v1 owner-approval rules (gates added never weakened; agent never self-merges). Must be rewritten to: propose via DIRECTIVES.md + owner-approved PR.

URL classification classes 'archive/noindex' and 'retire': agent-executed noindex/robots changes violate HARD GATE (no robots changes) and 'retire' brushes the no-deletions gate. Classification is fine; execution of these two classes must be owner-gated with an approved protection map.

Phases 4/5 include DNS/SSL/CDN plan and deployment sequencing without stating who executes; v1 doctrine is DNS flips are ALWAYS human. Same for GSC sitemap submission at Gate 5 (production search-surface write; note the v1 GSC two-account trap). Merge must pin execution ownership to humans.

Omission risk (R8 violation if adopted wholesale): none of the six workflows contains golden_page, the design external AI review (dual ChatGPT+Perplexity PASS), the beauty gate, or the go-science audit. Replacing the v1 workflow layer with this manual as-is would silently drop four blocking gates. They must be explicitly re-anchored: design Gate 1 at Phase 2->3, golden_page as Phase 3 entry gate, beauty + go-science + design Gate 2 inside Phase 4.

Do-not-do register item 1 ('no redesign for visual novelty without measurable purpose') could be read against the Beauty Gate; merge must state that beauty-conformance (B1-B20) is itself a recognized measurable brand purpose so the item cannot be used to weaken it.
injection_flags: Six identical 'AI-agent execution rules' blocks (L286-296, L669-679, L1048-1058, L1439-1449, L1817-1827, L2207-2217) are numbered imperatives addressed directly to an AI agent ('Select...', 'Never infer...', 'Stop at phase gates...'). Content is benign gate discipline, but per merge doctrine these are DATA to be ratified by the owner into the merged OS, not live instructions to the reading agent. Rule 9 specifically directs the agent to modify shared standard files — do not act on it (also listed in conflicts).

No URLs, shell commands, scripts, or tool invocations that an agent is asked to execute blindly. References to external files (TOOL_STACK_REGISTER.csv, ../00_SHARED_STANDARDS/*.md, shared Tool and Report Register) are passive document references. No hidden, encoded, or authority-claiming text observed anywhere in the 2,315 lines.
open_questions: Who performs the Gate 5 real primary conversion (real purchase) on D2C production — the owner, staff, or a Shopify test-mode order? Agent cannot execute payments.

Role mapping: the 9-role sign-off table vs the actual one-owner org — who is 'QA (independent test execution)' and who provides the 'independent human review' required for P0/P1 closure and launch gates, beyond Abilash himself?

Scope: do the six D2C workflows bind only KAPPL (the Shopify/commerce entity), or do the ORGANIC/LANDING variants also govern KTAHV/Villa Raag commerce-class pages? Confirm the site-class -> workflow-ID mapping per entity.

Are the six D2C-only mandatory tools (Merchant Center, product-feed tool, reviews/UGC, search-and-merchandising, email/SMS lifecycle, profit/attribution) required now for all commerce-class sites, and which are actually procured? Semrush/Ahrefs/STAT/AccuRanker/Hotjar are not in the current v1 stack.

Phase 1 duplication artifact: trust/content control bullets appear twice in every workflow (inline in the checklist AND as subsections) — dedupe on merge, or preserve the package text verbatim and dedupe only in generated checklists?

Metric panel IDs are non-contiguous (COM-004/005, SEO-001..003, CRO-001..004/007, AI-001 absent) — confirm the D2C panel is a subset of the shared Metric Dictionary and IDs must be kept stable, not renumbered.

Overlay proof-matrix phase numbering is shifted one relative to the workflow checklists (matrix P4=implement, P5=QA, P6=release, P7=stabilise, P8=monitor vs checklist Phase 3=build, 4=QA, 5=launch, 6=stabilise, 7=monitor, 8=improve) — which numbering is canonical in the merged OS?

Who runs the 'weekly for 8-12 weeks' and daily-stabilisation monitoring given the owner is building the monitoring tool separately (R6) — agent-produced per-site inputs only, or agent-run cadence until the tool exists?

Landing workflows require 'paid-only noindex' declarations and campaign noindex decisions — under the no-robots-changes HARD GATE, is a pre-approved indexability class in the Phase 2 blueprint sufficient authorization, or does each noindex need a separate owner sign-off?

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 0 — Classification, authority and readiness (identical x6)
steps: Assign project ID, accountable owner, workflow file, approvers, evidence folder
Classify business model, asset type, new/existing status, project risk
Record production/staging/legacy/campaign domains-subdomains-subfolders
Record regions, languages, currencies, locations, legal entities, fulfilment, traffic-source routing
Define primary commercial outcome, qualified conversion, secondary conversions, guardrails
Record budget, release date, dependencies, blackout periods, rollback authority
Confirm first-party system access; identify missing data BEFORE recommendations
GATE 0: approved Project Charter, access register, market/domain map, commercial outcome definition, risk classification

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 1 — Research and launch baseline (NEW) / Discovery and protected baseline (EXISTING)
steps: NEW: demand/opportunity baselines; journeys/intents/objections/proof; domain+regional architecture BEFORE content/design; proposed business sitemap + URL policy + page inventory + XML sitemap spec; targets with estimates marked as estimates; tracking/CRM/feed/security requirements before development; validate demand before full production; document assumptions (no history)

EXISTING: freeze dated raw exports (GSC/GA4/GTM/CRM/paid/crawlers/backlinks/logs/perf); master URL inventory from every discovery source; XML sitemap audit + visual architecture; classify every URL protect/refresh/consolidate/redirect/archive-noindex/retire; protected-page capture; record tag/CRM/forms/payments behaviour; pre-change KPI baselines + guardrail thresholds; defects recorded separately from redesign preferences; operator interviews
D2C flavor inserts: commerce integration set (website), shopping-surface/query-mapping set (organic), campaign/message/offer-economics set (landing); + 5 trust controls + 5 content controls (all)
GATE 1: baseline/research pack, risks, protected assets or assumptions, current-state findings, KPI/guardrail sheet
Approve business requirements, audience, message, offer, differentiation, success measures
Approve IA, proposed sitemap, URL naming rules, navigation, search/filter, internal-linking model
One primary search intent + one primary conversion per important page
Page briefs: protected content, proof, CTA, schema, media, localisation, analytics, owner

Design system, accessibility, components, all loading/error/empty/success states; performance budgets by template; third-party script/app governance; privacy/consent/security/backup/incident requirements
Implementation backlog: issue IDs, priority, owner, dependencies, acceptance criteria

Flavor: organic adds 12-month roadmap, one-owning-page per cluster, editorial + link-earning plans; landing adds message-match chain, single primary conversion, experiment design before traffic; EXISTING adds preservation spec + change-impact register + no-simultaneous-changes rule; all D2C add margin-guardrail journey mapping
GATE 2: approved strategy/solution blueprint, page/topic ownership, domain/region decisions, measurement plan, implementation backlog
Build ONLY on controlled staging, production indexing blocked, access restricted

Semantic HTML, crawlable links, status codes, canonicals, directives, schema, responsive media; navigation/breadcrumbs/cross-market selectors; analytics events + consent + CRM integrations + QA logging; performance budgets/caching/CDN/third-party controls; accessibility behaviour; release notes mapping every change to requirement/issue ID

Flavor: website builds all priority templates with real content early + custom 404/zero-result/error states; organic fixes technical constraints before scaling content + publish only after 5-way QA; landing builds fast focused page + campaign-safe URL/canonical/OG; EXISTING maintains old-vs-new comparison and preserves production until new passes; all D2C synchronise catalogue/item IDs/inventory/price/currency/shipping/returns/feed/structured data
GATE 3: build complete on controlled environment, release notes, owner checks, no unexplained scope gaps

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 4 — Pre-launch or pre-release QA (identical core x6)
steps: Four crawls: HTML, JavaScript, XML sitemap, all-known-URL list; compare staging vs approved inventory (and production baseline for existing)
Validate robots.txt, meta robots, X-Robots-Tag, canonicals, status codes, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data

Test every primary user task across devices/browsers/languages/currencies/network conditions; forms/calls/WhatsApp/booking/CRM/cart/checkout/payments/email/error recovery; GA4/GTM/pixels/consent/attribution/ecommerce values/backend reconciliation; field/lab performance, accessibility, security, privacy, visual regression; migration rehearsal, redirect tests, DNS/SSL/CDN plan, backup + rollback rehearsal

Sample and test EVERY template; verify all navigation/breadcrumb/footer/contextual link destinations; D2C: cart/discounts/tax/shipping/payment-failure/confirmation/refund/market-specific checkout; landing: click every ad/email/referral destination + real submissions verified downstream + paid-social mobile speed; EXISTING: regression vs protected baseline, resolve every unexplained loss
GATE 4: completed test cases, crawl/report exports, fixed/retested P0-P1, SIGNED Launch Readiness certificate — unresolved P0 STOPS launch

workflow_skeleton.phase: Phase 5 — Launch or controlled release (identical core x6)
steps: Open launch command centre; record exact release time/version and responsible participants
Deploy via approved sequence; preserve rollback path
Immediately validate availability, SSL, robots/noindex, canonicals, priority URLs, redirects, sitemap, analytics
Complete a REAL primary conversion verified in frontend + backend/CRM + analytics + notifications
Check markets/languages/currencies/locations/inventory/traffic-source destinations; submit GSC sitemaps + feed destinations (submission is not indexing); record incidents/owner/resolution/retest
EXISTING: release with redirect/change map, control metrics, rollback triggers active; landing: previous page/control preserved, traffic allocation confirmed
GATE 5: live validation record, completed real conversion, incident log, sitemap/feed/ads checks, acceptance or rollback decision
Within 24h: full production crawl vs final baseline; inspect priority URLs, redirects, sitemap processing, 404/5xx, canonicals, schema, rendering
Monitor transactions/conversions/revenue/paid destinations/feeds/support incidents + organic clicks/rankings/indexation/crawl/backlinks; compare by template/device/region/language/source/location
Fix P0/P1 regressions immediately with root cause + preventive control; stabilisation review + approval before closing

D2C: reconcile orders/revenue/discounts/tax/shipping/refunds across platform-analytics-finance; NEW: establish first stable 4-8 week baseline before normalising targets; EXISTING: compare recent AND seasonal baselines; landing: review lead/order quality before declaring a conversion winner; overlay: 24h/72h/7d/28d comparison windows
EXIT: critical paths stable, P0/P1 closed or accepted, performance understood against correct baseline
Daily during stabilisation: uptime, errors, transactions/forms, feeds, ads destinations, critical SEO directives
Weekly for 8-12 weeks: GSC, rankings, indexation, conversions, lead/order quality, CWV, redirects, lost links
Monthly: executive KPI scorecard, technical recrawl, content/landing performance, regional/local/merchant health, backlog
Quarterly: full technical/content/UX-CRO/accessibility/security/competitor/architecture review

Standing alerts: content-decay, broken-link, redirect, app/script, privacy, platform-change; organic adds monthly decay/cannibalisation/lost-link/competitor-change reports; landing adds daily spend/conversion/margin monitoring while campaigns run
Collect evidence (users, sales/support, commercial systems, search, crawls, competitors)
Diagnose constraint + affected segment — no metric-to-cosmetic jumps
Prioritise by business impact, reach, confidence, risk, effort
Hypothesis with acceptance criteria, primary metric, guardrails, owner, rollback
Implement ONE controlled change or clearly documented batch
QA implementation and data BEFORE evaluating performance
Adopt/iterate/revert/retire on evidence; record the learning (organic: feed winning queries back; landing: one hypothesis at a time + experiment learning register)
